title: 李爾王
author: William Shakespeare 威廉·莎士比亞
description: 《King Lear》(約1606)。年老嘅李爾王按女兒嘅甜言蜜語分割王國,放逐誠實嘅幼女考黛莉亞,隨即被兩個大女兒背棄,在荒野風暴中失去理智。同時葛羅斯特伯爵一家亦因庶子嘅陰謀而分崩離析。全劇五幕二十六場,每段對白標示說話者,英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Act I, Scene I — A Room of State in King Lear’s Palace 第一幕第一場:李爾王宮殿朝堂

passages.original: Enter Kent, Gloucester and Edmund.
passages.vernacular: [肯特、葛羅斯特同愛德蒙上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特、葛羅斯特和愛德蒙上。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I thought the King had more affected the Duke of Albany than Cornwall.
passages.vernacular: 我原以為國王更偏愛奧本尼公爵而唔係康華爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我原以為國王更偏愛奧本尼公爵而不是康華爾。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: It did always seem so to us; but now, in the division of the kingdom, it appears not which of the Dukes he values most, for qualities are so weighed that curiosity in neither can make choice of either’s moiety.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一向都咁樣覺得;但而家分割王國時,睇不出佢更睇重邊位公爵,因為兩者份量衡量得如此相當,再挑剔都無法選出邊一份更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一向也這樣覺得;但現在分割王國時,看不出他更看重哪位公爵,因為兩者份量衡量得如此相當,再挑剔也無法選出哪一份更好。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Is not this your son, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人,呢唔係您嘅兒子嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,這不是您的兒子嗎?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: His breeding, sir, hath been at my charge: I have so often blush’d to acknowledge him that now I am braz’d to’t.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅養育由我負擔,先生:我多次為承認佢而臉紅,而家已經臉皮厚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的養育由我負擔,先生:我多次為承認他而臉紅,現在已經臉皮厚了。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I cannot conceive you.
passages.vernacular: 我不明白您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不明白您。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Sir, this young fellow’s mother could; whereupon she grew round-wombed, and had indeed, sir, a son for her cradle ere she had a husband for her bed.
passages.vernacular: 先生,呢年輕人嘅母親明白;於是佢肚子圓咗起嚟,確實,先生,喺佢床上有丈夫之前,搖籃裡先有咗兒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,這年輕人的母親明白;於是她肚子圓了起來,確實,先生,在她床上有丈夫之前,搖籃裡先有了兒子。

passages.original: Do you smell a fault?
passages.vernacular: 您聞到過錯咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您聞到過錯了嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I cannot wish the fault undone, the issue of it being so proper.
passages.vernacular: 我不希望嗰過錯被抹去,因為佢嘅結果如此標致。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不希望那過錯被抹去,因為它的結果如此標致。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: But I have a son, sir, by order of law, some year elder than this, who yet is no dearer in my account:
passages.vernacular: 不過我仲有一個兒子,先生,按法律所生,比呢個大約一歲,卻並不比佢更親:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我還有一個兒子,先生,按法律所生,比這個大約一歲,卻並不比他更親:

passages.original: though this knave came something saucily to the world before he was sent for, yet was his mother fair;
passages.vernacular: 雖然呢小子不請自嚟,有點放肆地嚟到世上,但佢母親好美;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然這小子不請自來,有點放肆地來到世上,但他母親很美;

passages.original: there was good sport at his making, and the whoreson must be acknowledged.
passages.vernacular: 製造佢時好有樂趣,呢個雜種必須被承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 製造他時很有樂趣,這個雜種必須被承認。

passages.original: Do you know this noble gentleman, Edmund?
passages.vernacular: 你認識呢位高貴嘅紳士嗎,愛德蒙?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認識這位高貴的紳士嗎,愛德蒙?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: No, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 不認識,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不認識,大人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: My Lord of Kent: remember him hereafter as my honourable friend.
passages.vernacular: 肯特大人:以後要記得佢係我尊敬嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 肯特大人:以後要記得他是我尊敬的朋友。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: My services to your lordship.
passages.vernacular: 為大人效勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為大人效勞。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I must love you, and sue to know you better.
passages.vernacular: 我必須愛你,並請求更了解你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須愛你,並請求更了解你。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Sir, I shall study deserving.
passages.vernacular: 先生,我將努力配得上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我將努力配得上。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: He hath been out nine years, and away he shall again.
passages.vernacular: 佢出去咗九年,仲要再出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他出去了九年,還要再出去。

passages.original: The King is coming.
passages.vernacular: 國王嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王來了。

passages.original: [Sennet within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。]

passages.original: Enter Lear, Cornwall, Albany, Goneril, Regan, Cordelia and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [李爾、康華爾、奧本尼、高納麗、里根、考黛莉亞同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾、康華爾、奧本尼、高納麗、里根、考黛莉亞和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Attend the lords of France and Burgundy, Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: 葛羅斯特,去侍候法蘭西同勃艮第兩位大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛羅斯特,去侍候法蘭西和勃艮第兩位大人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I shall, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我去,陛下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去,陛下。

passages.original: [Exeunt Gloucester and Edmund.]
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特同愛德蒙下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特和愛德蒙下。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Meantime we shall express our darker purpose.
passages.vernacular: 同時我哋將宣布我哋更隱祕嘅意圖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時我們將宣布我們更隱祕的意圖。

passages.original: Give me the map there.
passages.vernacular: 把地圖畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把地圖給我。

passages.original: Know that we have divided In three our kingdom:
passages.vernacular: 要知道我哋已把王國分成三份:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要知道我們已把王國分成三份:

passages.original: and ’tis our fast intent To shake all cares and business from our age;
passages.vernacular: 我哋堅定嘅意圖係從我哋嘅年老中抖落一切憂慮同事務;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們堅定的意圖是從我們的年老中抖落一切憂慮和事務;

passages.original: Conferring them on younger strengths, while we Unburden’d crawl toward death.
passages.vernacular: 把佢哋交畀更年輕有力嘅人,而我哋無牽無掛地爬向死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把它們交給更年輕有力的人,而我們無牽無掛地爬向死亡。

passages.original: Our son of Cornwall, And you, our no less loving son of Albany, We have this hour a constant will to publish Our daughters’ several dowers, that future strife May be prevented now.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅康華爾兒子,仲有你,我哋同樣親愛嘅奧本尼兒子,我哋此刻有堅定嘅意志,公布我哋女兒哋各自嘅嫁妝,以免將來嘅紛爭而家就被預防。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的康華爾兒子,還有你,我們同樣親愛的奧本尼兒子,我們此刻有堅定的意志,公布我們女兒們各自的嫁妝,以免將來的紛爭現在就被預防。

passages.original: The princes, France and Burgundy, Great rivals in our youngest daughter’s love, Long in our court have made their amorous sojourn, And here are to be answer’d.
passages.vernacular: 兩位王子,法蘭西同勃艮第,係我哋幼女愛情嘅大對手,已喺我哋宮廷久居求愛,而家要得到答覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩位王子,法蘭西和勃艮第,是我們幼女愛情的大對手,已在我們宮廷久居求愛,現在要得到答覆。

passages.original: Tell me, my daughters,— Since now we will divest us both of rule, Interest of territory, cares of state,— Which of you shall we say doth love us most?
passages.vernacular: 告訴我,我嘅女兒哋——既然我哋而家要同時卸下統治權、領土利益同國家事務——我哋該講你哋邊一個最愛我哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我,我的女兒們——既然我們現在要同時卸下統治權、領土利益和國家事務——我們該說你們哪一個最愛我們?

passages.original: That we our largest bounty may extend Where nature doth with merit challenge.—Goneril, Our eldest born, speak first.
passages.vernacular: 好讓我哋把最大嘅恩賜畀予天性同功德都有所主張嘅人。——高納麗,我哋嘅長女,先講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好讓我們把最大的恩賜給予天性與功德都有所主張的人。——高納麗,我們的長女,先說。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Sir, I love you more than word can wield the matter;
passages.vernacular: 父親,我愛您,超過言語所能承載嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 父親,我愛您,超過言語所能承載的;

passages.original: Dearer than eyesight, space, and liberty; Beyond what can be valu’d, rich or rare;
passages.vernacular: 比眼睛、空間同自由更珍貴;超出任何可估價嘅,富有嘅或稀罕嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比眼睛、空間和自由更珍貴;超出任何可估價的,富有的或稀罕的;

passages.original: No less than life, with grace, health, beauty, honour;
passages.vernacular: 不亞於生命,連同優雅、健康、美貌、榮譽;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不亞於生命,連同優雅、健康、美貌、榮譽;

passages.original: As much as child e’er lov’d, or father found;
passages.vernacular: 像細路所曾愛、父親所曾感到嘅咁多;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像孩子所曾愛、父親所曾感到的那麼多;

passages.original: A love that makes breath poor and speech unable;
passages.vernacular: 一種使氣息貧乏、使言語無力嘅愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種使氣息貧乏、使言語無力的愛;

passages.original: Beyond all manner of so much I love you.
passages.vernacular: 超出一切呢類嘅量度,我愛您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 超出一切這類的量度,我愛您。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: What shall Cordelia speak?
passages.vernacular: 考黛莉亞要講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 考黛莉亞要說什麼?

passages.original: Love, and be silent.
passages.vernacular: 愛,並且沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛,並且沉默。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Of all these bounds, even from this line to this, With shadowy forests and with champains rich’d, With plenteous rivers and wide-skirted meads, We make thee lady:
passages.vernacular: 從呢條線到呢條線之間嘅所有疆域,有幽暗嘅森林同肥沃嘅平原,豐沛嘅河流同廣闊嘅草地,我哋都封你為女主人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從這條線到這條線之間的所有疆域,有幽暗的森林和肥沃的平原,豐沛的河流和廣闊的草地,我們都封你為女主人:

passages.original: to thine and Albany’s issue Be this perpetual.—What says our second daughter, Our dearest Regan, wife of Cornwall? Speak.
passages.vernacular: 呢永遠歸你同奧本尼嘅後代。——我哋嘅次女,最親愛嘅里根,康華爾嘅妻子,你講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這永遠歸你和奧本尼的後代。——我們的次女,最親愛的里根,康華爾的妻子,你說什麼?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Sir, I am made of the self mettle as my sister, And prize me at her worth.
passages.vernacular: 父親,我係用同一種金屬造嘅,同我姊姊一樣,請按佢嘅價值估價我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 父親,我是用同一種金屬造的,和我姊姊一樣,請按她的價值估價我。

passages.original: In my true heart I find she names my very deed of love;
passages.vernacular: 喺我真心中我發覺佢講出咗我愛嘅實際行為;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我真心中我發覺她說出了我愛的實際行為;

passages.original: Only she comes too short, that I profess Myself an enemy to all other joys Which the most precious square of sense possesses, And find I am alone felicitate In your dear highness’ love.
passages.vernacular: 只係佢講得太少,因為我宣稱自己係一切其他歡樂嘅敵人,包括最珍貴感官所擁有嘅歡樂,我發現我唯有喺陛下嘅愛中才係幸福嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是她說得太少,因為我宣稱自己是一切其他歡樂的敵人,包括最珍貴感官所擁有的歡樂,我發現我唯有在陛下的愛中才是幸福的。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: Then poor Cordelia, And yet not so; since, I am sure, my love’s More ponderous than my tongue.
passages.vernacular: 咁可憐嘅考黛莉亞!然而並非如此;因為我確信我嘅愛比我嘅舌頭更重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼可憐的考黛莉亞!然而並非如此;因為我確信我的愛比我的舌頭更重。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: To thee and thine hereditary ever Remain this ample third of our fair kingdom;
passages.vernacular: 呢遼闊嘅三分之一美好王國,永遠世襲歸你同你嘅後代;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這遼闊的三分之一美好王國,永遠世襲歸你和你的後代;

passages.original: No less in space, validity, and pleasure Than that conferr’d on Goneril.—Now, our joy, Although the last and least;
passages.vernacular: 喺面積、價值同樂趣上都不亞於畀高納麗嘅。——而家,我哋嘅喜悅,雖然係最後都係最小嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在面積、價值和樂趣上都不亞於給高納麗的。——現在,我們的喜悅,雖然是最後也是最小的;

passages.original: to whose young love The vines of France and milk of Burgundy Strive to be interess’d;
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西嘅葡萄藤同勃艮第嘅牛奶都爭住同佢年輕嘅愛情有份;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西的葡萄藤和勃艮第的牛奶都爭著與她年輕的愛情有份;

passages.original: what can you say to draw A third more opulent than your sisters? Speak.
passages.vernacular: 你能講乜嘢嚟換取比你姊姊哋更豐厚嘅三分之一?講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能說什麼來換取比你姊姊們更豐厚的三分之一?說。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Nothing, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 冇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Nothing?
passages.vernacular: 冇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有?

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Nothing.
passages.vernacular: 冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Nothing will come of nothing: speak again.
passages.vernacular: 無中唔能夠生有:再講一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無中不能生有:再說一次。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Unhappy that I am, I cannot heave My heart into my mouth:
passages.vernacular: 我真不幸,我唔能夠把心提到嘴裡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真不幸,我不能把心提到嘴裡:

passages.original: I love your majesty According to my bond; no more nor less.
passages.vernacular: 我愛陛下,按我嘅本分;不多都不少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛陛下,按我的本分;不多也不少。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How, how, Cordelia?
passages.vernacular: 點,點,考黛莉亞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,怎麼,考黛莉亞?

passages.original: Mend your speech a little, Lest you may mar your fortunes.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅話改一改,免得毀咗你嘅前程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的話改一改,免得毀了你的前程。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Good my lord, You have begot me, bred me, lov’d me:
passages.vernacular: 好大人,您生咗我、養咗我、愛我:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,您生了我、養了我、愛我:

passages.original: I Return those duties back as are right fit, Obey you, love you, and most honour you.
passages.vernacular: 我把呢啲恩情報答,正如應當,服從您、愛您、最尊敬您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把這些恩情報答,正如應當,服從您、愛您、最尊敬您。

passages.original: Why have my sisters husbands if they say They love you all?
passages.vernacular: 如果我姊姊哋講佢哋全心愛您,佢哋點解有丈夫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我姊姊們說她們全心愛您,她們為什麼有丈夫?

passages.original: Haply, when I shall wed, That lord whose hand must take my plight shall carry Half my love with him, half my care and duty:
passages.vernacular: 或者,當我結婚時,嗰將接受我誓言嘅丈夫,會帶走我一半嘅愛、一半嘅關懷同責任:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許,當我結婚時,那將接受我誓言的丈夫,會帶走我一半的愛、一半的關懷和責任:

passages.original: Sure I shall never marry like my sisters, To love my father all.
passages.vernacular: 我肯定我永遠唔會像我姊姊哋嗰樣出嫁,只愛父親一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定我永遠不會像我姊姊們那樣出嫁,只愛父親一個人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: But goes thy heart with this?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅心真係咁樣想嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的心真是這樣想的嗎?

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Ay, my good lord.
passages.vernacular: 係,我嘅好大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,我的好大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: So young, and so untender?
passages.vernacular: 咁年輕,卻咁不溫柔?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼年輕,卻這麼不溫柔?

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: So young, my lord, and true.
passages.vernacular: 咁年輕,大人,卻真誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼年輕,大人,卻真誠。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Let it be so, thy truth then be thy dower: For, by the sacred radiance of the sun, The mysteries of Hecate and the night;
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣吧,你嘅真誠就係你嘅嫁妝:因為,憑太陽神聖嘅光輝、赫卡忒嘅神祕同夜晚;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣吧,你的真誠就是你的嫁妝:因為,憑太陽神聖的光輝、赫卡忒的神祕和夜晚;

passages.original: By all the operation of the orbs, From whom we do exist and cease to be;
passages.vernacular: 憑諸天體嘅一切運作,我哋靠佢哋存在又消逝;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑諸天體的一切運作,我們靠它們存在又消逝;

passages.original: Here I disclaim all my paternal care, Propinquity and property of blood, And as a stranger to my heart and me Hold thee from this for ever.
passages.vernacular: 我喺此宣布放棄我所有嘅父愛、血緣嘅親近同所有權,從此把你當作陌生人,永遠不屬於我嘅心同我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在此宣布放棄我所有的父愛、血緣的親近與所有權,從此把你當作陌生人,永遠不屬於我的心和我。

passages.original: The barbarous Scythian, Or he that makes his generation messes To gorge his appetite, shall to my bosom Be as well neighbour’d, pitied, and reliev’d, As thou my sometime daughter.
passages.vernacular: 野蠻嘅斯基泰人,或者嗰為了滿足食慾而把自己嘅後代煮嚟食嘅人,喺我胸中都將得到同樣嘅鄰近、憐憫同救助,就像你,我曾經嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野蠻的斯基泰人,或者那為了滿足食慾而把自己的後代煮來吃的人,在我胸中也將得到同樣的鄰近、憐憫和救助,就像你,我曾經的女兒。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Good my liege,—
passages.vernacular: 好陛下——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好陛下——

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Peace, Kent!
passages.vernacular: 安靜,肯特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,肯特!

passages.original: Come not between the dragon and his wrath.
passages.vernacular: 唔好擋喺龍同佢嘅憤怒之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要擋在龍和它的憤怒之間。

passages.original: I lov’d her most, and thought to set my rest On her kind nursery.
passages.vernacular: 我最愛佢,原想靠佢善良嘅照料安度晚年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最愛她,原想靠她善良的照料安度晚年。

passages.original: [To Cordelia.]
passages.vernacular: [對考黛莉亞。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對考黛莉亞。]

passages.original: Hence and avoid my sight!
passages.vernacular: 走開,唔好畀我睇見你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,別讓我看見你!

passages.original: So be my grave my peace, as here I give Her father’s heart from her!
passages.vernacular: 願我嘅墳墓成為我嘅安寧,正如我而家從佢嗰度收回做父親嘅心!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願我的墳墓成為我的安寧,正如我現在從她那裡收回做父親的心!

passages.original: Call France. Who stirs?
passages.vernacular: 叫法蘭西嚟。邊個動喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫法蘭西來。誰動了?

passages.original: Call Burgundy!
passages.vernacular: 叫勃艮第嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫勃艮第來!

passages.original: Cornwall and Albany, With my two daughters’ dowers digest this third:
passages.vernacular: 康華爾同奧本尼,把呢三分之一同我兩個女兒嘅嫁妝合喺一起消化吧:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 康華爾和奧本尼,把這三分之一和我兩個女兒的嫁妝合在一起消化吧:

passages.original: Let pride, which she calls plainness, marry her.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢稱為直率嘅驕傲去嫁畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓她稱為直率的驕傲去嫁給她。

passages.original: I do invest you jointly with my power, Pre-eminence, and all the large effects That troop with majesty.
passages.vernacular: 我把我嘅權力、尊榮同一切伴隨王權嘅重大權益一併授予你哋兩人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把我的權力、尊榮和一切伴隨王權的重大權益一併授予你們兩人。

passages.original: Ourself, by monthly course, With reservation of an hundred knights, By you to be sustain’d, shall our abode Make with you by due turn.
passages.vernacular: 我自己將按月輪流,保留一百名騎士由你哋供養,輪流住到你哋嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己將按月輪流,保留一百名騎士由你們供養,輪流住到你們那裡。

passages.original: Only we shall retain The name, and all the addition to a king;
passages.vernacular: 我哋只保留國王嘅名號同一切銜頭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們只保留國王的名號和一切銜頭;

passages.original: the sway, Revenue, execution of the rest, Beloved sons, be yours;
passages.vernacular: 統治權、收入同其餘嘅執行,親愛嘅兒子哋,歸你哋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 統治權、收入和其餘的執行,親愛的兒子們,歸你們;

passages.original: which to confirm, This coronet part between you.
passages.vernacular: 為證實呢點,呢頂王冠由你哋分開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為證實這點,這頂王冠由你們分開。

passages.original: [Giving the crown.]
passages.vernacular: [交出王冠。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [交出王冠。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Royal Lear, Whom I have ever honour’d as my king, Lov’d as my father, as my master follow’d, As my great patron thought on in my prayers.—
passages.vernacular: 尊貴嘅李爾,我一向尊敬您為國王,愛您如父親,追隨您如主人,喺祈禱中想到您如我嘅大恩主——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尊貴的李爾,我一向尊敬您為國王,愛您如父親,追隨您如主人,在祈禱中想到您如我的大恩主——

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: The bow is bent and drawn; make from the shaft.
passages.vernacular: 弓已拉開,箭喺弦上;避開箭頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弓已拉開,箭在弦上;避開箭頭。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Let it fall rather, though the fork invade The region of my heart:
passages.vernacular: 讓佢落下吧,即使箭叉刺入我嘅心臟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓它落下吧,即使箭叉刺入我的心臟:

passages.original: be Kent unmannerly When Lear is mad.
passages.vernacular: 當李爾發瘋時,就讓肯特無禮吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當李爾發瘋時,就讓肯特無禮吧。

passages.original: What wouldst thou do, old man?
passages.vernacular: 你想做乜嘢,老頭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想做什麼,老頭?

passages.original: Think’st thou that duty shall have dread to speak, When power to flattery bows?
passages.vernacular: 你以為當權力向諂媚屈服時,忠誠會怕開口嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為當權力向諂媚屈服時,忠誠會怕開口嗎?

passages.original: To plainness honour’s bound When majesty falls to folly.
passages.vernacular: 當君王墮入愚蠢時,榮譽就被迫要直率。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當君王墮入愚蠢時,榮譽就被迫要直率。

passages.original: Reverse thy state; And in thy best consideration check This hideous rashness:
passages.vernacular: 收回你嘅決定;喺你最好嘅考慮中,制止呢可怕嘅輕率:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收回你的決定;在你最好的考慮中,制止這可怕的輕率:

passages.original: answer my life my judgement, Thy youngest daughter does not love thee least;
passages.vernacular: 我用生命擔保我嘅判斷,你嘅幼女並非最不愛你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用生命擔保我的判斷,你的幼女並非最不愛你;

passages.original: Nor are those empty-hearted, whose low sounds Reverb no hollowness.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲低聲講話卻冇空洞回響嘅人,都並非空心嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些低聲說話卻沒有空洞回響的人,也並非空心的。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Kent, on thy life, no more.
passages.vernacular: 肯特,以你嘅性命,唔好再講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 肯特,以你的性命,別再說了。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: My life I never held but as a pawn To wage against thine enemies;
passages.vernacular: 我從未把我嘅性命睇成別嘅,只係用嚟對抗你敵人嘅賭注;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未把我的性命看成別的,只是用來對抗你敵人的賭注;

passages.original: ne’er fear to lose it, Thy safety being the motive.
passages.vernacular: 從不怕失去佢,只要你嘅安全係動機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從不怕失去它,只要你的安全是動機。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Out of my sight!
passages.vernacular: 滾出我嘅視線!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾出我的視線!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: See better, Lear; and let me still remain The true blank of thine eye.
passages.vernacular: 睇得清楚些,李爾;讓我永遠做你眼睛嘅真正靶心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看得清楚些,李爾;讓我永遠做你眼睛的真正靶心。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Now, by Apollo,—
passages.vernacular: 而家,憑阿波羅——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,憑阿波羅——

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Now by Apollo, King, Thou swear’st thy gods in vain.
passages.vernacular: 而家憑阿波羅,國王,你係妄起你嘅神誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在憑阿波羅,國王,你是妄起你的神誓。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O vassal! Miscreant!
passages.vernacular: 啊,奴才!逆賊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,奴才!逆賊!

passages.original: [Laying his hand on his sword.]
passages.vernacular: [手按劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [手按劍。]

passages.title: Albany And Cornwall 奧本尼同康華爾
passages.original: Dear sir, forbear!
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅陛下,請忍耐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的陛下,請忍耐!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Kill thy physician, and the fee bestow Upon the foul disease.
passages.vernacular: 你殺你嘅醫生,把診金畀嗰骯髒嘅病吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你殺你的醫生,把診金給那骯髒的病吧。

passages.original: Revoke thy gift, Or, whilst I can vent clamour from my throat, I’ll tell thee thou dost evil.
passages.vernacular: 收回你嘅賞賜,否則只要我喉嚨能發出喊聲,我就要告訴你你喺作惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收回你的賞賜,否則只要我喉嚨能發出喊聲,我就要告訴你你在作惡。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Hear me, recreant!
passages.vernacular: 聽我講,叛徒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽我說,叛徒!

passages.original: on thine allegiance, hear me!
passages.vernacular: 憑你嘅效忠,聽我講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑你的效忠,聽我說!

passages.original: Since thou hast sought to make us break our vows, Which we durst never yet, and with strain’d pride To come betwixt our sentences and our power, Which nor our nature, nor our place can bear, Our potency made good, take thy reward.
passages.vernacular: 既然你想使我哋違背誓言,我哋從唔敢如此,又以緊繃嘅驕傲插喺我哋嘅判決同權力之間,呢個係我哋嘅本性同地位都無法容忍嘅,為了證明我哋嘅權威,接受你嘅報酬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然你想使我們違背誓言,我們從不敢如此,又以緊繃的驕傲插在我們的判決與權力之間,這是我們的本性和地位都無法容忍的,為了證明我們的權威,接受你的報酬。

passages.original: Five days we do allot thee for provision, To shield thee from disasters of the world;
passages.vernacular: 我哋畀你五天準備,以防世界嘅災難;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們給你五天準備,以防世界的災難;

passages.original: And on the sixth to turn thy hated back Upon our kingdom:
passages.vernacular: 第六天轉過你可憎嘅背離開我哋嘅王國:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第六天轉過你可憎的背離開我們的王國:

passages.original: if, on the next day following, Thy banish’d trunk be found in our dominions, The moment is thy death. Away!
passages.vernacular: 如果次日喺我哋嘅領土裡發現你被放逐嘅身軀,嗰一刻就係你嘅死期。滾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果次日在我們的領土裡發現你被放逐的身軀,那一刻就是你的死期。滾!

passages.original: By Jupiter, This shall not be revok’d.
passages.vernacular: 憑朱庇特,呢個決定唔會收回。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑朱庇特,這個決定不會收回。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Fare thee well, King: sith thus thou wilt appear, Freedom lives hence, and banishment is here.
passages.vernacular: 再見,國王:既然你咁樣表現,自由活喺別處,放逐就喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,國王:既然你這樣表現,自由活在別處,放逐就在這裡。

passages.original: [To Cordelia.]
passages.vernacular: [對考黛莉亞。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對考黛莉亞。]

passages.original: The gods to their dear shelter take thee, maid, That justly think’st and hast most rightly said!
passages.vernacular: 願諸神把你收喺佢哋親愛嘅庇護之下,少女,你想得正確,講得最恰當!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願諸神把你收在他們親愛的庇護之下,少女,你想得正確,說得最恰當!

passages.original: [To Goneril and Regan.]
passages.vernacular: [對高納麗同里根。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對高納麗和里根。]

passages.original: And your large speeches may your deeds approve, That good effects may spring from words of love.
passages.vernacular: 願你哋嘅大話能以行動證明,使好結果從愛嘅言辭中生出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願你們的大話能以行動證明,使好結果從愛的言辭中生出。

passages.original: Thus Kent, O princes, bids you all adieu; He’ll shape his old course in a country new.
passages.vernacular: 王子哋,肯特就咁樣向你哋告別;佢將喺新嘅國度裡重走佢嘅老路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王子們,肯特就這樣向你們告別;他將在新的國度裡重走他的老路。

passages.original: [Exit.]
Flourish. Re-enter Gloucester, with France, Burgundy and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [號角齊鳴。葛羅斯特同法蘭西、勃艮第及侍從哋再上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [號角齊鳴。葛羅斯特與法蘭西、勃艮第及侍從們再上。]

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Here’s France and Burgundy, my noble lord.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係法蘭西同勃艮第,我高貴嘅大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是法蘭西和勃艮第,我高貴的大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: My Lord of Burgundy, We first address toward you, who with this king Hath rivall’d for our daughter:
passages.vernacular: 勃艮第大人,我哋先對你講話,你同呢位國王為我哋嘅女兒爭奪過:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勃艮第大人,我們先對你說話,你和這位國王為我們的女兒爭奪過:

passages.original: what in the least Will you require in present dower with her, Or cease your quest of love?
passages.vernacular: 你而家要求佢至少有多少嫁妝,否則就停止你嘅求愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在要求她至少有多少嫁妝,否則就停止你的求愛?

passages.title: Burgundy 勃艮第
passages.original: Most royal majesty, I crave no more than hath your highness offer’d, Nor will you tender less.
passages.vernacular: 最尊貴嘅陛下,我只要求陛下已提出嘅,您都唔會畀得更少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最尊貴的陛下,我只要求陛下已提出的,您也不會給得更少。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Right noble Burgundy, When she was dear to us, we did hold her so;
passages.vernacular: 最高貴嘅勃艮第,當佢對我哋珍貴時,我哋就咁睇重佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最高貴的勃艮第,當她對我們珍貴時,我們就那麼看重她;

passages.original: But now her price is fall’n.
passages.vernacular: 但而家佢嘅價碼跌喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在她的價碼跌了。

passages.original: Sir, there she stands: If aught within that little-seeming substance, Or all of it, with our displeasure piec’d, And nothing more, may fitly like your grace, She’s there, and she is yours.
passages.vernacular: 先生,佢就站喺嗰度:如果喺嗰睇似微小嘅實質裡有任何部分,或全部,再加上我哋嘅不悅,別無其他,能合您嘅意,佢就喺嗰度,佢就係您嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,她就站在那裡:如果在那看似微小的實質裡有任何部分,或全部,再加上我們的不悅,別無其他,能合您的意,她就在那裡,她就是您的。

passages.title: Burgundy 勃艮第
passages.original: I know no answer.
passages.vernacular: 我無言以對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無言以對。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Will you, with those infirmities she owes, Unfriended, new adopted to our hate, Dower’d with our curse, and stranger’d with our oath, Take her or leave her?
passages.vernacular: 你願意帶住佢所有嘅缺陷,冇朋友,剛被收養進我哋嘅恨,以我哋嘅詛咒為嫁妝,被我哋嘅誓言變成陌生人,娶佢定係唔好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你願意帶著她所有的缺陷,沒有朋友,剛被收養進我們的恨,以我們的詛咒為嫁妝,被我們的誓言變成陌生人,娶她還是不要?

passages.title: Burgundy 勃艮第
passages.original: Pardon me, royal sir; Election makes not up in such conditions.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,尊貴嘅陛下;喺咁樣嘅條件下,選擇無法成立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,尊貴的陛下;在這樣的條件下,選擇無法成立。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Then leave her, sir; for, by the power that made me, I tell you all her wealth.
passages.vernacular: 咁放棄佢吧,先生;因為憑造我嘅力量,我已告訴你佢所有嘅財富。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼放棄她吧,先生;因為憑造我的力量,我已告訴你她所有的財富。

passages.original: [To France] For you, great king, I would not from your love make such a stray To match you where I hate;
passages.vernacular: [對法蘭西]至於您,偉大嘅國王,我唔願為了我對您嘅愛而偏離,把您配畀我所憎恨嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對法蘭西]至於您,偉大的國王,我不願為了我對您的愛而偏離,把您配給我所憎恨的人;

passages.original: therefore beseech you T’avert your liking a more worthier way Than on a wretch whom nature is asham’d Almost t’acknowledge hers.
passages.vernacular: 所以懇求您把您嘅喜愛轉向更配得上嘅方向,而唔係一個連造化都幾乎羞於承認嘅可憐人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以懇求您把您的喜愛轉向更配得上的方向,而不是一個連造化都幾乎羞於承認的可憐人。

passages.title: France 法蘭西國王
passages.original: This is most strange, That she, who even but now was your best object, The argument of your praise, balm of your age, The best, the dearest, should in this trice of time Commit a thing so monstrous, to dismantle So many folds of favour.
passages.vernacular: 呢最奇怪:佢頭先定係您最好嘅對象,您讚美嘅主題,您年老嘅香膏,最好、最親愛嘅,竟喺呢一瞬間幹出如此可怕嘅事,剝去咁多層恩寵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這最奇怪:她剛才還是您最好的對象,您讚美的主題,您年老的香膏,最好、最親愛的,竟在這一瞬間幹出如此可怕的事,剝去這麼多層恩寵。

passages.original: Sure her offence Must be of such unnatural degree That monsters it, or your fore-vouch’d affection Fall into taint;
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅過錯必定達到如此不自然嘅程度,才成為怪物,否則您先前所宣稱嘅愛就會受到玷污;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的過錯必定達到如此不自然的程度,才成為怪物,否則您先前所宣稱的愛就會受到玷污;

passages.original: which to believe of her Must be a faith that reason without miracle Should never plant in me.
passages.vernacular: 要相信佢咁樣,必須有一種信念,呢種信念冇奇蹟,理智絕唔會種進我心中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要相信她這樣,必須有一種信念,這種信念沒有奇蹟,理智絕不會種進我心中。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: I yet beseech your majesty, If for I want that glib and oily art To speak and purpose not;
passages.vernacular: 我仍然懇求陛下,如果因為我缺乏嗰種油滑嘅技巧,講話卻不誠心;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我仍然懇求陛下,如果因為我缺乏那種油滑的技巧,說話卻不誠心;

passages.original: since what I well intend, I’ll do’t before I speak,—that you make known It is no vicious blot, murder, or foulness, No unchaste action or dishonour’d step, That hath depriv’d me of your grace and favour;
passages.vernacular: 因為我真心想做嘅事,我先做後講——請您公開講明,剝奪我得到您恩寵嘅,唔係乜嘢惡行、謀殺或污穢,唔係乜嘢不貞嘅行為或不名譽嘅步伐;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我真心想做的事,我先做後說——請您公開說明,剝奪我得到您恩寵的,不是什麼惡行、謀殺或污穢,不是什麼不貞的行為或不名譽的步伐;

passages.original: But even for want of that for which I am richer, A still soliciting eye, and such a tongue As I am glad I have not, though not to have it Hath lost me in your liking.
passages.vernacular: 而正是因為缺少某種嘢,我反而更富有:一雙不斷懇求嘅眼睛、一條咁樣嘅舌頭,我慶幸我冇佢,雖然因為冇佢,我已失去您嘅喜愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而正是因為缺少某種東西,我反而更富有:一雙不斷懇求的眼睛、一條這樣的舌頭,我慶幸我沒有它,雖然因為沒有它,我已失去您的喜愛。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Better thou hadst Not been born than not to have pleas’d me better.
passages.vernacular: 你寧可冇出生,都不該冇能更讓我滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你寧可沒有出生,也不該沒能更讓我滿意。

passages.title: France 法蘭西國王
passages.original: Is it but this?—a tardiness in nature Which often leaves the history unspoke That it intends to do?
passages.vernacular: 只係呢個嗎?——一種天性上嘅遲鈍,往往把打算做嘅事留住冇講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是這個嗎?——一種天性上的遲鈍,往往把打算做的事留著沒說?

passages.original: My lord of Burgundy, What say you to the lady?
passages.vernacular: 勃艮第大人,你對呢位小姐點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勃艮第大人,你對這位小姐怎麼說?

passages.original: Love’s not love When it is mingled with regards that stands Aloof from the entire point.
passages.vernacular: 愛唔係愛,當佢混雜咗遠離整件事要點嘅考慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛不是愛,當它混雜了遠離整件事要點的考慮。

passages.original: Will you have her?
passages.vernacular: 你要娶佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要娶她嗎?

passages.original: She is herself a dowry.
passages.vernacular: 佢本身就係嫁妝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本身就是嫁妝。

passages.title: Burgundy 勃艮第
passages.original: Royal King, Give but that portion which yourself propos’d, And here I take Cordelia by the hand, Duchess of Burgundy.
passages.vernacular: 尊貴嘅國王,只要畀出您自己提出嘅嗰份,我喺此牽考黛莉亞嘅手,封佢為勃艮第公爵夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尊貴的國王,只要給出您自己提出的那份,我在此牽考黛莉亞的手,封她為勃艮第公爵夫人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Nothing: I have sworn; I am firm.
passages.vernacular: 冇:我已發誓;我堅定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有:我已發誓;我堅定。

passages.title: Burgundy 勃艮第
passages.original: I am sorry, then, you have so lost a father That you must lose a husband.
passages.vernacular: 咁我好遺憾,你失去咗父親,以致你必須失去丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼我很遺憾,你失去了父親,以致你必須失去丈夫。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Peace be with Burgundy!
passages.vernacular: 願平安同勃艮第同喺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願平安與勃艮第同在!

passages.original: Since that respects of fortunes are his love, I shall not be his wife.
passages.vernacular: 既然佢嘅愛係對財富嘅考量,我唔會做佢嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然他的愛是對財富的考量,我不會做他的妻子。

passages.title: France 法蘭西國王
passages.original: Fairest Cordelia, that art most rich, being poor;
passages.vernacular: 最美麗嘅考黛莉亞,你雖貧窮卻最富有;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最美麗的考黛莉亞,你雖貧窮卻最富有;

passages.original: Most choice forsaken; and most lov’d, despis’d!
passages.vernacular: 最被拋棄卻最珍貴;被鄙視卻最被愛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最被拋棄卻最珍貴;被鄙視卻最被愛!

passages.original: Thee and thy virtues here I seize upon: Be it lawful, I take up what’s cast away. Gods, gods!
passages.vernacular: 我喺此抓住你同你嘅美德:讓我拾起被丟棄嘅嘢,合乎法律。諸神,諸神!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在此抓住你和你的美德:讓我拾起被丟棄的東西,合乎法律。諸神,諸神!

passages.original: ’Tis strange that from their cold’st neglect My love should kindle to inflam’d respect.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪啊,從佢哋最冷漠嘅忽視中,我嘅愛竟燃起火熱嘅敬重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪啊,從他們最冷漠的忽視中,我的愛竟燃起火熱的敬重。

passages.original: Thy dowerless daughter, King, thrown to my chance, Is queen of us, of ours, and our fair France:
passages.vernacular: 國王啊,你呢無嫁妝嘅女兒落到我嘅機緣中,佢係我哋、我哋嘅同美好法蘭西嘅女王:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王啊,你這無嫁妝的女兒落到我的機緣中,她是我們、我們的和美好法蘭西的女王:

passages.original: Not all the dukes of waterish Burgundy Can buy this unpriz’d precious maid of me.
passages.vernacular: 整個水汪汪嘅勃艮第所有公爵,都唔能夠從我呢度買到呢位無人珍視嘅珍貴少女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個水汪汪的勃艮第所有公爵,也不能從我這裡買到這位無人珍視的珍貴少女。

passages.original: Bid them farewell, Cordelia, though unkind: Thou losest here, a better where to find.
passages.vernacular: 向佢哋告別吧,考黛莉亞,雖然佢哋不仁慈:你喺呢度失去,將喺別處找到更好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向他們告別吧,考黛莉亞,雖然他們不仁慈:你在這裡失去,將在別處找到更好的。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Thou hast her, France: let her be thine; for we Have no such daughter, nor shall ever see That face of hers again.
passages.vernacular: 你得到佢喇,法蘭西:佢係你嘅;因為我哋冇咁樣嘅女兒,都永遠唔會再見到佢嗰張臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得到她了,法蘭西:她是你的;因為我們沒有這樣的女兒,也永遠不會再見到她那張臉。

passages.original: Therefore be gone Without our grace, our love, our benison.
passages.vernacular: 所以走吧,冇我哋嘅恩寵、愛同祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以走吧,沒有我們的恩寵、愛和祝福。

passages.original: Come, noble Burgundy.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,高貴嘅勃艮第。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,高貴的勃艮第。

passages.original: [Flourish. Exeunt Lear, Burgundy, Cornwall, Albany, Gloucester and Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [號角齊鳴。李爾、勃艮第、康華爾、奧本尼、葛羅斯特同侍從哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [號角齊鳴。李爾、勃艮第、康華爾、奧本尼、葛羅斯特和侍從們下。]

passages.title: France 法蘭西國王
passages.original: Bid farewell to your sisters.
passages.vernacular: 向你哋姊姊告別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向你們姊姊告別。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: The jewels of our father, with wash’d eyes Cordelia leaves you:
passages.vernacular: 我哋父親嘅珍寶,考黛莉亞含住洗過嘅淚眼向你哋告別:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們父親的珍寶,考黛莉亞含著洗過的淚眼向你們告別:

passages.original: I know you what you are; And like a sister am most loath to call Your faults as they are nam’d.
passages.vernacular: 我知道你哋係乜嘢人;作為妹妹,我好唔願按名稱稱呼你哋嘅過錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道你們是什麼人;作為妹妹,我非常不願按名稱稱呼你們的過錯。

passages.original: Love well our father: To your professed bosoms I commit him:
passages.vernacular: 好好愛我哋嘅父親:我把佢託付畀你哋口口聲聲講嘅胸懷:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好好愛我們的父親:我把他託付給你們口口聲聲說的胸懷:

passages.original: But yet, alas, stood I within his grace, I would prefer him to a better place.
passages.vernacular: 但哎呀,如果我仲喺佢嘅恩寵之內,我會把佢安置到更好嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但哎呀,如果我還在他的恩寵之內,我會把他安置到更好的地方。

passages.original: So farewell to you both.
passages.vernacular: 所以向你哋兩位告別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以向你們兩位告別。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Prescribe not us our duties.
passages.vernacular: 唔使你嚟規定我哋嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用你來規定我們的責任。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Let your study Be to content your lord, who hath receiv’d you At fortune’s alms.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅心思該放喺讓你丈夫滿意上,佢接納你,係出於命運嘅施捨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的心思該放在讓你丈夫滿意上,他接納你,是出於命運的施捨。

passages.original: You have obedience scanted, And well are worth the want that you have wanted.
passages.vernacular: 你吝嗇咗順從,正配得上你所缺少嘅嗰份。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你吝嗇了順從,正配得上你所缺少的那份。

passages.title: Cordelia 考黛莉亞
passages.original: Time shall unfold what plighted cunning hides:
passages.vernacular: 時間會揭示誓言所掩蓋嘅詭計:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間會揭示誓言所掩蓋的詭計:

passages.original: Who covers faults, at last shame derides.
passages.vernacular: 掩蓋過錯嘅人,最終被羞恥嘲笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 掩蓋過錯的人,最終被羞恥嘲笑。

passages.original: Well may you prosper.
passages.vernacular: 祝你哋好運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 祝你們好運。

passages.title: France 法蘭西國王
passages.original: Come, my fair Cordelia.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我美麗嘅考黛莉亞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我美麗的考黛莉亞。

passages.original: [Exeunt France and Cordelia.]
passages.vernacular: [法蘭西同考黛莉亞下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [法蘭西和考黛莉亞下。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Sister, it is not little I have to say of what most nearly appertains to us both.
passages.vernacular: 姊姊,關於同我哋兩人最切身嘅事,我有不少要講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 姊姊,關於與我們兩人最切身的事,我有不少要說。

passages.original: I think our father will hence tonight.
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋父親今晚就會離開呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們父親今晚就會離開這裡。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: That’s most certain, and with you; next month with us.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係肯定嘅,而且係到你嗰度;下個月到我哋嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是肯定的,而且是到你那裡;下個月到我們那裡。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: You see how full of changes his age is; the observation we have made of it hath not been little:
passages.vernacular: 你睇佢年老幾咁多變;我哋對此嘅觀察不少:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看他年老多麼多變;我們對此的觀察不少:

passages.original: he always loved our sister most; and with what poor judgement he hath now cast her off appears too grossly.
passages.vernacular: 佢一向最愛我哋妹妹;佢而家用幾咁拙劣嘅判斷拋棄咗佢,顯得太明顯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一向最愛我們妹妹;他現在用多麼拙劣的判斷拋棄了她,顯得太明顯。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: ’Tis the infirmity of his age: yet he hath ever but slenderly known himself.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係佢年老嘅弱點:然而佢一向只係淺薄地認識自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是他年老的弱點:然而他一向只是淺薄地認識自己。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: The best and soundest of his time hath been but rash;
passages.vernacular: 佢一生最好最健全嘅時期,都不過係魯莽;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一生最好最健全的時期,也不過是魯莽;

passages.original: then must we look from his age to receive not alone the imperfections of long-engrafted condition, but therewithal the unruly waywardness that infirm and choleric years bring with them.
passages.vernacular: 所以我哋必須預期從佢嘅年老中得到嘅,不只係長期根深蒂固嘅性情缺陷,仲有衰弱同易怒嘅年歲帶嚟嘅任性難馴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我們必須預期從他的年老中得到的,不只是長期根深蒂固的性情缺陷,還有衰弱和易怒的年歲帶來的任性難馴。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Such unconstant starts are we like to have from him as this of Kent’s banishment.
passages.vernacular: 我哋可能仲會從佢得到像肯特被放逐咁樣不穩定嘅衝動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們可能還會從他得到像肯特被放逐這樣不穩定的衝動。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: There is further compliment of leave-taking between France and him.
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西同佢之間仲有告別嘅客套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西與他之間還有告別的客套。

passages.original: Pray you let us hit together: if our father carry authority with such disposition as he bears, this last surrender of his will but offend us.
passages.vernacular: 請你,我哋一起行動:如果我哋父親帶住佢而家嘅性情行使權力,佢呢次最後嘅退位只會冒犯我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,我們一起行動:如果我們父親帶著他現在的性情行使權力,他這次最後的退位只會冒犯我們。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: We shall further think of it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋再進一步考慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們再進一步考慮。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: We must do something, and i’ th’ heat.
passages.vernacular: 我哋必須做些乜嘢,而且趁熱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們必須做些什麼,而且趁熱。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene II — A Hall in Gloucester’s Castle 第一幕第二場:葛羅斯特伯爵城堡大廳

passages.original: Enter Edmund with a letter.
passages.vernacular: [愛德蒙持信上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德蒙持信上。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Thou, Nature, art my goddess; to thy law My services are bound.
passages.vernacular: 你,自然,係我嘅女神;我嘅服務受你嘅法則約束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,自然,是我的女神;我的服務受你的法則約束。

passages.original: Wherefore should I Stand in the plague of custom, and permit The curiosity of nations to deprive me?
passages.vernacular: 點解我要陷喺習俗嘅瘟疫中,讓國家嘅挑剔剝奪我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼我要陷在習俗的瘟疫中,讓國家的挑剔剝奪我?

passages.original: For that I am some twelve or fourteen moonshines Lag of a brother?
passages.vernacular: 就因為我比哥哥晚出生十二、十四個月亮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就因為我比哥哥晚出生十二、十四個月亮?

passages.original: Why bastard?
passages.vernacular: 點解係私生子?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼是私生子?

passages.original: Wherefore base?
passages.vernacular: 點解卑賤?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼卑賤?

passages.original: When my dimensions are as well compact, My mind as generous, and my shape as true As honest madam’s issue?
passages.vernacular: 當我嘅體格同樣勻稱,心靈同樣高貴,身材同樣端正,像正經夫人所生嘅細路一樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我的體格同樣勻稱,心靈同樣高貴,身材同樣端正,像正經夫人所生的孩子一樣?

passages.original: Why brand they us With base?
passages.vernacular: 點解佢哋畀我哋烙上卑賤?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼他們給我們烙上卑賤?

passages.original: With baseness? bastardy? Base, base?
passages.vernacular: 卑賤?私生?卑賤,卑賤?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卑賤?私生?卑賤,卑賤?

passages.original: Who, in the lusty stealth of nature, take More composition and fierce quality Than doth within a dull stale tired bed Go to the creating a whole tribe of fops Got ’tween asleep and wake?
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺自然嗰旺盛嘅偷歡中,得到嘅組成同強烈嘅品質,比嗰喺沉悶、陳舊、疲倦嘅床上、半瞓半醒間生出嘅一整群蠢貨,仲要多?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在自然那旺盛的偷歡中,得到的組成和強烈的品質,比那在沉悶、陳舊、疲倦的床上、半睡半醒間生出的一整群蠢貨,還要多?

passages.original: Well then, Legitimate Edgar, I must have your land:
passages.vernacular: 好,咁,合法嘅愛德伽,我必須得到你嘅土地:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那麼,合法的愛德伽,我必須得到你的土地:

passages.original: Our father’s love is to the bastard Edmund As to the legitimate: fine word: legitimate!
passages.vernacular: 我哋父親對私生子愛德蒙嘅愛,同對合法嘅一樣:好詞:合法!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們父親對私生子愛德蒙的愛,和對合法的一樣:好詞:合法!

passages.original: Well, my legitimate, if this letter speed, And my invention thrive, Edmund the base Shall top the legitimate.
passages.vernacular: 好,我嘅合法兒,如果呢封信成功,我嘅計謀得逞,卑賤嘅愛德蒙將壓過合法嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我的合法兒,如果這封信成功,我的計謀得逞,卑賤的愛德蒙將壓過合法的。

passages.original: I grow, I prosper.
passages.vernacular: 我喺成長,我喺興旺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在成長,我在興旺。

passages.original: Now, gods, stand up for bastards!
passages.vernacular: 而家,諸神啊,為私生子撐腰吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,諸神啊,為私生子撐腰吧!

passages.original: Enter Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特上。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Kent banish’d thus!
passages.vernacular: 肯特就咁樣被放逐喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 肯特就這樣被放逐了!

passages.original: and France in choler parted!
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西盛怒而去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西盛怒而去!

passages.original: And the King gone tonight!
passages.vernacular: 國王今晚走喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王今晚走了!

passages.original: Prescrib’d his pow’r!
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅權力被限制!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的權力被限制!

passages.original: Confin’d to exhibition!
passages.vernacular: 被限制到只領津貼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被限制到只領津貼!

passages.original: All this done Upon the gad!—Edmund, how now! What news?
passages.vernacular: 呢一切都係倉促做成!——愛德蒙,點喇!有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切都是倉促做成!——愛德蒙,怎麼了!有什麼消息?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: So please your lordship, none.
passages.vernacular: 稟大人,冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稟大人,沒有。

passages.original: [Putting up the letter.]
passages.vernacular: [把信收起。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把信收起。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Why so earnestly seek you to put up that letter?
passages.vernacular: 你點解咁急住把嗰封信收起嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼這麼急著把那封信收起來?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I know no news, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道有乜嘢消息,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道有什麼消息,大人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: What paper were you reading?
passages.vernacular: 你喺睇乜嘢紙?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在看什麼紙?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Nothing, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 冇乜嘢,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒什麼,大人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: No?
passages.vernacular: 冇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有?

passages.original: What needed then that terrible dispatch of it into your pocket?
passages.vernacular: 嗰點解要嗰樣可怕地急住塞進口袋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那為什麼要那樣可怕地急著塞進口袋?

passages.original: The quality of nothing hath not such need to hide itself. Let’s see.
passages.vernacular: 無關緊要嘅嘢不需要咁藏住。讓我睇睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無關緊要的東西不需要這麼藏著。讓我看看。

passages.original: Come, if it be nothing, I shall not need spectacles.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,如果係無關緊要嘅,我就不需要眼鏡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,如果是無關緊要的,我就不需要眼鏡。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I beseech you, sir, pardon me.
passages.vernacular: 我懇求您,父親,請原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求您,父親,請原諒我。

passages.original: It is a letter from my brother that I have not all o’er-read;
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我哥哥嘅信,我仲冇完全讀完;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我哥哥的信,我還沒完全讀完;

passages.original: and for so much as I have perus’d, I find it not fit for your o’er-looking.
passages.vernacular: 就我已經睇過嘅部分來講,我覺得不適合您過目。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我已經看過的部分來說,我覺得不適合您過目。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Give me the letter, sir.
passages.vernacular: 把信畀我,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把信給我,先生。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I shall offend, either to detain or give it.
passages.vernacular: 無論扣留定係畀出,我都會冒犯您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論扣留還是給出,我都會冒犯您。

passages.original: The contents, as in part I understand them, are to blame.
passages.vernacular: 內容,就我所理解嘅部分,係有過錯嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 內容,就我所理解的部分,是有過錯的。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Let’s see, let’s see!
passages.vernacular: 讓我睇睇,讓我睇睇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我看看,讓我看看!

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I hope, for my brother’s justification, he wrote this but as an essay, or taste of my virtue.
passages.vernacular: 我希望,為替我哥哥辯護,佢寫呢個只係作為一種試驗,或測試我嘅美德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望,為替我哥哥辯護,他寫這個只是作為一種試驗,或測試我的美德。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: [Reads.]
‘This policy and reverence of age makes the world bitter to the best of our times;
passages.vernacular: 「呢種對老年嘅政策同敬畏,使世界對我哋最好嘅年華變得苦澀;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這種對老年的政策和敬畏,使世界對我們最好的年華變得苦澀;

passages.original: keeps our fortunes from us till our oldness cannot relish them.
passages.vernacular: 佢使我哋嘅財富喺我哋老得無法享受之前被扣留。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它使我們的財富在我們老得無法享受之前被扣留。

passages.original: I begin to find an idle and fond bondage in the oppression of aged tyranny;
passages.vernacular: 我開始發而家年老暴君嘅壓迫中有一種無聊愚蠢嘅奴役;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我開始發現在年老暴君的壓迫中有一種無聊愚蠢的奴役;

passages.original: who sways not as it hath power, but as it is suffered.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係憑權力統治,而係憑人哋嘅容忍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是憑權力統治,而是憑人們的容忍。

passages.original: Come to me, that of this I may speak more.
passages.vernacular: 到我呢度嚟,我好就此多講些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到我這裡來,我好就此多說些。

passages.original: If our father would sleep till I waked him, you should enjoy half his revenue for ever, and live the beloved of your brother EDGAR.’ Hum! Conspiracy?
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋嘅父親瞓到我叫醒佢為止,你就能永遠享有佢一半嘅收入,並作為你哥哥愛德伽所愛嘅人生活。」哼!陰謀?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們的父親睡到我叫醒他為止,你就能永遠享有他一半的收入,並作為你哥哥愛德伽所愛的人生活。」哼!陰謀?

passages.original: ‘Sleep till I wake him, you should enjoy half his revenue.’—My son Edgar!
passages.vernacular: 「瞓到我叫醒佢,你就能享有佢一半嘅收入。」——我嘅兒子愛德伽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「睡到我叫醒他,你就能享有他一半的收入。」——我的兒子愛德伽!

passages.original: Had he a hand to write this?
passages.vernacular: 佢有手寫呢個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有手寫這個?

passages.original: A heart and brain to breed it in?
passages.vernacular: 有心同腦去孕育佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有心和腦去孕育它?

passages.original: When came this to you?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係乜嘢時候畀你嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是什麼時候給你的?

passages.original: Who brought it?
passages.vernacular: 邊個帶嚟嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰帶來的?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: It was not brought me, my lord, there’s the cunning of it.
passages.vernacular: 唔係帶畀我嘅,大人,呢個就係佢嘅狡猾之處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是帶給我的,大人,這就是它的狡猾之處。

passages.original: I found it thrown in at the casement of my closet.
passages.vernacular: 我發現佢從我書房嘅窗戶扔進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現它從我書房的窗戶扔進來。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: You know the character to be your brother’s?
passages.vernacular: 你知道呢筆跡係你哥哥嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道這筆跡是你哥哥的嗎?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: If the matter were good, my lord, I durst swear it were his;
passages.vernacular: 如果內容係好嘅,大人,我敢發誓係佢嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果內容是好的,大人,我敢發誓是他的;

passages.original: but in respect of that, I would fain think it were not.
passages.vernacular: 但就內容而言,我寧願認為唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但就內容而言,我寧願認為不是。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: It is his.
passages.vernacular: 係佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是他的。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: It is his hand, my lord; but I hope his heart is not in the contents.
passages.vernacular: 係佢嘅手跡,大人;不過我希望佢嘅心不在內容裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是他的手跡,大人;不過我希望他的心不在內容裡。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Has he never before sounded you in this business?
passages.vernacular: 佢以前冇就呢件事試探過你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以前沒有就這件事試探過你嗎?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Never, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 從冇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從沒有,大人。

passages.original: But I have heard him oft maintain it to be fit that, sons at perfect age, and fathers declined, the father should be as ward to the son, and the son manage his revenue.
passages.vernacular: 但我常聽佢主張,兒子到咗成年、父親衰老時,父親應該像被監護人一樣受兒子監護,由兒子管理佢嘅收入。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我常聽他主張,兒子到了成年、父親衰老時,父親應該像被監護人一樣受兒子監護,由兒子管理他的收入。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: O villain, villain!
passages.vernacular: 啊惡棍,惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊惡棍,惡棍!

passages.original: His very opinion in the letter!
passages.vernacular: 就係信裡嘅意見!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是信裡的意見!

passages.original: Abhorred villain!
passages.vernacular: 可憎嘅惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憎的惡棍!

passages.original: Unnatural, detested, brutish villain!
passages.vernacular: 不自然、可憎、野獸般嘅惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不自然、可憎、野獸般的惡棍!

passages.original: worse than brutish!
passages.vernacular: 比野獸仲不如!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比野獸還不如!

passages.original: Go, sirrah, seek him; I’ll apprehend him.
passages.vernacular: 去,小子,找佢;我要逮捕佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,小子,找他;我要逮捕他。

passages.original: Abominable villain, Where is he?
passages.vernacular: 可憎嘅惡棍,佢喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憎的惡棍,他在哪裡?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I do not well know, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我不太清楚,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不太清楚,大人。

passages.original: If it shall please you to suspend your indignation against my brother till you can derive from him better testimony of his intent, you should run a certain course;
passages.vernacular: 如果您肯暫時按下對我哥哥嘅憤怒,直到能從佢嗰度得到更好嘅關於佢意圖嘅證據,您就會走上一條穩妥嘅路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您肯暫時按下對我哥哥的憤怒,直到能從他那裡得到更好的關於他意圖的證據,您就會走上一條穩妥的路;

passages.original: where, if you violently proceed against him, mistaking his purpose, it would make a great gap in your own honour, and shake in pieces the heart of his obedience.
passages.vernacular: 若您暴烈地對付佢,誤解咗佢嘅用意,會對您自己嘅名譽造成好大缺口,並震碎佢順從嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 若您暴烈地對付他,誤解了他的用意,會對您自己的名譽造成很大缺口,並震碎他順從的心。

passages.original: I dare pawn down my life for him, that he hath writ this to feel my affection to your honour, and to no other pretence of danger.
passages.vernacular: 我敢用我嘅生命為佢擔保,佢寫呢個係為了試探我對您嘅敬愛,並無其他危險嘅圖謀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢用我的生命為他擔保,他寫這個是為了試探我對您的敬愛,並無其他危險的圖謀。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Think you so?
passages.vernacular: 你咁樣想嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這樣想嗎?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: If your honour judge it meet, I will place you where you shall hear us confer of this, and by an auricular assurance have your satisfaction, and that without any further delay than this very evening.
passages.vernacular: 如果您認為合適,我會把您安置喺一處,讓您聽到我哋談呢件事,憑親耳聽到嘅保證得到滿足,而且唔使比今晚更多嘅拖延。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您認為合適,我會把您安置在一處,讓您聽到我們談這件事,憑親耳聽到的保證得到滿足,而且不用比今晚更多的拖延。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: He cannot be such a monster.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔可能係咁樣嘅怪物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不可能是這樣的怪物。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Nor is not, sure.
passages.vernacular: 確實唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實不是。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: To his father, that so tenderly and entirely loves him.
passages.vernacular: 對待嗰樣溫柔、全心愛佢嘅父親!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對待那樣溫柔、全心愛他的父親!

passages.original: Heaven and earth!
passages.vernacular: 天地啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天地啊!

passages.original: Edmund, seek him out; wind me into him, I pray you:
passages.vernacular: 愛德蒙,去找佢;請你設法套佢嘅話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛德蒙,去找他;請你設法套他的話:

passages.original: frame the business after your own wisdom.
passages.vernacular: 按你自己嘅智慧安排呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按你自己的智慧安排這件事。

passages.original: I would unstate myself to be in a due resolution.
passages.vernacular: 我願放棄我嘅身份,只為得到確切嘅了結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我願放棄我的身份,只為得到確切的了結。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I will seek him, sir, presently; convey the business as I shall find means, and acquaint you withal.
passages.vernacular: 我會即刻去找佢,先生;我會按我找到嘅辦法安排呢件事,然後告訴您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會馬上去找他,先生;我會按我找到的辦法安排這件事,然後告訴您。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: These late eclipses in the sun and moon portend no good to us:
passages.vernacular: 最近呢啲日蝕月蝕對我哋唔係好兆頭:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最近這些日蝕月蝕對我們不是好兆頭:

passages.original: though the wisdom of Nature can reason it thus and thus, yet nature finds itself scourged by the sequent effects.
passages.vernacular: 雖然自然嘅智慧可以咁樣嗰樣地推理,但自然發現自己被隨後嘅結果鞭笞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然自然的智慧可以這樣那樣地推理,但自然發現自己被隨後的結果鞭笞。

passages.original: Love cools, friendship falls off, brothers divide:
passages.vernacular: 愛冷卻,友誼崩落,兄弟分裂:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛冷卻,友誼崩落,兄弟分裂:

passages.original: in cities, mutinies; in countries, discord; in palaces, treason;
passages.vernacular: 城市裡有叛亂,國家裡有不同,宮殿裡有叛逆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 城市裡有叛亂,國家裡有不和,宮殿裡有叛逆;

passages.original: and the bond cracked ’twixt son and father.
passages.vernacular: 兒子同父親之間嘅紐帶斷裂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兒子與父親之間的紐帶斷裂。

passages.original: This villain of mine comes under the prediction;
passages.vernacular: 我呢個惡棍兒子正應咗預言;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這個惡棍兒子正應了預言;

passages.original: there’s son against father: the King falls from bias of nature;
passages.vernacular: 呢個係兒子對父親:國王偏離咗天性嘅軌道;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是兒子對父親:國王偏離了天性的軌道;

passages.original: there’s father against child.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係父親對細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是父親對孩子。

passages.original: We have seen the best of our time.
passages.vernacular: 我哋已經見過我哋最好嘅時代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們已經見過我們最好的時代。

passages.original: Machinations, hollowness, treachery, and all ruinous disorders follow us disquietly to our graves.
passages.vernacular: 陰謀、空洞、背叛,以及一切毀滅性嘅混亂,不安地跟隨我哋直到墳墓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 陰謀、空洞、背叛,以及一切毀滅性的混亂,不安地跟隨我們直到墳墓。

passages.original: Find out this villain, Edmund; it shall lose thee nothing;
passages.vernacular: 找出呢個惡棍,愛德蒙;你唔會有損失;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找出這個惡棍,愛德蒙;你不會有損失;

passages.original: do it carefully.—And the noble and true-hearted Kent banished!
passages.vernacular: 要小心做。——仲有高貴而真心嘅肯特被放逐喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要小心做。——還有高貴而真心的肯特被放逐了!

passages.original: his offence, honesty!
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅罪過,係誠實!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的罪過,是誠實!

passages.original: ’Tis strange.
passages.vernacular: 真奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真奇怪。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: This is the excellent foppery of the world, that, when we are sick in fortune, often the surfeits of our own behaviour, we make guilty of our disasters the sun, the moon, and the stars;
passages.vernacular: 呢個係世界最精彩嘅愚蠢:當我哋命運不濟(往往係自己行為過度嘅結果)時,我哋把災難歸咎於太陽、月亮同星星;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是世界最精彩的愚蠢:當我們命運不濟(往往是自己行為過度的結果)時,我們把災難歸咎於太陽、月亮和星星;

passages.original: as if we were villains on necessity; fools by heavenly compulsion;
passages.vernacular: 彷彿我哋係被迫嘅惡棍;係天意驅使嘅傻瓜;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彷彿我們是被迫的惡棍;是天意驅使的傻瓜;

passages.original: knaves, thieves, and treachers by spherical predominance;
passages.vernacular: 因天體主宰而成為騙子、盜賊同叛徒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因天體主宰而成為騙子、盜賊和叛徒;

passages.original: drunkards, liars, and adulterers by an enforced obedience of planetary influence;
passages.vernacular: 因行星影響嘅強制服從而成為酒鬼、騙子同姦夫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因行星影響的強制服從而成為酒鬼、騙子和姦夫;

passages.original: and all that we are evil in, by a divine thrusting on.
passages.vernacular: 我哋所有嘅惡,都係神聖嘅推動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們所有的惡,都是神聖的推動。

passages.original: An admirable evasion of whoremaster man, to lay his goatish disposition to the charge of a star.
passages.vernacular: 嫖客人類真係絕妙嘅推諉:把佢山羊般嘅性情歸咎於一顆星。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嫖客人類真是絕妙的推諉:把他山羊般的性情歸咎於一顆星。

passages.original: My father compounded with my mother under the dragon’s tail, and my nativity was under Ursa Major, so that it follows I am rough and lecherous. Fut!
passages.vernacular: 我父親喺龍尾星座之下同我母親交合,我出生喺大熊星座之下,所以我必然粗暴好色。呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親在龍尾星座之下與我母親交合,我出生在大熊星座之下,所以我必然粗暴好色。呸!

passages.original: I should have been that I am, had the maidenliest star in the firmament twinkled on my bastardizing.
passages.vernacular: 即使天上最貞潔嘅星星喺我成為私生子時閃爍,我都定係而家咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使天上最貞潔的星星在我成為私生子時閃爍,我也還是現在這樣。

passages.original: Enter Edgar.
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽上。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Pat!
passages.vernacular: 正好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正好!

passages.original: he comes, like the catastrophe of the old comedy:
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟喇,像老喜劇嘅收場:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來了,像老喜劇的收場:

passages.original: my cue is villainous melancholy, with a sigh like Tom o’Bedlam.—O, these eclipses do portend these divisions!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅提示係惡毒嘅憂鬱,像貝德蘭嘅湯姆嗰樣歎氣。——啊,呢啲日蝕月蝕預示呢啲分裂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的提示是惡毒的憂鬱,像貝德蘭的湯姆那樣歎氣。——啊,這些日蝕月蝕預示這些分裂!

passages.original: Fa, sol, la, mi.
passages.vernacular: 發,索,拉,咪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發,索,拉,咪。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: How now, brother Edmund, what serious contemplation are you in?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,哥哥愛德蒙,你喺沉思乜嘢嚴肅嘅事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,哥哥愛德蒙,你在沉思什麼嚴肅的事?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I am thinking, brother, of a prediction I read this other day, what should follow these eclipses.
passages.vernacular: 我喺想,哥哥,我前幾天讀到嘅一個預言,講呢啲日蝕月蝕之後會發生乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在想,哥哥,我前幾天讀到的一個預言,說這些日蝕月蝕之後會發生什麼。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Do you busy yourself with that?
passages.vernacular: 你為呢個操心?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為這個操心?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I promise you, the effects he writes of succeed unhappily:
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證,佢所寫嘅後果不幸地接連發生:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證,他所寫的後果不幸地接連發生:

passages.original: as of unnaturalness between the child and the parent;
passages.vernacular: 比如細路同父母之間嘅不自然;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比如孩子與父母之間的不自然;

passages.original: death, dearth, dissolutions of ancient amities;
passages.vernacular: 死亡、饑荒、古老友誼嘅解體;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 死亡、饑荒、古老友誼的解體;

passages.original: divisions in state, menaces and maledictions against King and nobles;
passages.vernacular: 國家嘅分裂、對國王同貴族嘅威脅同詛咒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國家的分裂、對國王和貴族的威脅與詛咒;

passages.original: needless diffidences, banishment of friends, dissipation of cohorts, nuptial breaches, and I know not what.
passages.vernacular: 無謂嘅猜疑、朋友被放逐、軍隊離散、婚姻破裂,仲有我唔知道嘅乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無謂的猜疑、朋友被放逐、軍隊離散、婚姻破裂,還有我不知道的什麼。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: How long have you been a sectary astronomical?
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢時候成咗星相學嘅信徒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼時候成了星相學的信徒?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Come, come!
passages.vernacular: 嚟,嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,來!

passages.original: when saw you my father last?
passages.vernacular: 你最後一次見我父親係乜嘢時候?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最後一次見我父親是什麼時候?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: The night gone by.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Spake you with him?
passages.vernacular: 你同佢講話咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和他說話了嗎?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Ay, two hours together.
passages.vernacular: 講喇,一起兩個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說了,一起兩個小時。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Parted you in good terms?
passages.vernacular: 你哋分別時關係好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們分別時關係好嗎?

passages.original: Found you no displeasure in him, by word nor countenance?
passages.vernacular: 你喺佢言語或神色中冇發現不悅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在他言語或神色中沒有發現不悅嗎?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: None at all.
passages.vernacular: 啲都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一點也沒有。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Bethink yourself wherein you may have offended him:
passages.vernacular: 想想你可能喺邊方面冒犯咗佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想你可能在哪方面冒犯了他:

passages.original: and at my entreaty forbear his presence until some little time hath qualified the heat of his displeasure;
passages.vernacular: 並請你聽我嘅勸告,暫時避開佢,直到過一段時間緩和佢嘅怒氣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並請你聽我的勸告,暫時避開他,直到過一段時間緩和他的怒氣;

passages.original: which at this instant so rageth in him that with the mischief of your person it would scarcely allay.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢正怒火中燒,即使傷害你嘅身體都未必能平息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他正怒火中燒,即使傷害你的身體也未必能平息。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Some villain hath done me wrong.
passages.vernacular: 有個惡棍冤枉咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個惡棍冤枉了我。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: That’s my fear.
passages.vernacular: 我就係怕呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是怕這個。

passages.original: I pray you have a continent forbearance till the speed of his rage goes slower;
passages.vernacular: 請你克制地忍耐,直到佢嘅怒氣嘅速度放慢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你克制地忍耐,直到他的怒氣的速度放慢;

passages.original: and, as I say, retire with me to my lodging, from whence I will fitly bring you to hear my lord speak:
passages.vernacular: 並且,正如我講,隨我到我嘅住處,我會喺適當嘅時候帶你去聽我哋大人講話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並且,正如我說,隨我到我的住處,我會在適當的時候帶你去聽我們大人說話:

passages.original: pray ye, go; there’s my key.
passages.vernacular: 請你去吧;呢個係我嘅鑰匙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你去吧;這是我的鑰匙。

passages.original: If you do stir abroad, go armed.
passages.vernacular: 如果你出門,要帶武器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你出門,要帶武器。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Armed, brother?
passages.vernacular: 帶武器,哥哥?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶武器,哥哥?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Brother, I advise you to the best; I am no honest man if there be any good meaning toward you:
passages.vernacular: 哥哥,我為你好才咁樣勸;如果有任何好意對你,我就唔係誠實嘅人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哥哥,我為你好才這樣勸;如果有任何好意對你,我就不是誠實的人:

passages.original: I have told you what I have seen and heard.
passages.vernacular: 我已告訴你我所見所聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已告訴你我所見所聞。

passages.original: But faintly; nothing like the image and horror of it: pray you, away!
passages.vernacular: 只係好微弱;完全冇嗰景象同恐怖嘅樣子:請你快走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是很微弱;完全沒有那景象和恐怖的樣子:請你快走!

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Shall I hear from you anon?
passages.vernacular: 我好快會收到你嘅消息嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很快會收到你的消息嗎?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I do serve you in this business.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢件事上我為你效勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這件事上我為你效勞。

passages.original: [Exit Edgar.]
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽下。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: A credulous father!
passages.vernacular: 輕信嘅父親!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕信的父親!

passages.original: and a brother noble, Whose nature is so far from doing harms That he suspects none;
passages.vernacular: 仲有高貴嘅哥哥,佢嘅天性遠離害人,以致佢不懷疑任何人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有高貴的哥哥,他的天性遠離害人,以致他不懷疑任何人;

passages.original: on whose foolish honesty My practices ride easy!
passages.vernacular: 喺佢愚蠢嘅誠實之上,我嘅計謀騎得幾咁輕鬆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他愚蠢的誠實之上,我的計謀騎得多麼輕鬆!

passages.original: I see the business.
passages.vernacular: 我睇清咗呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看清了這件事。

passages.original: Let me, if not by birth, have lands by wit; All with me’s meet that I can fashion fit.
passages.vernacular: 讓我,若唔能夠憑出身,就憑智慧得到土地;凡是我能設計得合適嘅,一切都合我意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我,若不能憑出身,就憑智慧得到土地;凡是我能設計得合適的,一切都合我意。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene III — A Room in Albany’s Palace 第一幕第三場:奧本尼公爵宮中一室

passages.original: Enter Goneril and Oswald.
passages.vernacular: [高納麗同奧斯華上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [高納麗和奧斯華上。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Did my father strike my gentleman for chiding of his fool?
passages.vernacular: 我父親係為了責備佢嘅弄臣,就打咗我嘅紳士嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親是為了責備他的弄臣,就打了我的紳士嗎?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Ay, madam.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,夫人。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: By day and night, he wrongs me; every hour He flashes into one gross crime or other, That sets us all at odds;
passages.vernacular: 日日夜夜,佢都冤枉我;每一個小時佢都爆發出某樁粗劣嘅過錯,使我哋大家不同;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 日日夜夜,他都冤枉我;每一個小時他都爆發出某樁粗劣的過錯,使我們大家不和;

passages.original: I’ll not endure it: His knights grow riotous, and himself upbraids us On every trifle.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠忍受:佢嘅騎士哋越嚟越放肆,佢自己都為每件小事責罵我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能忍受:他的騎士們越來越放肆,他自己也為每件小事責罵我們。

passages.original: When he returns from hunting, I will not speak with him; say I am sick.
passages.vernacular: 當佢打獵回嚟,我不跟佢講話;講我病喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他打獵回來,我不跟他說話;說我病了。

passages.original: If you come slack of former services, You shall do well;
passages.vernacular: 如果你比以前嘅服侍怠慢啲,你會做得好好;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你比以前的服侍怠慢一些,你會做得很好;

passages.original: the fault of it I’ll answer.
passages.vernacular: 呢個過錯由我承擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個過錯由我承擔。

passages.original: [Horns within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。]

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: He’s coming, madam; I hear him.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟喇,夫人;我聽到佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來了,夫人;我聽到他了。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Put on what weary negligence you please, You and your fellows;
passages.vernacular: 你同你嘅同伴哋儘管表現得多疲倦懶散都行;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和你的同伴們儘管表現得多疲倦懶散都行;

passages.original: I’d have it come to question: If he distaste it, let him to our sister, Whose mind and mine, I know, in that are one, Not to be overruled.
passages.vernacular: 我要讓佢成為問題:如果佢不滿意,讓佢去找我哋妹妹,佢嘅想法同我嘅喺呢點上係一致嘅,唔會被推翻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要讓它成為問題:如果他不滿意,讓他去找我們妹妹,她的想法和我的在這點上是一致的,不會被推翻。

passages.original: Idle old man, That still would manage those authorities That he hath given away!
passages.vernacular: 無聊嘅老頭,仲想管理佢已經畀出去嘅權力!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無聊的老頭,還想管理他已經給出去的權力!

passages.original: Now, by my life, Old fools are babes again; and must be us’d With checks as flatteries, when they are seen abus’d.
passages.vernacular: 而家,憑我嘅生命,老傻瓜又變成嬰兒喇;當睇到佢哋被縱容壞咗時,必須像哄騙一樣用責罵嚟對待佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,憑我的生命,老傻瓜又變成嬰兒了;當看到他們被縱容壞了時,必須像哄騙一樣用責罵來對待他們。

passages.original: Remember what I have said.
passages.vernacular: 記住我講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記住我說的話。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Very well, madam.
passages.vernacular: 好好,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很好,夫人。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: And let his knights have colder looks among you;
passages.vernacular: 仲要讓佢嘅騎士哋喺你哋中間得到更冷嘅臉色;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還要讓他的騎士們在你們中間得到更冷的臉色;

passages.original: What grows of it, no matter; advise your fellows so;
passages.vernacular: 結果如何唔好緊;叫你嘅同伴都咁樣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果如何不要緊;叫你的同伴也這樣;

passages.original: I would breed from hence occasions, and I shall, That I may speak.
passages.vernacular: 我要從呢度製造機會,我會嘅,好讓我講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要從這裡製造機會,我會的,好讓我說話。

passages.original: I’ll write straight to my sister To hold my very course.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻寫信畀我妹妹,讓佢走同樣嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我立刻寫信給我妹妹,讓她走同樣的路。

passages.original: Prepare for dinner.
passages.vernacular: 準備晚餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 準備晚餐。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene IV — A Hall in Albany’s Palace 第一幕第四場:奧本尼宮殿大廳

passages.original: Enter Kent, disguised.
passages.vernacular: [肯特喬裝上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特喬裝上。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: If but as well I other accents borrow, That can my speech defuse, my good intent May carry through itself to that full issue For which I rais’d my likeness.
passages.vernacular: 只要我同樣能借用其他口音,使我嘅語音變形,我嘅善意就能貫徹到我改變容貌所要達成嘅完整結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我同樣能借用其他口音,使我的語音變形,我的善意就能貫徹到我改變容貌所要達成的完整結果。

passages.original: Now, banish’d Kent, If thou canst serve where thou dost stand condemn’d, So may it come, thy master, whom thou lov’st, Shall find thee full of labours.
passages.vernacular: 而家,被放逐嘅肯特,如果你能喺被判罪嘅地方侍奉,或者你所愛嘅主人會發現你充滿勞績。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,被放逐的肯特,如果你能在被判罪的地方侍奉,也許你所愛的主人會發現你充滿勞績。

passages.original: Horns within. Enter King Lear, Knights and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。李爾王、騎士同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。李爾王、騎士和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Let me not stay a jot for dinner; go get it ready.
passages.vernacular: 我一刻都不等晚餐;去準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一刻也不等晚餐;去準備好。

passages.original: [Exit an Attendant.]
passages.vernacular: [一名侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名侍從下。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How now!
passages.vernacular: 點喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了!

passages.original: what art thou?
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼人?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: A man, sir.
passages.vernacular: 一個人,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人,先生。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What dost thou profess?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅職業係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的職業是什麼?

passages.original: What wouldst thou with us?
passages.vernacular: 你想要我哋做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想要我們做什麼?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I do profess to be no less than I seem; to serve him truly that will put me in trust;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅職業係不亞於我嘅外表;忠實地侍奉信任我嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的職業是不亞於我的外表;忠實地侍奉信任我的人;

passages.original: to love him that is honest; to converse with him that is wise and says little;
passages.vernacular: 愛誠實嘅人;同聰明又少言嘅人交談;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛誠實的人;與聰明又少言的人交談;

passages.original: to fear judgement; to fight when I cannot choose; and to eat no fish.
passages.vernacular: 敬畏審判;唔得已才打架;不食魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 敬畏審判;不得已才打架;不吃魚。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What art thou?
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼人?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: A very honest-hearted fellow, and as poor as the King.
passages.vernacular: 一個好誠實嘅人,同國王一樣窮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個非常誠實的人,和國王一樣窮。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: If thou be’st as poor for a subject as he’s for a king, thou art poor enough.
passages.vernacular: 如果你作為臣民像佢作為國王嗰樣窮,你就夠窮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你作為臣民像他作為國王那樣窮,你就夠窮了。

passages.original: What wouldst thou?
passages.vernacular: 你想要乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想要什麼?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Service.
passages.vernacular: 服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 服務。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Who wouldst thou serve?
passages.vernacular: 你想侍奉邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想侍奉誰?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: You.
passages.vernacular: 您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Dost thou know me, fellow?
passages.vernacular: 你認識我嗎,朋友?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認識我嗎,朋友?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: No, sir; but you have that in your countenance which I would fain call master.
passages.vernacular: 不認識,先生;但您臉上有一種我願稱為主人嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不認識,先生;但您臉上有一種我願稱為主人的東西。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What’s that?
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Authority.
passages.vernacular: 權威。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 權威。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What services canst thou do?
passages.vernacular: 你能做乜嘢服務?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能做什麼服務?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I can keep honest counsel, ride, run, mar a curious tale in telling it and deliver a plain message bluntly.
passages.vernacular: 我能保守誠實嘅祕密,騎馬,奔跑,把一個精巧嘅故事講砸,直率地轉達簡單嘅訊息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能保守誠實的祕密,騎馬,奔跑,把一個精巧的故事講砸,直率地轉達簡單的訊息。

passages.original: That which ordinary men are fit for, I am qualified in, and the best of me is diligence.
passages.vernacular: 凡是普通人所適合嘅,我都具備,而我最好嘅係勤勉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡是普通人所適合的,我都具備,而我最好的是勤勉。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How old art thou?
passages.vernacular: 你多大年紀?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你多大年紀?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Not so young, sir, to love a woman for singing;
passages.vernacular: 冇年輕到會因為女人唱歌就愛佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有年輕到會因為女人唱歌就愛她;

passages.original: nor so old to dote on her for anything: I have years on my back forty-eight.
passages.vernacular: 都冇老到會因任何原因溺愛佢:我背上有四十八年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也沒有老到會因任何原因溺愛她:我背上有四十八年。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Follow me; thou shalt serve me.
passages.vernacular: 跟住我;你要侍奉我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟著我;你要侍奉我。

passages.original: If I like thee no worse after dinner, I will not part from thee yet.
passages.vernacular: 如果晚餐後我對你嘅睇法冇變差,我暫時唔會讓你走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果晚餐後我對你的看法沒有變差,我暫時不會讓你走。

passages.original: Dinner, ho, dinner!
passages.vernacular: 晚餐,喂,晚餐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚餐,喂,晚餐!

passages.original: Where’s my knave? my fool?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅小子喺邊?我嘅弄臣呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的小子在哪?我的弄臣呢?

passages.original: Go you and call my fool hither.
passages.vernacular: 你去把我嘅弄臣叫嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去把我的弄臣叫來。

passages.original: [Exit an Attendant.]
passages.vernacular: [一名侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名侍從下。]

passages.original: Enter Oswald.
passages.vernacular: [奧斯華上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧斯華上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: You, you, sirrah, where’s my daughter?
passages.vernacular: 你,你,小子,我女兒喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,你,小子,我女兒在哪?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: So please you,—
passages.vernacular: 稟大人——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稟大人——

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What says the fellow there?
passages.vernacular: 嗰傢伙講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那傢伙說什麼?

passages.original: Call the clotpoll back.
passages.vernacular: 把嗰蠢貨叫回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把那蠢貨叫回來。

passages.original: [Exit a Knight.]
passages.vernacular: [一名騎士下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名騎士下。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Where’s my fool?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅弄臣喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的弄臣在哪?

passages.original: Ho, I think the world’s asleep.
passages.vernacular: 喂,我睇全世界都瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,我看全世界都睡著了。

passages.original: Re-enter Knight.
passages.vernacular: [騎士再上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [騎士再上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How now!
passages.vernacular: 點喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了!

passages.original: where’s that mongrel?
passages.vernacular: 嗰雜種喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那雜種在哪?

passages.title: Knight 騎士
passages.original: He says, my lord, your daughter is not well.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,大人,您女兒不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,大人,您女兒不舒服。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Why came not the slave back to me when I called him?
passages.vernacular: 我叫佢時,嗰奴才點解不回嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫他時,那奴才為什麼不回來?

passages.title: Knight 騎士
passages.original: Sir, he answered me in the roundest manner, he would not.
passages.vernacular: 先生,佢用最乾脆嘅方式回答我,佢唔肯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,他用最乾脆的方式回答我,他不肯。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: He would not?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔肯?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不肯?

passages.title: Knight 騎士
passages.original: My lord, I know not what the matter is; but to my judgement your highness is not entertained with that ceremonious affection as you were wont;
passages.vernacular: 大人,我唔知道係點回事;但依我判斷,陛下冇得到像從前嗰樣隆重嘅親愛招待;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我不知道是怎麼回事;但依我判斷,陛下沒有得到像從前那樣隆重的親愛招待;

passages.original: there’s a great abatement of kindness appears as well in the general dependants as in the Duke himself also, and your daughter.
passages.vernacular: 無論係一般嘅僕從,定係公爵本人,定係您嘅女兒,善意都明顯減少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論是一般的僕從,還是公爵本人,還是您的女兒,善意都明顯減少。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Ha!
passages.vernacular: 哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈!

passages.original: say’st thou so?
passages.vernacular: 你咁講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這麼說?

passages.title: Knight 騎士
passages.original: I beseech you pardon me, my lord, if I be mistaken;
passages.vernacular: 我懇求您原諒,大人,如果我弄錯喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求您原諒,大人,如果我弄錯了;

passages.original: for my duty cannot be silent when I think your highness wronged.
passages.vernacular: 因為當我認為陛下受咗冤屈,我嘅職責唔能夠沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為當我認為陛下受了冤屈,我的職責不能沉默。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Thou but rememberest me of mine own conception:
passages.vernacular: 你只係提醒咗我自己嘅想法:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只是提醒了我自己的想法:

passages.original: I have perceived a most faint neglect of late;
passages.vernacular: 我最近察覺到一種好微弱嘅怠慢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最近察覺到一種很微弱的怠慢;

passages.original: which I have rather blamed as mine own jealous curiosity than as a very pretence and purpose of unkindness:
passages.vernacular: 我寧願責怪係我自己多疑嘅好奇心,而唔係真有不友善嘅意圖同用心:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願責怪是我自己多疑的好奇心,而不是真有不友善的意圖和用心:

passages.original: I will look further into’t.
passages.vernacular: 我要進一步調查。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要進一步調查。

passages.original: But where’s my fool?
passages.vernacular: 但我嘅弄臣呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我的弄臣呢?

passages.original: I have not seen him this two days.
passages.vernacular: 兩天冇見到佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩天沒見到他了。

passages.title: Knight 騎士
passages.original: Since my young lady’s going into France, sir, the fool hath much pined away.
passages.vernacular: 自從我嘅小姐去咗法蘭西,先生,弄臣憔悴咗許多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我的小姐去了法蘭西,先生,弄臣憔悴了許多。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No more of that; I have noted it well.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再講呢個;我已經留意到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再說這個;我已經留意到了。

passages.original: Go you and tell my daughter I would speak with her.
passages.vernacular: 你去告訴我女兒我想同佢談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去告訴我女兒我想和她談話。

passages.original: [Exit Attendant.]
passages.vernacular: [一名侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名侍從下。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Go you, call hither my fool.
passages.vernacular: 你去,把我嘅弄臣叫嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去,把我的弄臣叫來。

passages.original: [Exit another Attendant.]
passages.vernacular: [另一名侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [另一名侍從下。]

passages.original: Re-enter Oswald.
passages.vernacular: [奧斯華再上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧斯華再上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O, you, sir, you, come you hither, sir: who am I, sir?
passages.vernacular: 啊,你,先生,你,過嚟,先生:我係邊個,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你,先生,你,過來,先生:我是誰,先生?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: My lady’s father.
passages.vernacular: 我家夫人嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我家夫人的父親。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: My lady’s father!
passages.vernacular: 我家夫人嘅父親!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我家夫人的父親!

passages.original: my lord’s knave: you whoreson dog! you slave! you cur!
