passages.vernacular: 我家大人嘅奴才:你呢雜種狗!你呢奴才!你呢惡犬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我家大人的奴才:你這雜種狗!你這奴才!你這惡犬!

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: I am none of these, my lord; I beseech your pardon.
passages.vernacular: 我都唔係,大人;懇求您原諒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我都不是,大人;懇求您原諒。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Do you bandy looks with me, you rascal?
passages.vernacular: 你敢跟我擠眉弄眼,你呢無賴?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你敢跟我擠眉弄眼,你這無賴?

passages.original: [Striking him.]
passages.vernacular: [打佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [打他。]

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: I’ll not be struck, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我不挨打,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不挨打,大人。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Nor tripp’d neither, you base football player.
passages.vernacular: 都不被絆倒,你呢卑賤嘅足球員。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不被絆倒,你這卑賤的足球員。

passages.original: [Tripping up his heels.]
passages.vernacular: [絆倒佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [絆倒他。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I thank thee, fellow.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝你,朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝你,朋友。

passages.original: Thou serv’st me, and I’ll love thee.
passages.vernacular: 你侍奉我,我會愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你侍奉我,我會愛你。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Come, sir, arise, away!
passages.vernacular: 嚟,先生,起嚟,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,先生,起來,走!

passages.original: I’ll teach you differences: away, away!
passages.vernacular: 我嚟教你分別:走,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來教你分別:走,走!

passages.original: If you will measure your lubber’s length again, tarry; but away!
passages.vernacular: 如果你想再量一量你笨重身軀嘅長度,就留下;但走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你想再量一量你笨重身軀的長度,就留下;但走!

passages.original: go to; have you wisdom? So.
passages.vernacular: 去吧;你有智慧嗎?咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧;你有智慧嗎?這樣。

passages.original: [Pushes Oswald out.]
passages.vernacular: [把奧斯華推出去。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把奧斯華推出去。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Now, my friendly knave, I thank thee: there’s earnest of thy service.
passages.vernacular: 而家,我友善嘅小子,謝謝你:呢個係你服務嘅定金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,我友善的小子,謝謝你:這是你服務的定金。

passages.original: [Giving Kent money.]
passages.vernacular: [畀肯特錢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [給肯特錢。]

passages.original: Enter Fool.
passages.vernacular: [弄臣上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [弄臣上。]

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Let me hire him too; here’s my coxcomb.
passages.vernacular: 讓我都雇用佢;呢個係我嘅雞冠帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我也雇用他;這是我的雞冠帽。

passages.original: [Giving Kent his cap.]
passages.vernacular: [畀肯特佢嘅帽子。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [給肯特他的帽子。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How now, my pretty knave, how dost thou?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,我可愛嘅小子,你好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,我可愛的小子,你好嗎?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Sirrah, you were best take my coxcomb.
passages.vernacular: 小子,你最好攞我嘅雞冠帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,你最好拿我的雞冠帽。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Why, fool?
passages.vernacular: 點解,弄臣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,弄臣?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Why, for taking one’s part that’s out of favour.
passages.vernacular: 點解,因為你幫咗一個失寵嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,因為你幫了一個失寵的人。

passages.original: Nay, an thou canst not smile as the wind sits, thou’lt catch cold shortly:
passages.vernacular: 不,如果你唔能夠順住風向微笑,你好快會住涼:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,如果你不能順著風向微笑,你很快會著涼:

passages.original: there, take my coxcomb: why, this fellow has banish’d two on’s daughters, and did the third a blessing against his will;
passages.vernacular: 嚟,攞我嘅雞冠帽:你睇,呢個人放逐咗佢兩個女兒,又違背自己嘅意願祝福咗第三個;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,拿我的雞冠帽:你看,這個人放逐了他兩個女兒,又違背自己的意願祝福了第三個;

passages.original: if thou follow him, thou must needs wear my coxcomb.
passages.vernacular: 如果你跟隨佢,你必須戴我嘅雞冠帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你跟隨他,你必須戴我的雞冠帽。

passages.original: How now, nuncle!
passages.vernacular: 點喇,叔叔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,叔叔!

passages.original: Would I had two coxcombs and two daughters!
passages.vernacular: 但願我有兩頂雞冠帽同兩個女兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願我有兩頂雞冠帽和兩個女兒!

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Why, my boy?
passages.vernacular: 點解,我嘅細路?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,我的孩子?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: If I gave them all my living, I’d keep my coxcombs myself.
passages.vernacular: 如果我把所有產業都畀咗佢哋,我自己仲留住雞冠帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我把所有產業都給了她們,我自己還留著雞冠帽。

passages.original: There’s mine; beg another of thy daughters.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅;向你嘅女兒再要一頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的;向你的女兒再要一頂。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Take heed, sirrah, the whip.
passages.vernacular: 小心,小子,鞭子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小心,小子,鞭子。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Truth’s a dog must to kennel; he must be whipped out, when the Lady Brach may stand by the fire and stink.
passages.vernacular: 真理係條狗,必須進狗窩;要被鞭子趕出去,而布拉奇夫人(母獵犬)卻可以站喺火爐邊發臭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真理是條狗,必須進狗窩;要被鞭子趕出去,而布拉奇夫人(母獵犬)卻可以站在火爐邊發臭。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: A pestilent gall to me!
passages.vernacular: 對我來講係害人嘅膽汁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說是害人的膽汁!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Sirrah, I’ll teach thee a speech.
passages.vernacular: 小子,我教你一段話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,我教你一段話。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Do.
passages.vernacular: 好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Mark it, nuncle: Have more than thou showest, Speak less than thou knowest, Lend less than thou owest, Ride more than thou goest, Learn more than thou trowest, Set less than thou throwest;
passages.vernacular: 留意,叔叔:擁有比你顯示嘅多,講得比你知道嘅少,借出比你欠嘅少,騎馬比走路多,學到比你相信嘅多,下注比你擲出嘅少;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意,叔叔:擁有比你顯示的多,說得比你知道的少,借出比你欠的少,騎馬比走路多,學到比你相信的多,下注比你擲出的少;

passages.original: Leave thy drink and thy whore, And keep in-a-door, And thou shalt have more Than two tens to a score.
passages.vernacular: 戒掉酒同娼妓,待喺家裡,你就會有更多,多過二十個十個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戒掉酒和娼妓,待在家裡,你就會有更多,多過二十個十個。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: This is nothing, fool.
passages.vernacular: 呢個冇乜嘢,弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這沒什麼,弄臣。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Then ’tis like the breath of an unfee’d lawyer, you gave me nothing for’t.
passages.vernacular: 咁就像冇收費嘅律師嘅話,你畀咗我冇乜嘢嘅報酬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼就像沒收費的律師的話,你給了我沒什麼的報酬。

passages.original: Can you make no use of nothing, nuncle?
passages.vernacular: 叔叔,你唔能夠利用冇乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叔叔,你不能利用沒什麼嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Why, no, boy; nothing can be made out of nothing.
passages.vernacular: 唔,唔能夠,細路;無中唔能夠生有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唔,不能,孩子;無中不能生有。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: [to Kent.]
passages.vernacular: [對肯特。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對肯特。]

passages.original: Prythee tell him, so much the rent of his land comes to:
passages.vernacular: 請你告訴佢,佢土地嘅租金就係咁多:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你告訴他,他土地的租金就是這麼多:

passages.original: he will not believe a fool.
passages.vernacular: 佢不相信弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不相信弄臣。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: A bitter fool.
passages.vernacular: 一個苦澀嘅弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個苦澀的弄臣。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Dost thou know the difference, my boy, between a bitter fool and a sweet one?
passages.vernacular: 細路,你知道苦澀弄臣同甜蜜弄臣嘅差別嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子,你知道苦澀弄臣和甜蜜弄臣的差別嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No, lad; teach me.
passages.vernacular: 唔知道,細路;教我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知道,孩子;教我。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: That lord that counsell’d thee To give away thy land, Come place him here by me, Do thou for him stand.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位勸你把土地送出去嘅大人,請把佢放喺呢度我旁邊,你嚟代替佢站:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位勸你把土地送出去的大人,請把他放在這裡我旁邊,你來代替他站:

passages.original: The sweet and bitter fool Will presently appear;
passages.vernacular: 甜弄臣同苦弄臣即刻就會顯現;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甜弄臣和苦弄臣馬上就會顯現;

passages.original: The one in motley here, The other found out there.
passages.vernacular: 一個穿雜色衣喺呢度,另一個喺嗰邊找到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個穿雜色衣在這裡,另一個在那邊找到。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Dost thou call me fool, boy?
passages.vernacular: 你叫我弄臣嗎,細路?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫我弄臣嗎,孩子?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: All thy other titles thou hast given away; that thou wast born with.
passages.vernacular: 你所有其他頭銜都送掉喇;呢個係你同生俱嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你所有其他頭銜都送掉了;這是你與生俱來的。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: This is not altogether fool, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 大人,呢並非全然係弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,這並非全然是弄臣。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: No, faith; lords and great men will not let me;
passages.vernacular: 不,講真嘅;大人同大人物不讓我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,說真的;大人和大人物不讓我;

passages.original: if I had a monopoly out, they would have part on’t and ladies too, they will not let me have all the fool to myself; they’ll be snatching.
passages.vernacular: 如果我有專利,佢哋都要分一份,貴婦哋都係,佢哋不讓我獨占全部愚蠢;佢哋會搶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我有專利,他們也要分一份,貴婦們也是,他們不讓我獨占全部愚蠢;他們會搶。

passages.original: Nuncle, give me an egg, and I’ll give thee two crowns.
passages.vernacular: 叔叔,畀我一個蛋,我畀你兩頂王冠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叔叔,給我一個蛋,我給你兩頂王冠。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What two crowns shall they be?
passages.vernacular: 會係邊兩頂王冠?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會是哪兩頂王冠?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Why, after I have cut the egg i’ the middle and eat up the meat, the two crowns of the egg.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,等我把蛋從中間切開食掉蛋肉後,蛋嘅兩頂王冠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,等我把蛋從中間切開吃掉蛋肉後,蛋的兩頂王冠。

passages.original: When thou clovest thy crown i’ the middle and gav’st away both parts, thou bor’st thine ass on thy back o’er the dirt:
passages.vernacular: 當你把你嘅王冠從中間劈開,把兩半都送人,你就係背住你嘅驢子過泥濘:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你把你的王冠從中間劈開,把兩半都送人,你就是背著你的驢子過泥濘:

passages.original: thou hadst little wit in thy bald crown when thou gav’st thy golden one away.
passages.vernacular: 你送出金王冠時,你禿頭裡嘅智慧好少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你送出金王冠時,你禿頭裡的智慧很少。

passages.original: If I speak like myself in this, let him be whipped that first finds it so. [Singing.]
passages.vernacular: 如果我喺呢點上講得像我自己,讓第一個發現如此嘅人被鞭打。[唱。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我在這點上說得像我自己,讓第一個發現如此的人被鞭打。[唱。]

passages.original: Fools had ne’er less grace in a year; For wise men are grown foppish, And know not how their wits to wear, Their manners are so apish.
passages.vernacular: 弄臣一年中從未咁不受恩惠;因為聰明人變得愚蠢,唔知道點樣運用佢哋嘅智慧,佢哋嘅舉止如此猴子般模仿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弄臣一年中從未這麼不受恩惠;因為聰明人變得愚蠢,不知道怎樣運用他們的智慧,他們的舉止如此猴子般模仿。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: When were you wont to be so full of songs, sirrah?
passages.vernacular: 小子,你乜嘢時候開始咁樣滿口歌喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,你什麼時候開始這樣滿口歌了?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: I have used it, nuncle, e’er since thou mad’st thy daughters thy mothers;
passages.vernacular: 叔叔,自從你把你女兒變成你母親起我就咁樣喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叔叔,自從你把你女兒變成你母親起我就這樣了;

passages.original: for when thou gav’st them the rod, and put’st down thine own breeches, [Singing.]
passages.vernacular: 因為當你把鞭子畀咗佢哋,自己脫下褲子,[唱。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為當你把鞭子給了她們,自己脫下褲子,[唱。]

passages.original: Then they for sudden joy did weep, And I for sorrow sung, That such a king should play bo-peep, And go the fools among.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋因突然嘅喜悅哭泣,我因悲傷而唱,咁樣一位國王玩捉迷藏,混喺弄臣中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們因突然的喜悅哭泣,我因悲傷而唱,這樣一位國王玩捉迷藏,混在弄臣中。

passages.original: Prythee, nuncle, keep a schoolmaster that can teach thy fool to lie;
passages.vernacular: 請你,叔叔,雇一位教書先生,能教你嘅弄臣講謊;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,叔叔,雇一位教書先生,能教你的弄臣說謊;

passages.original: I would fain learn to lie.
passages.vernacular: 我好想學講謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很想學說謊。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: An you lie, sirrah, we’ll have you whipped.
passages.vernacular: 如果你講謊,小子,我哋會鞭打你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你說謊,小子,我們會鞭打你。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: I marvel what kin thou and thy daughters are:
passages.vernacular: 我奇怪你同你女兒係乜嘢親戚:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我奇怪你和你女兒是什麼親戚:

passages.original: they’ll have me whipped for speaking true; thou’lt have me whipped for lying;
passages.vernacular: 佢哋為我講真話要鞭打我;你為我講謊要鞭打我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們為我說真話要鞭打我;你為我說謊要鞭打我;

passages.original: and sometimes I am whipped for holding my peace.
passages.vernacular: 有時我保持沉默都被鞭打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我保持沉默也被鞭打。

passages.original: I had rather be any kind o’thing than a fool:
passages.vernacular: 我寧願做任何嘢都不做弄臣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願做任何東西也不做弄臣:

passages.original: and yet I would not be thee, nuncle: thou hast pared thy wit o’both sides, and left nothing i’ the middle:
passages.vernacular: 然而我都唔願做你,叔叔:你把你嘅智慧兩邊都削掉,中間乜嘢都冇剩:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而我也不願做你,叔叔:你把你的智慧兩邊都削掉,中間什麼也沒剩:

passages.original: here comes one o’ the parings.
passages.vernacular: 呢度嚟咗一片削下嚟嘅邊角料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡來了一片削下來的邊角料。

passages.original: Enter Goneril.
passages.vernacular: [高納麗上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [高納麗上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How now, daughter?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,女兒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,女兒?

passages.original: What makes that frontlet on?
passages.vernacular: 你點解戴住嗰塊額帶?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼戴著那塊額帶?

passages.original: Methinks you are too much of late i’ the frown.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得你最近皺眉太多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得你最近皺眉太多了。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Thou wast a pretty fellow when thou hadst no need to care for her frowning.
passages.vernacular: 你以前係個可愛嘅傢伙,嗰時你唔使在意佢嘅皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以前是個可愛的傢伙,那時你不必在意她的皺眉。

passages.original: Now thou art an O without a figure: I am better than thou art now.
passages.vernacular: 而家你係個冇數字嘅零:我比你而家強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你是個沒有數字的零:我比你現在強。

passages.original: I am a fool, thou art nothing.
passages.vernacular: 我係弄臣,你乜嘢都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是弄臣,你什麼都不是。

passages.original: [To Goneril.]
passages.vernacular: [對高納麗。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對高納麗。]

passages.original: Yes, forsooth, I will hold my tongue.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,真嘅,我會閉嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,真的,我會閉嘴。

passages.original: So your face bids me, though you say nothing.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅臉咁樣命令我,雖然你乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的臉這樣命令我,雖然你什麼都沒說。

passages.original: Mum, mum, He that keeps nor crust nor crum, Weary of all, shall want some.
passages.vernacular: 噓,噓,不留麵包皮都不留碎屑嘅人,對一切厭倦後,會缺少啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 噓,噓,不留麵包皮也不留碎屑的人,對一切厭倦後,會缺少一些。

passages.original: [Pointing to Lear.]
passages.vernacular: [指住李爾。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [指著李爾。]

passages.original: That’s a shealed peascod.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一顆剝咗殼嘅豌豆莢(空殼)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一顆剝了殼的豌豆莢(空殼)。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Not only, sir, this your all-licens’d fool, But other of your insolent retinue Do hourly carp and quarrel;
passages.vernacular: 不只係,先生,您呢位被一切許可嘅弄臣,仲有您其他傲慢嘅隨從,每小時都喺挑剔爭吵;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不只是,先生,您這位被一切許可的弄臣,還有您其他傲慢的隨從,每小時都在挑剔爭吵;

passages.original: breaking forth In rank and not-to-be-endured riots.
passages.vernacular: 爆發出惡劣而不可忍受嘅喧鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爆發出惡劣而不可忍受的喧鬧。

passages.original: Sir, I had thought, by making this well known unto you, To have found a safe redress;
passages.vernacular: 先生,我原以為把呢事讓您知道,就能找到安全嘅補救;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我原以為把這事讓您知道,就能找到安全的補救;

passages.original: but now grow fearful, By what yourself too late have spoke and done, That you protect this course, and put it on By your allowance;
passages.vernacular: 但而家擔心起嚟,由您自己最近所講所做嘅,您喺庇護呢種行為,並以您嘅許可助長佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在擔心起來,由您自己最近所說所做的,您在庇護這種行為,並以您的許可助長它;

passages.original: which if you should, the fault Would not scape censure, nor the redresses sleep, Which, in the tender of a wholesome weal, Might in their working do you that offence Which else were shame, that then necessity Will call discreet proceeding.
passages.vernacular: 如果您咁樣,呢個過錯就逃不過責難,補救都唔會沉瞓,呢啲補救喺對健全福祉嘅關懷下,運作時或者會對您造成冒犯,否則嗰個係羞恥,但嗰時必要性會稱之為審慎嘅行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您這樣,這個過錯就逃不過責難,補救也不會沉睡,這些補救在對健全福祉的關懷下,運作時也許會對您造成冒犯,否則那是羞恥,但那時必要性會稱之為審慎的行動。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: For you know, nuncle, The hedge-sparrow fed the cuckoo so long That it’s had it head bit off by it young.
passages.vernacular: 因為你知道,叔叔,籬雀餵杜鵑太久,結果自己嘅頭被幼鳥咬掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你知道,叔叔,籬雀餵杜鵑太久,結果自己的頭被幼鳥咬掉。

passages.original: So out went the candle, and we were left darkling.
passages.vernacular: 於是蠟燭熄滅喇,我哋留喺黑暗中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是蠟燭熄滅了,我們留在黑暗中。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Are you our daughter?
passages.vernacular: 你係我哋嘅女兒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是我們的女兒嗎?

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Come, sir, I would you would make use of that good wisdom, Whereof I know you are fraught;
passages.vernacular: 嚟,先生,我希望您運用您嗰良好嘅智慧,我知道您充滿智慧;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,先生,我希望您運用您那良好的智慧,我知道您充滿智慧;

passages.original: and put away These dispositions, which of late transform you From what you rightly are.
passages.vernacular: 並拋開呢啲近來使您變得不像您本來面目的脾性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並拋開這些近來使您變得不像您本來面目的脾性。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: May not an ass know when the cart draws the horse? Whoop, Jug!
passages.vernacular: 驢子難道唔知道乜嘢時候車拉住馬嗎?嗬,嘰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 驢子難道不知道什麼時候車拉著馬嗎?嗬,嘰!

passages.original: I love thee!
passages.vernacular: 我愛你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛你!

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Doth any here know me?
passages.vernacular: 呢度有人認識我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有人認識我嗎?

passages.original: This is not Lear; Doth Lear walk thus? speak thus?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係李爾;李爾咁樣走路?咁樣講話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是李爾;李爾這樣走路?這樣說話?

passages.original: Where are his eyes?
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛在哪?

passages.original: Either his notion weakens, his discernings Are lethargied. Ha! waking?
passages.vernacular: 要麼佢嘅認知衰弱喇,佢嘅辨別力昏沉喇。哈!醒住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼他的認知衰弱了,他的辨別力昏沉了。哈!醒著?

passages.original: ’Tis not so!
passages.vernacular: 唔係咁樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是這樣!

passages.original: Who is it that can tell me who I am?
passages.vernacular: 邊個能告訴我我係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰能告訴我我是誰?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Lear’s shadow.
passages.vernacular: 李爾嘅影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 李爾的影子。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I would learn that; for by the marks of sovereignty, knowledge and reason, I should be false persuaded I had daughters.
passages.vernacular: 我想知道呢個;因為憑王權嘅標記、知識同理智,我會被錯誤地講服,以為我有女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想知道這個;因為憑王權的標記、知識和理智,我會被錯誤地說服,以為我有女兒。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Which they will make an obedient father.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋會使佢成為一個順從嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們會使他成為一個順從的父親。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Your name, fair gentlewoman?
passages.vernacular: 您嘅名字,美麗嘅夫人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您的名字,美麗的夫人?

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: This admiration, sir, is much o’ the favour Of other your new pranks.
passages.vernacular: 呢種驚訝,先生,好像您其他新鬧劇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種驚訝,先生,很像您其他新鬧劇。

passages.original: I do beseech you To understand my purposes aright:
passages.vernacular: 我懇求您正確理解我嘅用意:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求您正確理解我的用意:

passages.original: As you are old and reverend, you should be wise.
passages.vernacular: 您年老受尊敬,應當明智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您年老受尊敬,應當明智。

passages.original: Here do you keep a hundred knights and squires;
passages.vernacular: 您喺呢度養住一百名騎士同侍從;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您在這裡養著一百名騎士和侍從;

passages.original: Men so disorder’d, so debosh’d and bold That this our court, infected with their manners, Shows like a riotous inn.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲人如此放縱、墮落、大膽,以致我哋呢座宮廷被佢哋嘅習氣感染,睇起嚟像一家喧鬧嘅客棧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些人如此放縱、墮落、大膽,以致我們這座宮廷被他們的習氣感染,看起來像一家喧鬧的客棧。

passages.original: Epicurism and lust Makes it more like a tavern or a brothel Than a grac’d palace.
passages.vernacular: 享樂同淫慾使佢更像酒館或妓院,而唔係優雅嘅宮殿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 享樂與淫慾使它更像酒館或妓院,而不是優雅的宮殿。

passages.original: The shame itself doth speak For instant remedy.
passages.vernacular: 呢恥辱本身喺呼喊立即補救。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這恥辱本身在呼喊立即補救。

passages.original: Be, then, desir’d By her that else will take the thing she begs A little to disquantity your train;
passages.vernacular: 所以,請求您,佢若不請求就會直接動手:稍微減少您嘅隨從;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,請求您,她若不請求就會直接動手:稍微減少您的隨從;

passages.original: And the remainder that shall still depend, To be such men as may besort your age, Which know themselves, and you.
passages.vernacular: 而留下仍然依靠我哋嘅人,要適合您年紀嘅人,懂得自己都懂得您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而留下仍然依靠我們的人,要適合您年紀的人,懂得自己也懂得您。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Darkness and devils!
passages.vernacular: 黑暗同魔鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑暗與魔鬼!

passages.original: Saddle my horses; call my train together.
passages.vernacular: 畀我嘅即刻鞍;把我嘅隨從召集起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我的馬上鞍;把我的隨從召集起來。

passages.original: Degenerate bastard!
passages.vernacular: 墮落嘅私生女!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 墮落的私生女!

passages.original: I’ll not trouble thee: Yet have I left a daughter.
passages.vernacular: 我不麻煩你:我仲有一個女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不麻煩你:我還有一個女兒。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: You strike my people; and your disorder’d rabble Make servants of their betters.
passages.vernacular: 你打我嘅人;你嗰無秩序嘅烏合之眾把僕人變成佢哋上司嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你打我的人;你那無秩序的烏合之眾把僕人變成他們上司的主人。

passages.original: Enter Albany.
passages.vernacular: [奧本尼上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧本尼上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Woe that too late repents!— [To Albany.]
passages.vernacular: 悔得太遲嘅人有禍喇!——[對奧本尼。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 悔得太遲的人有禍了!——[對奧本尼。]

passages.original: O, sir, are you come?
passages.vernacular: 啊,先生,你嚟喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,先生,你來了?

passages.original: Is it your will?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係你嘅意思嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是你的意思嗎?

passages.original: Speak, sir.—Prepare my horses.
passages.vernacular: 講,先生。——準備我嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說,先生。——準備我的馬。

passages.original: Ingratitude, thou marble-hearted fiend, More hideous when thou show’st thee in a child Than the sea-monster!
passages.vernacular: 忘恩負義,你呢鐵石心腸嘅魔鬼,出而家細路身上時,比海怪更可怕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 忘恩負義,你這鐵石心腸的魔鬼,出現在孩子身上時,比海怪更可怕!

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Pray, sir, be patient.
passages.vernacular: 請您,先生,耐心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請您,先生,耐心。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: [to Goneril.]
passages.vernacular: [對高納麗。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對高納麗。]

passages.original: Detested kite, thou liest.
passages.vernacular: 可憎嘅鳶,你講謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憎的鳶,你說謊。

passages.original: My train are men of choice and rarest parts, That all particulars of duty know;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅隨從係經過挑選、才能罕見嘅人,通曉一切職責細節;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的隨從是經過挑選、才能罕見的人,通曉一切職責細節;

passages.original: And in the most exact regard support The worships of their name.
passages.vernacular: 並以最嚴謹嘅態度維護佢哋名號嘅尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並以最嚴謹的態度維護他們名號的尊嚴。

passages.original: O most small fault, How ugly didst thou in Cordelia show!
passages.vernacular: 啊,最小嘅過錯,你喺考黛莉亞身上顯得多醜陋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,最小的過錯,你在考黛莉亞身上顯得多醜陋!

passages.original: Which, like an engine, wrench’d my frame of nature From the fix’d place;
passages.vernacular: 佢像一部機器,把我天性嘅框架從固定嘅位置撬開;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它像一部機器,把我天性的框架從固定的位置撬開;

passages.original: drew from my heart all love, And added to the gall.
passages.vernacular: 從我心裡抽走所有嘅愛,並增添咗苦膽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我心裡抽走所有的愛,並增添了苦膽。

passages.original: O Lear, Lear, Lear!
passages.vernacular: 啊李爾,李爾,李爾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊李爾,李爾,李爾!

passages.original: [Striking his head.]
passages.vernacular: [敲自己嘅頭。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [敲自己的頭。]

passages.original: Beat at this gate that let thy folly in And thy dear judgement out!
passages.vernacular: 敲呢扇讓你嘅愚蠢進嚟、讓你寶貴嘅判斷出去嘅門吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 敲這扇讓你的愚蠢進來、讓你寶貴的判斷出去的門吧!

passages.original: Go, go, my people.
passages.vernacular: 走,走,我嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走,走,我的人。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: My lord, I am guiltless, as I am ignorant Of what hath moved you.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我係無辜嘅,正如我唔知道係乜嘢觸動咗您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我是無辜的,正如我不知道是什麼觸動了您。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: It may be so, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 或者係咁樣,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許是這樣,大人。

passages.original: Hear, nature, hear; dear goddess, hear!
passages.vernacular: 聽,自然,聽;親愛嘅女神,聽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽,自然,聽;親愛的女神,聽!

passages.original: Suspend thy purpose, if thou didst intend To make this creature fruitful!
passages.vernacular: 如果你曾打算使呢個生物生育,就中止你嘅意圖!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你曾打算使這個生物生育,就中止你的意圖!

passages.original: Into her womb convey sterility!
passages.vernacular: 把不孕送進佢嘅子宮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把不孕送進她的子宮!

passages.original: Dry up in her the organs of increase; And from her derogate body never spring A babe to honour her!
passages.vernacular: 喺佢身上枯竭生育嘅器官;從佢墮落嘅身體永遠唔好生出能使佢榮耀嘅嬰兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她身上枯竭生育的器官;從她墮落的身體永遠不要生出能使她榮耀的嬰兒!

passages.original: If she must teem, Create her child of spleen, that it may live And be a thwart disnatur’d torment to her!
passages.vernacular: 如果佢必須生育,就用怨恨造佢嘅細路,使佢活住成為佢乖戾、違反天性嘅折磨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她必須生育,就用怨恨造她的孩子,使他活著成為她乖戾、違反天性的折磨!

passages.original: Let it stamp wrinkles in her brow of youth; With cadent tears fret channels in her cheeks;
passages.vernacular: 讓佢喺佢年輕嘅額頭刻下皺紋;用滴落嘅眼淚喺佢臉頰磨出溝渠;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他在她年輕的額頭刻下皺紋;用滴落的眼淚在她臉頰磨出溝渠;

passages.original: Turn all her mother’s pains and benefits To laughter and contempt;
passages.vernacular: 把佢做母親嘅一切痛苦同恩惠,變成嘲笑同輕蔑;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把她做母親的一切痛苦和恩惠,變成嘲笑和輕蔑;

passages.original: that she may feel How sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is To have a thankless child! Away, away!
passages.vernacular: 讓佢感到有一個忘恩負義嘅細路,比蛇嘅牙齒更鋒利!走,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓她感到有一個忘恩負義的孩子,比蛇的牙齒更鋒利!走,走!

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Now, gods that we adore, whereof comes this?
passages.vernacular: 而家,我哋崇拜嘅諸神啊,呢個係從何而嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,我們崇拜的諸神啊,這是從何而來?

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Never afflict yourself to know more of it; But let his disposition have that scope That dotage gives it.
passages.vernacular: 唔好為了知道更多而折磨自己;讓佢嘅性情有老年昏聵所畀嘅範圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要為了知道更多而折磨自己;讓他的性情有老年昏聵所給的範圍。

passages.original: Re-enter Lear.
passages.vernacular: [李爾再上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾再上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What, fifty of my followers at a clap?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我嘅五十個隨從一下子就冇喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我的五十個隨從一下子就沒了?

passages.original: Within a fortnight?
passages.vernacular: 喺兩個星期內?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在兩個星期內?

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: What’s the matter, sir?
passages.vernacular: 點回事,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼回事,先生?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I’ll tell thee.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你。

passages.original: [To Goneril.]
passages.vernacular: [對高納麗。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對高納麗。]

passages.original: Life and death!
passages.vernacular: 生同死!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 生與死!

passages.original: I am asham’d That thou hast power to shake my manhood thus;
passages.vernacular: 我羞愧,你有力量咁樣動搖我嘅男子氣概;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我羞愧,你有力量這樣動搖我的男子氣概;

passages.original: That these hot tears, which break from me perforce, Should make thee worth them.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲被迫從我眼中迸出嘅熱淚,竟使你覺得值得得到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些被迫從我眼中迸出的熱淚,竟使你覺得值得得到。

passages.original: Blasts and fogs upon thee!
passages.vernacular: 暴風同霧氣降喺你身上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暴風和霧氣降在你身上!

passages.original: Th’untented woundings of a father’s curse Pierce every sense about thee!
passages.vernacular: 一個父親詛咒嘅無法包紮嘅創傷,刺穿你周身每一種感覺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個父親詛咒的無法包紮的創傷,刺穿你周身每一種感覺!

passages.original: Old fond eyes, Beweep this cause again, I’ll pluck ye out, And cast you with the waters that you lose To temper clay. Ha!
passages.vernacular: 愚蠢嘅老眼睛,再為呢件事哭,我就把你哋挖出嚟,同你哋流失嘅水一起扔去調泥。哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愚蠢的老眼睛,再為這件事哭,我就把你們挖出來,和你們流失的水一起扔去調泥。哈!

passages.original: Let it be so.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣吧。

passages.original: I have another daughter, Who, I am sure, is kind and comfortable:
passages.vernacular: 我仲有另一個女兒,我確信佢善良、令人安慰:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還有另一個女兒,我確信她善良、令人安慰:

passages.original: When she shall hear this of thee, with her nails She’ll flay thy wolvish visage.
passages.vernacular: 當佢聽到你咁樣,佢會用指甲剝下你狼一般嘅面皮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她聽到你這樣,她會用指甲剝下你狼一般的面皮。

passages.original: Thou shalt find That I’ll resume the shape which thou dost think I have cast off for ever.
passages.vernacular: 你會發現我將恢復你以為我永遠丟棄嘅形象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會發現我將恢復你以為我永遠丟棄的形象。

passages.original: [Exeunt Lear, Kent and Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [李爾、肯特同侍從哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾、肯特和侍從們下。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Do you mark that?
passages.vernacular: 你注意到嗰個咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你注意到那個了嗎?

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: I cannot be so partial, Goneril, To the great love I bear you,—
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠偏袒到,高納麗,因我對你嘅深愛——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能偏袒到,高納麗,因我對你的深愛——

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Pray you, content.
passages.vernacular: 請你,安心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,安心。

passages.original: What, Oswald, ho!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,奧斯華,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,奧斯華,喂!

passages.original: [To the Fool.]
passages.vernacular: [對弄臣。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對弄臣。]

passages.original: You, sir, more knave than fool, after your master.
passages.vernacular: 你,先生,同其講係弄臣不如講係惡棍,跟住你嘅主人去吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,先生,與其說是弄臣不如說是惡棍,跟著你的主人去吧。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Nuncle Lear, nuncle Lear, tarry and take the fool with thee.
passages.vernacular: 叔叔李爾,叔叔李爾,等等,把弄臣帶上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叔叔李爾,叔叔李爾,等等,把弄臣帶上。

passages.original: A fox when one has caught her, And such a daughter, Should sure to the slaughter, If my cap would buy a halter;
passages.vernacular: 捉到一隻狐狸,仲有咁樣一個女兒,應當送去屠宰,如果我嘅帽子能買一條絞索;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 捉到一隻狐狸,還有這樣一個女兒,應當送去屠宰,如果我的帽子能買一條絞索;

passages.original: So the fool follows after.
passages.vernacular: 於是弄臣跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是弄臣跟在後面。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: This man hath had good counsel.—A hundred knights!
passages.vernacular: 呢人有好顧問。——一百名騎士!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這人有好顧問。——一百名騎士!

passages.original: ’Tis politic and safe to let him keep At point a hundred knights:
passages.vernacular: 讓佢保留一百名隨時待命嘅騎士,既審慎又安全:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他保留一百名隨時待命的騎士,既審慎又安全:

passages.original: yes, that on every dream, Each buzz, each fancy, each complaint, dislike, He may enguard his dotage with their powers, And hold our lives in mercy.
passages.vernacular: 係啊,每當佢做夢、聽到嗡嗡聲、突發奇想、抱怨、不滿時,佢都可以用佢哋嘅力量護衛佢嘅昏聵,把我哋嘅性命捏喺佢手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,每當他做夢、聽到嗡嗡聲、突發奇想、抱怨、不滿時,他都可以用他們的力量護衛他的昏聵,把我們的性命捏在他手裡。

passages.original: Oswald, I say!
passages.vernacular: 奧斯華,我講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧斯華,我說!

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Well, you may fear too far.
passages.vernacular: 好,你可能擔心得太過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你可能擔心得太過。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Safer than trust too far: Let me still take away the harms I fear, Not fear still to be taken: I know his heart.
passages.vernacular: 比太過信任更安全:讓我始終消除我擔心嘅禍害,而唔係始終擔心被佢抓住:我了解佢嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比太過信任更安全:讓我始終消除我擔心的禍害,而不是始終擔心被它抓住:我了解他的心。

passages.original: What he hath utter’d I have writ my sister: If she sustain him and his hundred knights, When I have show’d th’unfitness,—
passages.vernacular: 佢講過嘅話我都寫信告訴咗我妹妹:如果佢供養佢同佢嘅一百名騎士,當我表明了不合適——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說過的話我都寫信告訴了我妹妹:如果她供養他和他的一百名騎士,當我表明了不合適——

passages.original: Re-enter Oswald.
passages.vernacular: [奧斯華再上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧斯華再上。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: How now, Oswald!
passages.vernacular: 點樣,奧斯華!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣,奧斯華!

passages.original: What, have you writ that letter to my sister?
passages.vernacular: 點,你把嗰封信寫畀我妹妹咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,你把那封信寫給我妹妹了嗎?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Ay, madam.
passages.vernacular: 係,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,夫人。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Take you some company, and away to horse: Inform her full of my particular fear;
passages.vernacular: 帶些人,上馬去:把我個人嘅擔憂全告訴佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶些人,上馬去:把我個人的擔憂全告訴她;

passages.original: And thereto add such reasons of your own As may compact it more.
passages.vernacular: 並加上你自己嘅啲理由,使佢更有分量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並加上你自己的一些理由,使它更有分量。

passages.original: Get you gone; And hasten your return.
passages.vernacular: 去吧;快去快回。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧;快去快回。

passages.original: [Exit Oswald.]
passages.vernacular: [奧斯華下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧斯華下。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: No, no, my lord!
passages.vernacular: 不,不,大人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不,大人!

passages.original: This milky gentleness and course of yours, Though I condemn not, yet, under pardon, You are much more attask’d for want of wisdom Than prais’d for harmful mildness.
passages.vernacular: 您呢種乳白般嘅溫和同作風,雖然我不譴責,但恕我直言,您因缺乏智慧受到嘅責備,比因有害嘅溫和受到嘅稱讚更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您這種乳白般的溫和和作風,雖然我不譴責,但恕我直言,您因缺乏智慧受到的責備,比因有害的溫和受到的稱讚更多。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: How far your eyes may pierce I cannot tell: Striving to better, oft we mar what’s well.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅眼睛能睇多遠我唔知道:我哋努力求好,往往毀掉咗本來好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的眼睛能看多遠我不知道:我們努力求好,往往毀掉了本來好的。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Nay then,—
passages.vernacular: 不,咁——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,那麼——

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Well, well; the event.
passages.vernacular: 好,好;睇結果吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,好;看結果吧。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene V — Court before Albany’s Palace 第一幕第五場:奧本尼宮殿前庭

passages.original: Enter Lear, Kent and Fool.
passages.vernacular: [李爾、肯特同弄臣上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾、肯特和弄臣上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Go you before to Gloucester with these letters:
passages.vernacular: 你先帶呢啲信去葛羅斯特:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你先帶這些信去葛羅斯特:

passages.original: acquaint my daughter no further with anything you know than comes from her demand out of the letter.
passages.vernacular: 除咗佢睇信後問起嘅,唔好再向我女兒透露你所知道嘅任何事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了她看信後問起的,不要再向我女兒透露你所知道的任何事。

passages.original: If your diligence be not speedy, I shall be there afore you.
passages.vernacular: 如果你唔夠勤快,我會比你先到嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你不夠勤快,我會比你先到那裡。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I will not sleep, my lord, till I have delivered your letter.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我不瞓覺,直到把您嘅信送到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我不睡覺,直到把您的信送到。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: If a man’s brains were in’s heels, were’t not in danger of kibes?
passages.vernacular: 如果一個人嘅腦子長喺腳跟上,唔係有生凍瘡嘅危險嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果一個人的腦子長在腳跟上,不是有生凍瘡的危險嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Ay, boy.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,孩子。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Then I prythee be merry; thy wit shall not go slipshod.
passages.vernacular: 咁請你開心點;你嘅智慧唔會穿住拖鞋走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼請你開心點;你的智慧不會穿著拖鞋走路。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Ha, ha, ha!
passages.vernacular: 哈,哈,哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈,哈,哈!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Shalt see thy other daughter will use thee kindly, for though she’s as like this as a crab’s like an apple, yet I can tell what I can tell.
passages.vernacular: 你會睇到你另一個女兒待你好,因為雖然佢同呢個像沙果同蘋果嗰樣相像,我定係知道我知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會看到你另一個女兒待你好,因為雖然她和這個像沙果和蘋果那樣相像,我還是知道我知道的。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What canst tell, boy?
passages.vernacular: 你知道乜嘢,細路?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道什麼,孩子?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: She’ll taste as like this as a crab does to a crab.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚐起嚟像呢個,就像沙果嚐起嚟像沙果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她嚐起來像這個,就像沙果嚐起來像沙果。

passages.original: Thou canst tell why one’s nose stands i’the middle on’s face?
passages.vernacular: 你能講點解人嘅鼻子長喺臉嘅中間嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能說為什麼人的鼻子長在臉的中間嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No.
passages.vernacular: 唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不能。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Why, to keep one’s eyes of either side’s nose, that what a man cannot smell out, he may spy into.
passages.vernacular: 為了讓人嘅眼睛分居鼻子兩邊,咁樣一個人聞不出嘅,佢可以窺睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了讓人的眼睛分居鼻子兩邊,這樣一個人聞不出的,他可以窺看。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I did her wrong.
passages.vernacular: 我冤枉咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我冤枉了她。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Canst tell how an oyster makes his shell?
passages.vernacular: 你能講牡蠣點樣造佢嘅殼嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能說牡蠣怎樣造它的殼嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No.
passages.vernacular: 唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不能。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Nor I neither; but I can tell why a snail has a house.
passages.vernacular: 我都唔能夠;但我能講蝸牛點解有房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不能;但我能說蝸牛為什麼有房子。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Why?
passages.vernacular: 點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Why, to put’s head in; not to give it away to his daughters, and leave his horns without a case.
passages.vernacular: 為了把頭放進去;而唔係把房子送畀佢嘅女兒哋,讓自己嘅角冇套子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了把頭放進去;而不是把房子送給他的女兒們,讓自己的角沒有套子。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I will forget my nature.
passages.vernacular: 我要忘掉我嘅天性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要忘掉我的天性。

passages.original: So kind a father!
passages.vernacular: 咁慈愛嘅父親!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼慈愛的父親!

passages.original: Be my horses ready?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅馬準備好咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的馬準備好了嗎?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Thy asses are gone about ’em.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅驢子哋去準備喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的驢子們去準備了。

passages.original: The reason why the seven stars are no more than seven is a pretty reason.
passages.vernacular: 七星不多不少只有七顆,原因好可愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七星不多不少只有七顆,原因很可愛。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Because they are not eight?
passages.vernacular: 因為佢哋唔係八顆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為它們不是八顆?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Yes indeed: thou wouldst make a good fool.
passages.vernacular: 對,確實:你可以做個好弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,確實:你可以做個好弄臣。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: To tak’t again perforce!—Monster ingratitude!
passages.vernacular: 要強行奪回佢!——可怕嘅忘恩負義!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要強行奪回它!——可怕的忘恩負義!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: If thou wert my fool, nuncle, I’d have thee beaten for being old before thy time.
passages.vernacular: 如果你係我嘅弄臣,叔叔,我會因為你未老先衰而打你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你是我的弄臣,叔叔,我會因為你未老先衰而打你。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How’s that?
passages.vernacular: 點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼說?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Thou shouldst not have been old till thou hadst been wise.
passages.vernacular: 你冇變聰明之前,不該變老。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒變聰明之前,不該變老。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O, let me not be mad, not mad, sweet heaven!
passages.vernacular: 啊,唔好畀我發瘋,別發瘋,仁慈嘅上天!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,別讓我發瘋,別發瘋,仁慈的上天!

passages.original: Keep me in temper; I would not be mad!
passages.vernacular: 讓我保持理智;我唔想發瘋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我保持理智;我不想發瘋!

passages.original: Enter Gentleman.
passages.vernacular: [紳士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [紳士上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: How now?
passages.vernacular: 點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣?

passages.original: are the horses ready?
passages.vernacular: 馬準備好咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬準備好了嗎?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: Ready, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 準備好喇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 準備好了,大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Come, boy.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,孩子。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: She that’s a maid now, and laughs at my departure, Shall not be a maid long, unless things be cut shorter.
passages.vernacular: 嗰而家定係處女、嘲笑我離開嘅人,除非事情被縮短,佢唔會當好久嘅處女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那現在還是處女、嘲笑我離開的人,除非事情被縮短,她不會當很久的處女。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene I — A Court within Gloucester’s Castle 第二幕第一場:葛羅斯特城堡庭院

passages.original: Enter Edmund and Curan, meeting.
passages.vernacular: [愛德蒙同柯蘭相遇上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德蒙和柯蘭相遇上。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Save thee, Curan.
passages.vernacular: 向你問好,柯蘭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向你問好,柯蘭。

passages.title: Curan 柯蘭
passages.original: And you, sir.
passages.vernacular: 都向您,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也向您,先生。

passages.original: I have been with your father, and given him notice that the Duke of Cornwall and Regan his Duchess will be here with him this night.
passages.vernacular: 我去過您父親嗰度,告訴佢康華爾公爵同佢嘅公爵夫人里根今晚會嚟佢嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去過您父親那裡,告訴他康華爾公爵和他的公爵夫人里根今晚會來他那兒。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: How comes that?
passages.vernacular: 點會咁樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼會這樣?

passages.title: Curan 柯蘭
passages.original: Nay, I know not.
passages.vernacular: 不,我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我不知道。

passages.original: You have heard of the news abroad; I mean the whispered ones, for they are yet but ear-kissing arguments?
passages.vernacular: 您聽講外面嘅消息咗嗎?我係指悄悄傳嘅,因為佢哋仲只係耳邊親吻嘅議論?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您聽說外面的消息了嗎?我是指悄悄傳的,因為它們還只是耳邊親吻的議論?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Not I: pray you, what are they?
passages.vernacular: 我冇:請問,係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有:請問,是什麼?

passages.title: Curan 柯蘭
passages.original: Have you heard of no likely wars toward, ’twixt the two dukes of Cornwall and Albany?
passages.vernacular: 您冇聽講康華爾同奧本尼兩位公爵之間可能有戰爭嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您沒聽說康華爾和奧本尼兩位公爵之間可能有戰爭嗎?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Not a word.
passages.vernacular: 一個字都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個字也沒有。

passages.title: Curan 柯蘭
passages.original: You may do, then, in time.
passages.vernacular: 嗰您遲早會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那您遲早會的。

passages.original: Fare you well, sir.
passages.vernacular: 再見,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,先生。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: The Duke be here tonight? The better! best!
passages.vernacular: 公爵今晚喺呢度?更好!最好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵今晚在這裡?更好!最好!

passages.original: This weaves itself perforce into my business.
passages.vernacular: 呢自然而然地織進咗我嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這自然而然地織進了我的事。

passages.original: My father hath set guard to take my brother; And I have one thing, of a queasy question, Which I must act.
passages.vernacular: 我父親派咗守衛抓我哥哥;而我有一件棘手嘅事必須行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親派了守衛抓我哥哥;而我有一件棘手的事必須行動。

passages.original: Briefness and fortune work!
passages.vernacular: 願簡潔同好運起作用!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願簡潔與好運起作用!

passages.original: Brother, a word, descend, brother, I say!
passages.vernacular: 哥哥,講句話,下嚟,哥哥,我講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哥哥,說句話,下來,哥哥,我說!

passages.original: Enter Edgar.
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽上。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: My father watches: O sir, fly this place; Intelligence is given where you are hid;
passages.vernacular: 我父親喺監視:啊先生,逃離呢度;有人報告咗您藏身嘅地方;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親在監視:啊先生,逃離這裡;有人報告了您藏身的地方;

passages.original: You have now the good advantage of the night.
passages.vernacular: 您而家有夜晚嘅好條件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您現在有夜晚的好條件。

passages.original: Have you not spoken ’gainst the Duke of Cornwall?
passages.vernacular: 您冇講過反對康華爾公爵嘅話吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您沒說過反對康華爾公爵的話吧?

passages.original: He’s coming hither; now, i’ the night, i’ the haste, And Regan with him:
passages.vernacular: 佢正在嚟呢度;而家,喺夜裡,匆匆趕嚟,里根跟佢喺一起:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他正在來這裡;現在,在夜裡,匆匆趕來,里根跟他在一起:

passages.original: have you nothing said Upon his party ’gainst the Duke of Albany?
passages.vernacular: 您有冇喺佢嘅立場上講過反對奧本尼公爵嘅話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有沒有在他的立場上說過反對奧本尼公爵的話?

passages.original: Advise yourself.
passages.vernacular: 好好想想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好好想想。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: I am sure on’t, not a word.
passages.vernacular: 我確定,一個字都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確定,一個字也沒有。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I hear my father coming:—pardon me; In cunning I must draw my sword upon you:
passages.vernacular: 我聽到我父親嚟喇:——原諒我;我為了做戲必須向您拔劍:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到我父親來了:——原諒我;我為了做戲必須向您拔劍:

passages.original: Draw: seem to defend yourself: now quit you well.
passages.vernacular: 拔劍:裝作自衛:而家好好脫身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔劍:裝作自衛:現在好好脫身。

passages.original: Yield: come before my father.
passages.vernacular: 投降:嚟到我父親面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 投降:來到我父親面前。

passages.original: Light, ho, here!
passages.vernacular: 攞燈嚟,喂,呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿燈來,喂,這裡!

passages.original: Fly, brother.
passages.vernacular: 逃吧,哥哥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 逃吧,哥哥。

passages.original: Torches, torches!—So farewell.
passages.vernacular: 火把,火把!——再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火把,火把!——再見。

passages.original: [Exit Edgar.]
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽下。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Some blood drawn on me would beget opinion Of my more fierce endeavour: [Wounds his arm.]
passages.vernacular: 讓我身上流點血會增加人哋對我更激烈努力嘅睇法:[刺傷自己嘅手臂。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我身上流點血會增加人們對我更激烈努力的看法:[刺傷自己的手臂。]

passages.original: I have seen drunkards Do more than this in sport.
passages.vernacular: 我見過醉漢玩笑時做得比呢更過分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我見過醉漢玩笑時做得比這更過分。

passages.original: Father, father! Stop, stop! No help?
passages.vernacular: 父親,父親!住手,住手!冇人幫忙嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 父親,父親!住手,住手!沒人幫忙嗎?

passages.original: Enter Gloucester and Servants with torches.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特同持火把嘅僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特和持火把的僕人們上。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Now, Edmund, where’s the villain?
passages.vernacular: 而家,愛德蒙,惡棍喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,愛德蒙,惡棍在哪?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Here stood he in the dark, his sharp sword out, Mumbling of wicked charms, conjuring the moon To stand auspicious mistress.
passages.vernacular: 佢就站喺呢度嘅黑暗中,亮出利劍,喃喃念邪惡嘅咒語,召喚月亮作佢嘅吉祥女主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他就站在這裡的黑暗中,亮出利劍,喃喃念邪惡的咒語,召喚月亮作他的吉祥女主人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: But where is he?
passages.vernacular: 但佢喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他在哪?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Look, sir, I bleed.
passages.vernacular: 睇,先生,我流血喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,先生,我流血了。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Where is the villain, Edmund?
passages.vernacular: 惡棍喺邊,愛德蒙?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡棍在哪,愛德蒙?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Fled this way, sir.
passages.vernacular: 往呢邊逃喇,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 往這邊逃了,先生。

passages.original: When by no means he could,—
passages.vernacular: 當佢無論如何唔能夠——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他無論如何不能——

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Pursue him, ho! Go after.
passages.vernacular: 追佢,喂!去追。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 追他,喂!去追。

passages.original: [Exeunt Servants.]
passages.vernacular: [僕人哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [僕人們下。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: —By no means what?
passages.vernacular: ——無論如何唔能夠乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: ——無論如何不能什麼?

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Persuade me to the murder of your lordship; But that I told him the revenging gods ’Gainst parricides did all their thunders bend;
passages.vernacular: 講服我謀殺大人;不過我告訴佢,復仇嘅諸神對弒親者傾瀉所有嘅雷霆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說服我謀殺大人;可是我告訴他,復仇的諸神對弒親者傾瀉所有的雷霆;

passages.original: Spoke with how manifold and strong a bond The child was bound to the father;
passages.vernacular: 講明細路對父親有幾咁多重、幾咁強嘅紐帶;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說明孩子對父親有多麼多重、多麼強的紐帶;

passages.original: sir, in fine, Seeing how loathly opposite I stood To his unnatural purpose, in fell motion With his prepared sword, he charges home My unprovided body, latch’d mine arm;
passages.vernacular: 先生,最後,睇到我幾咁厭惡地反對佢不自然嘅企圖,佢猛烈地揮動準備好嘅劍,直攻我冇防備嘅身體,刺傷我嘅手臂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,最後,看到我多麼厭惡地反對他不自然的企圖,他猛烈地揮動準備好的劍,直攻我沒有防備的身體,刺傷我的手臂;

passages.original: But when he saw my best alarum’d spirits, Bold in the quarrel’s right, rous’d to th’encounter, Or whether gasted by the noise I made, Full suddenly he fled.
passages.vernacular: 但當佢睇到我最好嘅精神被警醒,喺正義嘅爭吵中大膽,被喚起迎戰,或者係被我發出嘅聲音嚇住,佢突然逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當他看到我最好的精神被警醒,在正義的爭吵中大膽,被喚起迎戰,或者是被我發出的聲音嚇住,他突然逃走。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Let him fly far; Not in this land shall he remain uncaught; And found—dispatch’d.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢逃得遠遠嘅;佢唔會喺呢片土地上不被抓住;一旦找到——處決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他逃得遠遠的;他不會在這片土地上不被抓住;一旦找到——處決。

passages.original: The noble Duke my master, My worthy arch and patron, comes tonight:
passages.vernacular: 高貴嘅公爵,我嘅主人,我可敬嘅大恩人,今晚嚟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高貴的公爵,我的主人,我可敬的大恩人,今晚來:

passages.original: By his authority I will proclaim it, That he which finds him shall deserve our thanks, Bringing the murderous coward to the stake;
passages.vernacular: 憑佢嘅權威我要宣布,找到佢嘅人將得到我哋嘅感謝,把呢個兇殘嘅懦夫送上刑柱;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑他的權威我要宣布,找到他的人將得到我們的感謝,把這個兇殘的懦夫送上刑柱;

passages.original: He that conceals him, death.
passages.vernacular: 窩藏佢嘅人,處死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窩藏他的人,處死。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: When I dissuaded him from his intent, And found him pight to do it, with curst speech I threaten’d to discover him:
passages.vernacular: 當我勸阻佢嘅企圖,發現佢決意要做時,我用惡毒嘅話威脅要揭發佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我勸阻他的企圖,發現他決意要做時,我用惡毒的話威脅要揭發他:

passages.original: he replied, ‘Thou unpossessing bastard!
passages.vernacular: 佢回答:「你呢個冇財產嘅私生子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回答:「你這沒有財產的私生子!

passages.original: dost thou think, If I would stand against thee, would the reposal Of any trust, virtue, or worth in thee Make thy words faith’d?
passages.vernacular: 你以為,如果我同你對抗,你有任何信用、美德或價值嘅信任,能使你嘅話被人相信嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為,如果我與你對抗,你有任何信用、美德或價值的信任,能使你的話被人相信嗎?

passages.original: No: what I should deny As this I would; ay, though thou didst produce My very character, I’d turn it all To thy suggestion, plot, and damned practice:
passages.vernacular: 不:我會否認嘅,正如我會否認呢件事;係嘅,即使你攞出我自己嘅筆跡,我都會把佢全都轉成你嘅唆使、計謀同該死嘅行徑:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不:我會否認的,正如我會否認這件事;是的,即使你拿出我自己的筆跡,我也會把它全都轉成你的唆使、計謀和該死的行徑:

passages.original: And thou must make a dullard of the world, If they not thought the profits of my death Were very pregnant and potential spurs To make thee seek it.
passages.vernacular: 如果人哋不認為我死後嘅利益係好豐厚、有力嘅刺激,使你去尋求,嗰你必須把世界當成笨蛋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果人們不認為我死後的利益是非常豐厚、有力的刺激,使你去尋求,那你必須把世界當成笨蛋。」

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: O strange and fast’ned villain!
passages.vernacular: 啊奇怪而頑固嘅惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊奇怪而頑固的惡棍!

passages.original: Would he deny his letter, said he?
passages.vernacular: 佢會否認佢嘅信,佢講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會否認他的信,他說?

passages.original: I never got him.
passages.vernacular: 我從未生佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未生他。

passages.original: [Tucket within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Hark, the Duke’s trumpets!
passages.vernacular: 聽,公爵嘅號角!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽,公爵的號角!

passages.original: I know not why he comes.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道佢點解嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道他為什麼來。

passages.original: All ports I’ll bar; the villain shall not scape;
passages.vernacular: 我要封鎖所有港口;惡棍逃不掉;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要封鎖所有港口;惡棍逃不掉;

passages.original: The Duke must grant me that: besides, his picture I will send far and near, that all the kingdom May have due note of him;
passages.vernacular: 公爵必須答應我嗰點:而且,我要把佢嘅畫像送到遠近各處,使全國都注意到佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵必須答應我那點:而且,我要把他的畫像送到遠近各處,使全國都注意到他;

passages.original: and of my land, Loyal and natural boy, I’ll work the means To make thee capable.
passages.vernacular: 至於我嘅土地,忠誠而天性嘅細路,我會設法讓你有資格繼承。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我的土地,忠誠而天性的孩子,我會設法讓你有資格繼承。

passages.original: Enter Cornwall, Regan and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [康華爾、里根同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [康華爾、里根和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: How now, my noble friend!
passages.vernacular: 點樣,我高貴嘅朋友!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣,我高貴的朋友!

passages.original: since I came hither, Which I can call but now, I have heard strange news.
passages.vernacular: 自從我嚟到呢度(我剛講過就係頭先),聽到咗奇怪嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我來到這裡(我剛說過就是剛才),聽到了奇怪的消息。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: If it be true, all vengeance comes too short Which can pursue th’offender.
passages.vernacular: 如果係真嘅,任何追捕罪犯嘅復仇都嫌不足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是真的,任何追捕罪犯的復仇都嫌不足。

passages.original: How dost, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 你點樣,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎樣,大人?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: O madam, my old heart is crack’d, it’s crack’d!
passages.vernacular: 啊夫人,我年老嘅心碎喇,碎喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊夫人,我年老的心碎了,碎了!

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: What, did my father’s godson seek your life?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我父親嘅教子想要你嘅命?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我父親的教子想要你的命?

passages.original: He whom my father nam’d? your Edgar?
passages.vernacular: 佢,我父親取名嘅嗰位?你嘅愛德伽?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他,我父親取名的那位?你的愛德伽?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: O lady, lady, shame would have it hid!
passages.vernacular: 啊夫人,夫人,羞恥要把佢藏起嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊夫人,夫人,羞恥要把它藏起來!

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Was he not companion with the riotous knights That tend upon my father?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係同嗰啲服侍我父親嘅放蕩騎士為伴嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是與那些服侍我父親的放蕩騎士為伴嗎?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I know not, madam; ’tis too bad, too bad.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道,夫人;太糟喇,太糟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道,夫人;太糟了,太糟了。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Yes, madam, he was of that consort.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,夫人,佢係嗰夥人嘅同伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,夫人,他是那夥人的同伴。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: No marvel then though he were ill affected: ’Tis they have put him on the old man’s death, To have the expense and waste of his revenues.
passages.vernacular: 難怪佢心懷不軌:係佢哋唆使佢謀害老人,好獲得佢收入嘅花費同浪費。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪他心懷不軌:是他們唆使他謀害老人,好獲得他收入的花費和浪費。

passages.original: I have this present evening from my sister Been well inform’d of them;
passages.vernacular: 今晚我剛從我姊姊嗰度得到佢哋嘅詳細消息;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚我剛從我姊姊那裡得到他們的詳細消息;

passages.original: and with such cautions That if they come to sojourn at my house, I’ll not be there.
passages.vernacular: 並附有咁樣嘅警告:如果佢哋嚟我家小住,我就不喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並附有這樣的警告:如果他們來我家小住,我就不在那裡。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Nor I, assure thee, Regan.
passages.vernacular: 我都不喺,里根,向你保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不在,里根,向你保證。

passages.original: Edmund, I hear that you have shown your father A childlike office.
passages.vernacular: 愛德蒙,我聽講你對你父親盡咗孝子嘅職責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛德蒙,我聽說你對你父親盡了孝子的職責。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: It was my duty, sir.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅本分,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的本分,先生。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: He did bewray his practice; and receiv’d This hurt you see, striving to apprehend him.
passages.vernacular: 佢暴露咗佢嘅圖謀;而且為了抓佢,受咗你睇到嘅呢傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他暴露了他的圖謀;而且為了抓他,受了你看到的這傷。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Is he pursued?
passages.vernacular: 有人追佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人追他嗎?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Ay, my good lord.
passages.vernacular: 有,我嘅好大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,我的好大人。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: If he be taken, he shall never more Be fear’d of doing harm:
passages.vernacular: 如果佢被抓住,佢就再都唔會被人害怕佢害人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他被抓住,他就再也不會被人害怕他害人;

passages.original: make your own purpose, How in my strength you please.
passages.vernacular: 你可以隨意按你自己嘅目的使用我嘅力量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以隨意按你自己的目的使用我的力量。

passages.original: For you, Edmund, Whose virtue and obedience doth this instant So much commend itself, you shall be ours:
passages.vernacular: 至於你,愛德蒙,你嘅美德同順從此刻如此值得稱讚,你將係我哋嘅人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於你,愛德蒙,你的美德與順從此刻如此值得稱讚,你將是我們的人:

passages.original: Natures of such deep trust we shall much need; You we first seize on.
passages.vernacular: 我哋好需要呢種深可信賴嘅品性;我哋首先要抓住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們非常需要這種深可信賴的品性;我們首先要抓住你。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: I shall serve you, sir, truly, however else.
passages.vernacular: 我會忠誠地侍奉您,先生,不管別嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會忠誠地侍奉您,先生,不管別的。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: For him I thank your grace.
passages.vernacular: 為了佢,我感謝殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了他,我感謝殿下。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: You know not why we came to visit you?
passages.vernacular: 你知道我哋為何嚟拜訪你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我們為何來拜訪你嗎?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Thus out of season, threading dark-ey’d night:
passages.vernacular: 咁樣不合時宜,穿過黑眼睛嘅夜:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣不合時宜,穿過黑眼睛的夜:

passages.original: Occasions, noble Gloucester, of some poise, Wherein we must have use of your advice.
passages.vernacular: 係有些份量嘅事,高貴嘅葛羅斯特,我哋需要你嘅建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是有些份量的事,高貴的葛羅斯特,我們需要你的建議。

passages.original: Our father he hath writ, so hath our sister, Of differences, which I best thought it fit To answer from our home;
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅父親寫咗信,我哋嘅姊姊都寫咗信,關於啲分歧,我覺得最好從我哋家裡回覆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的父親寫了信,我們的姊姊也寫了信,關於一些分歧,我覺得最好從我們家裡回覆;

passages.original: the several messengers From hence attend dispatch.
passages.vernacular: 幾位信使從呢度等待發送。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾位信使從這裡等待發送。

passages.original: Our good old friend, Lay comforts to your bosom;
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅好老朋友,安慰你嘅胸懷;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的好老朋友,安慰你的胸懷;

passages.original: and bestow Your needful counsel to our business, Which craves the instant use.
passages.vernacular: 並畀予我哋嘅事務必需嘅建議,呢事迫切需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並給予我們的事務必需的建議,這事迫切需要。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I serve you, madam: Your graces are right welcome.
passages.vernacular: 我為您效勞,夫人:殿下哋好歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為您效勞,夫人:殿下們非常歡迎。

passages.original: [Exeunt. Flourish.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。號角齊鳴。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。號角齊鳴。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene II — Before Gloucester’s Castle 第二幕第二場:葛羅斯特城堡前

passages.original: Enter Kent and Oswald, severally.
passages.vernacular: [肯特同奧斯華分別上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特和奧斯華分別上。]

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Good dawning to thee, friend: art of this house?
passages.vernacular: 早安,朋友:你係呢家嘅人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,朋友:你是這家的人嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Ay.
passages.vernacular: 係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Where may we set our horses?
passages.vernacular: 我哋可以把馬放喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們可以把馬放在哪裡?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I’ the mire.
passages.vernacular: 喺爛泥裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在爛泥裡。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Prythee, if thou lov’st me, tell me.
passages.vernacular: 請你,如果你愛我,告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,如果你愛我,告訴我。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I love thee not.
passages.vernacular: 我不愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不愛你。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Why then, I care not for thee.
passages.vernacular: 咁我都不在乎你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼我也不在乎你。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: If I had thee in Lipsbury pinfold, I would make thee care for me.
passages.vernacular: 如果我把你抓進利普斯伯里嘅畜欄,我就讓你在乎我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我把你抓進利普斯伯里的畜欄,我就讓你在乎我。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Why dost thou use me thus?
passages.vernacular: 你點解咁樣對我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼這樣對我?

passages.original: I know thee not.
passages.vernacular: 我不認識你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不認識你。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Fellow, I know thee.
passages.vernacular: 朋友,我認識你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朋友,我認識你。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: What dost thou know me for?
passages.vernacular: 你認識我係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認識我是什麼?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: A knave; a rascal; an eater of broken meats; a base, proud, shallow, beggarly, three-suited, hundred-pound, filthy, worsted-stocking knave;
passages.vernacular: 一個惡棍;一個無賴;一個食剩菜嘅人;一個卑賤、驕傲、淺薄、乞丐般、只有三套衣服、一百鎊家產、骯髒、穿毛線襪嘅惡棍;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個惡棍;一個無賴;一個吃剩菜的人;一個卑賤、驕傲、淺薄、乞丐般、只有三套衣服、一百鎊家產、骯髒、穿毛線襪的惡棍;

passages.original: a lily-livered, action-taking, whoreson, glass-gazing, super-serviceable, finical rogue;
passages.vernacular: 一個膽小如鼠、動不動訴訟、雜種、對鏡自憐、過分殷勤、挑剔嘅無賴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個膽小如鼠、動不動訴訟、雜種、對鏡自憐、過分殷勤、挑剔的無賴;

passages.original: one trunk-inheriting slave; one that wouldst be a bawd in way of good service, and art nothing but the composition of a knave, beggar, coward, pander, and the son and heir of a mongrel bitch:
passages.vernacular: 一個只繼承一隻箱子嘅奴才;一個為了好好服務願意做皮條客嘅人,只係惡棍、乞丐、懦夫、拉皮條者嘅混合物,以及一條雜種母狗嘅兒子同繼承人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個只繼承一隻箱子的奴才;一個為了好好服務願意做皮條客的人,只是惡棍、乞丐、懦夫、拉皮條者的混合物,以及一條雜種母狗的兒子和繼承人:

passages.original: one whom I will beat into clamorous whining, if thou deniest the least syllable of thy addition.
passages.vernacular: 如果你否認你頭銜中最小嘅一個音節,我就把你打到哀號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你否認你頭銜中最小的一個音節,我就把你打到哀號。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Why, what a monstrous fellow art thou, thus to rail on one that’s neither known of thee nor knows thee?
passages.vernacular: 咦,你呢個係乜嘢怪物,竟咁樣辱罵一個既不認識你、你都不認識嘅人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,你這是什麼怪物,竟這樣辱罵一個既不認識你、你也不認識的人?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: What a brazen-faced varlet art thou, to deny thou knowest me!
passages.vernacular: 你呢厚臉皮嘅無賴,竟否認你認識我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這厚臉皮的無賴,竟否認你認識我!

passages.original: Is it two days ago since I tripped up thy heels and beat thee before the King?
passages.vernacular: 兩天前我唔係絆倒你並喺國王面前打你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩天前我不是絆倒你並在國王面前打你嗎?

passages.original: Draw, you rogue: for, though it be night, yet the moon shines;
passages.vernacular: 拔劍,你呢無賴:因為雖然係夜晚,月亮仲亮住;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔劍,你這無賴:因為雖然是夜晚,月亮還亮著;

passages.original: I’ll make a sop o’ the moonshine of you: draw, you whoreson cullionly barber-monger, draw!
passages.vernacular: 我要把你變成月光下嘅泡麵包:拔劍,你呢雜種、下流理髮匠嫖客,拔劍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把你變成月光下的泡麵包:拔劍,你這雜種、下流理髮匠嫖客,拔劍!

passages.original: [Drawing his sword.]
passages.vernacular: [拔劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拔劍。]

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Away!
passages.vernacular: 走開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開!

passages.original: I have nothing to do with thee.
passages.vernacular: 我跟你冇乜嘢關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟你沒什麼關係。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Draw, you rascal: you come with letters against the King;
passages.vernacular: 拔劍,你呢無賴:你帶住反對國王嘅信嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔劍,你這無賴:你帶著反對國王的信來;

passages.original: and take vanity the puppet’s part against the royalty of her father:
passages.vernacular: 又站喺虛榮木偶嘅一邊,反對佢父親嘅王權:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又站在虛榮木偶的一邊,反對她父親的王權:

passages.original: draw, you rogue, or I’ll so carbonado your shanks:—draw, you rascal; come your ways!
passages.vernacular: 拔劍,你呢無賴,否則我把你嘅腿肉烤焦:——拔劍,你呢無賴;嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拔劍,你這無賴,否則我把你的腿肉烤焦:——拔劍,你這無賴;來!

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Help, ho! murder! help!
passages.vernacular: 救命,喂!謀殺!救命!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 救命,喂!謀殺!救命!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Strike, you slave; stand, rogue, stand; you neat slave, strike!
passages.vernacular: 打,你呢奴才;站住,無賴,站住;你呢漂亮嘅奴才,打!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打,你這奴才;站住,無賴,站住;你這漂亮的奴才,打!

passages.original: [Beating him.]
passages.vernacular: [打佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [打他。]

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Help, ho! murder! murder!
passages.vernacular: 救命,喂!謀殺!謀殺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 救命,喂!謀殺!謀殺!

passages.original: Enter Edmund, Cornwall, Regan, Gloucester and Servants.
passages.vernacular: [愛德蒙、康華爾、里根、葛羅斯特同僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德蒙、康華爾、里根、葛羅斯特和僕人們上。]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: How now!
passages.vernacular: 點喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了!

passages.original: What’s the matter? Part!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢事?住手!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼事?住手!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: With you, goodman boy, if you please: come, I’ll flesh ye; come on, young master.
passages.vernacular: 跟你,好小子,如果你願意:嚟,我畀你見血;嚟吧,年輕少爺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟你,好小子,如果你願意:來,我給你見血;來吧,年輕少爺。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Weapons! arms!
passages.vernacular: 武器!兵器!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 武器!兵器!

passages.original: What’s the matter here?
passages.vernacular: 呢度乜嘢事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡什麼事?

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Keep peace, upon your lives, he dies that strikes again.
passages.vernacular: 憑你哋嘅性命,保持安靜,邊個再打邊個死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑你們的性命,保持安靜,誰再打誰死。

passages.original: What is the matter?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼事?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: The messengers from our sister and the King.
passages.vernacular: 我哋姊姊同國王嘅信使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們姊姊和國王的信使。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: What is your difference? Speak.
passages.vernacular: 你哋嘅分歧係乜嘢?講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們的分歧是什麼?說。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: I am scarce in breath, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我幾乎喘不過氣,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾乎喘不過氣,大人。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: No marvel, you have so bestirr’d your valour.
passages.vernacular: 難怪,你咁樣發揮咗你嘅勇氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪,你這樣發揮了你的勇氣。

passages.original: You cowardly rascal, nature disclaims in thee; a tailor made thee.
passages.vernacular: 你呢膽怯嘅無賴,自然否認你;係裁縫做咗你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這膽怯的無賴,自然否認你;是裁縫做了你。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Thou art a strange fellow: a tailor make a man?
passages.vernacular: 你係個奇怪嘅傢伙:裁縫造人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個奇怪的傢伙:裁縫造人?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Ay, a tailor, sir: a stonecutter or a painter could not have made him so ill, though he had been but two years at the trade.
passages.vernacular: 係,裁縫,先生:就算石匠或畫家只學咗兩年,都唔會把佢造得咁糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,裁縫,先生:就算石匠或畫家只學了兩年,也不會把他造得這麼糟。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Speak yet, how grew your quarrel?
passages.vernacular: 再講,你哋嘅爭吵係點起嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,你們的爭吵是怎麼起的?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: This ancient ruffian, sir, whose life I have spared at suit of his grey beard,—
passages.vernacular: 呢個老流氓,先生,我睇喺佢灰鬍子嘅份上饒咗佢嘅命——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個老流氓,先生,我看在他灰鬍子的份上饒了他的命——

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Thou whoreson zed!
passages.vernacular: 你呢雜種嘅「Z」字!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這雜種的「Z」字!

passages.original: thou unnecessary letter!
passages.vernacular: 你呢個唔使要嘅字母!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這個不必要的字母!

passages.original: My lord, if you’ll give me leave, I will tread this unbolted villain into mortar and daub the walls of a jakes with him.
passages.vernacular: 大人,如果您允許,我要把呢個冇篩過嘅惡棍踩成灰泥,用佢塗抹茅廁嘅牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,如果您允許,我要把這個沒篩過的惡棍踩成灰泥,用他塗抹茅廁的牆。

passages.original: Spare my grey beard, you wagtail?
passages.vernacular: 饒我嘅灰鬍子,你呢鶺鴒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 饒我的灰鬍子,你這鶺鴒?

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Peace, sirrah!
passages.vernacular: 安靜,小子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,小子!

passages.original: You beastly knave, know you no reverence?
passages.vernacular: 你呢畜生般嘅惡棍,你不懂得尊敬嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這畜生般的惡棍,你不懂得尊敬嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Yes, sir; but anger hath a privilege.
passages.vernacular: 懂,先生;但憤怒有特權。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懂,先生;但憤怒有特權。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Why art thou angry?
passages.vernacular: 你點解生氣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼生氣?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: That such a slave as this should wear a sword, Who wears no honesty.
passages.vernacular: 因為咁樣一個冇誠實嘅奴才竟佩劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為這樣一個沒有誠實的奴才竟佩劍。

passages.original: Such smiling rogues as these, Like rats, oft bite the holy cords a-twain Which are too intrince t’unloose;
passages.vernacular: 呢類笑嘻嘻嘅無賴,像老鼠一樣,常把神聖嘅繩索咬斷,嗰啲繩索太緊密無法解開;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這類笑嘻嘻的無賴,像老鼠一樣,常把神聖的繩索咬斷,那些繩索太緊密無法解開;

passages.original: smooth every passion That in the natures of their lords rebel;
passages.vernacular: 佢哋撫平主人天性中每一種反叛嘅激情;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們撫平主人天性中每一種反叛的激情;

passages.original: Bring oil to fire, snow to their colder moods;
passages.vernacular: 對主人嘅怒火添油,對佢哋較冷嘅情緒添雪;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對主人的怒火添油,對他們較冷的情緒添雪;

passages.original: Renege, affirm, and turn their halcyon beaks With every gale and vary of their masters, Knowing naught, like dogs, but following.
passages.vernacular: 否認、肯定,隨住主人每一陣風嘅變化轉動佢哋嘅翠鳥嘴,乜嘢都不懂,像狗一樣只會跟隨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 否認、肯定,隨著主人每一陣風的變化轉動他們的翠鳥嘴,什麼都不懂,像狗一樣只會跟隨。

passages.original: A plague upon your epileptic visage!
passages.vernacular: 瘟疫降喺你癲癇般嘅臉上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瘟疫降在你癲癇般的臉上!

passages.original: Smile you my speeches, as I were a fool?
passages.vernacular: 你笑我嘅話,好像我係傻瓜?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你笑我的話,好像我是傻瓜?

passages.original: Goose, if I had you upon Sarum plain, I’d drive ye cackling home to Camelot.
passages.vernacular: 鵝,如果我喺薩勒姆平原上抓到你,我會把你呱呱叫住趕回卡梅洛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鵝,如果我在薩勒姆平原上抓到你,我會把你呱呱叫著趕回卡梅洛。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: What, art thou mad, old fellow?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你瘋咗嗎,老傢伙?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你瘋了嗎,老傢伙?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: How fell you out? Say that.
passages.vernacular: 你哋點吵起嚟嘅?講講睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們怎麼吵起來的?說說看。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: No contraries hold more antipathy Than I and such a knave.
passages.vernacular: 冇任何對立比我同咁樣一個惡棍更相互仇恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有任何對立比我和這樣一個惡棍更相互仇恨。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Why dost thou call him knave?
passages.vernacular: 你點解叫佢惡棍?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼叫他惡棍?

passages.original: What is his fault?
passages.vernacular: 佢犯咗乜嘢錯?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他犯了什麼錯?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: His countenance likes me not.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意佢嘅面相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡他的面相。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: No more perchance does mine, or his, or hers.
passages.vernacular: 或者你都不鍾意我嘅、佢嘅或佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你也不喜歡我的、他的或她的。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Sir, ’tis my occupation to be plain: I have seen better faces in my time Than stands on any shoulder that I see Before me at this instant.
passages.vernacular: 先生,直率係我嘅職業:我呢輩子見過更好嘅臉,比而家我面前任何肩膀上所站嘅都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,直率是我的職業:我這輩子見過更好的臉,比現在我面前任何肩膀上所站的都好。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: This is some fellow Who, having been prais’d for bluntness, doth affect A saucy roughness, and constrains the garb Quite from his nature:
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個傢伙,因為被稱讚直率,就裝作放肆嘅粗魯,把姿態完全扭曲咗天性:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個傢伙,因為被稱讚直率,就裝作放肆的粗魯,把姿態完全扭曲了天性:

passages.original: he cannot flatter, he, An honest mind and plain, he must speak truth!
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會諂媚,佢!一個誠實質樸嘅心,佢必須講真話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不會諂媚,他!一個誠實質樸的心,他必須說真話!

passages.original: An they will take it, so; if not, he’s plain.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋接受,好;如果不,佢就係直率。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們接受,好;如果不,他就是直率。

passages.original: These kind of knaves I know which in this plainness Harbour more craft and more corrupter ends Than twenty silly-ducking observants That stretch their duties nicely.
passages.vernacular: 我知道呢類惡棍,喺呢種直率之下藏住比二十個愚蠢鞠躬嘅奉承者更多嘅詭詐同更腐敗嘅目的,嗰啲奉承者把職責拉伸得恰到好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道這類惡棍,在這種直率之下藏著比二十個愚蠢鞠躬的奉承者更多的詭詐和更腐敗的目的,那些奉承者把職責拉伸得恰到好處。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Sir, in good faith, in sincere verity, Under th’allowance of your great aspect, Whose influence, like the wreath of radiant fire On flickering Phoebus’ front,—
passages.vernacular: 先生,講真嘅,誠懇地,喺您偉大容貌嘅許可之下,其影響像閃爍嘅福玻斯額前嘅光環花環——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,說真的,誠懇地,在您偉大容貌的許可之下,其影響像閃爍的福玻斯額前的光環花環——

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: What mean’st by this?
passages.vernacular: 你呢個係乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這是什麼意思?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: To go out of my dialect, which you discommend so much.
passages.vernacular: 為了離開我嘅方言,您咁不贊成嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了離開我的方言,您這麼不贊成的。

passages.original: I know, sir, I am no flatterer: he that beguiled you in a plain accent was a plain knave;
passages.vernacular: 我知道,先生,我唔係諂媚者:用直白口吻騙您嘅人,係個直白嘅惡棍;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道,先生,我不是諂媚者:用直白口吻騙您的人,是個直白的惡棍;

passages.original: which, for my part, I will not be, though I should win your displeasure to entreat me to’t.
passages.vernacular: 就我而言,我唔會做,即使我要因此得到您嘅不悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我而言,我不會做,即使我要因此得到您的不悅。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: What was the offence you gave him?
passages.vernacular: 你冒犯佢乜嘢喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你冒犯他什麼了?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: I never gave him any: It pleas’d the King his master very late To strike at me, upon his misconstruction;
passages.vernacular: 我從冇冒犯過佢:佢嘅主人國王最近高興地因佢嘅誤解打我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒冒犯過他:他的主人國王最近高興地因他的誤解打我;

passages.original: When he, compact, and flattering his displeasure, Tripp’d me behind;
passages.vernacular: 當佢串通一氣,諂媚佢嘅不悅,從背後絆倒我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他串通一氣,諂媚他的不悅,從背後絆倒我;

passages.original: being down, insulted, rail’d And put upon him such a deal of man, That worthied him, got praises of the King For him attempting who was self-subdu’d;
passages.vernacular: 倒地後,侮辱、辱罵,並擺出咁多男子氣概,使佢顯得英勇,得到國王稱讚,因為佢攻擊咗一個自己已經屈服嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 倒地後,侮辱、辱罵,並擺出那麼多男子氣概,使他顯得英勇,得到國王稱讚,因為他攻擊了一個自己已經屈服的人;

passages.original: And, in the fleshment of this dread exploit, Drew on me here again.
passages.vernacular: 又喺呢可怕壯舉嘅興奮中,再次向我拔劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又在這可怕壯舉的興奮中,再次向我拔劍。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: None of these rogues and cowards But Ajax is their fool.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲無賴同懦夫中,冇一個唔係埃阿斯喺佢哋面前都像個傻瓜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些無賴和懦夫中,沒有一個不是埃阿斯在他們面前也像個傻瓜。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Fetch forth the stocks!
passages.vernacular: 攞木枷嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿木枷來!

passages.original: You stubborn ancient knave, you reverent braggart, We’ll teach you.
passages.vernacular: 你呢頑固嘅老惡棍,可敬嘅吹牛者,我哋嚟教你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這頑固的老惡棍,可敬的吹牛者,我們來教你。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Sir, I am too old to learn: Call not your stocks for me:
passages.vernacular: 先生,我太老咗唔能夠學:別為我叫木枷:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我太老了不能學:別為我叫木枷:

passages.original: I serve the King; On whose employment I was sent to you:
passages.vernacular: 我侍奉國王;奉佢嘅差遣我嚟見你:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我侍奉國王;奉他的差遣我來見你:

passages.original: You shall do small respect, show too bold malice Against the grace and person of my master, Stocking his messenger.
passages.vernacular: 你把佢嘅信使鎖進木枷,係對我主人嘅恩寵同人格極不尊重、表現過分大膽嘅惡意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把他的信使鎖進木枷,是對我主人的恩寵與人格極不尊重、表現過分大膽的惡意。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Fetch forth the stocks!
passages.vernacular: 攞木枷嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿木枷來!

passages.original: As I have life and honour, there shall he sit till noon.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅生命同榮譽,佢要坐到中午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的生命和榮譽,他要坐到中午。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Till noon!
passages.vernacular: 到中午!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到中午!

passages.original: Till night, my lord; and all night too!
passages.vernacular: 到夜晚,大人;而且整夜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到夜晚,大人;而且整夜!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Why, madam, if I were your father’s dog, You should not use me so.
passages.vernacular: 咦,夫人,如果我係您父親嘅狗,您都不該咁樣對我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,夫人,如果我是您父親的狗,您也不該這樣對我。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Sir, being his knave, I will.
passages.vernacular: 先生,既然係佢嘅奴才,我就要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,既然是他的奴才,我就要。

passages.original: [Stocks brought out.]
passages.vernacular: [木枷被攞出嚟。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [木枷被拿出來。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: This is a fellow of the selfsame colour Our sister speaks of.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我姊姊所講嘅同一種顏色嘅傢伙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我姊姊所說的同一種顏色的傢伙。

passages.original: Come, bring away the stocks!
passages.vernacular: 嚟,把木枷攞嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,把木枷拿來!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Let me beseech your grace not to do so: His fault is much, and the good King his master Will check him for’t:
passages.vernacular: 請殿下別咁樣:佢嘅過錯好大,佢嘅主人好國王會為此責備佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請殿下別這樣:他的過錯很大,他的主人好國王會為此責備他:

passages.original: your purpos’d low correction Is such as basest and contemned’st wretches For pilferings and most common trespasses, Are punish’d with.
passages.vernacular: 您打算施加嘅卑賤懲罰,係最卑賤、最被鄙視嘅可憐人,因偷竊同最普通嘅過失所受嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您打算施加的卑賤懲罰,是最卑賤、最被鄙視的可憐人,因偷竊和最普通的過失所受的。

passages.original: The King must take it ill That he, so slightly valued in his messenger, Should have him thus restrained.
passages.vernacular: 國王一定會不高興,佢嘅信使被咁樣輕視,竟被如此拘禁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王一定會不高興,他的信使被這樣輕視,竟被如此拘禁。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: I’ll answer that.
passages.vernacular: 我嚟回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來回答。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: My sister may receive it much more worse, To have her gentleman abus’d, assaulted, For following her affairs.
passages.vernacular: 我姊姊可能更加不高興,因為佢嘅紳士為佢辦事被辱罵、攻擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我姊姊可能更加不高興,因為她的紳士為她辦事被辱罵、攻擊。

passages.original: Put in his legs.
passages.vernacular: 把佢嘅腿放進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他的腿放進去。

passages.original: [Kent is put in the stocks.]
passages.vernacular: [肯特被鎖進木枷。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特被鎖進木枷。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Come, my good lord, away.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我嘅好大人,走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我的好大人,走吧。

passages.original: [Exeunt all but Gloucester and Kent.]
passages.vernacular: [除葛羅斯特同肯特外,眾人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [除葛羅斯特和肯特外,眾人下。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I am sorry for thee, friend; ’tis the Duke’s pleasure, Whose disposition, all the world well knows, Will not be rubb’d nor stopp’d; I’ll entreat for thee.
passages.vernacular: 我為你難過,朋友;呢個係公爵嘅意思,佢嘅性情,全世界都知道,唔容摩擦或阻擋;我會為你求情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為你難過,朋友;這是公爵的意思,他的性情,全世界都知道,不容摩擦或阻擋;我會為你求情。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
