passages.original: Pray do not, sir: I have watch’d, and travell’d hard;
passages.vernacular: 請你別,先生:我守夜、趕路辛苦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你別,先生:我守夜、趕路辛苦;

passages.original: Some time I shall sleep out, the rest I’ll whistle.
passages.vernacular: 有些時候我會瞓過去,其餘時候我吹口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些時候我會睡過去,其餘時候我吹口哨。

passages.original: A good man’s fortune may grow out at heels: Give you good morrow!
passages.vernacular: 好人嘅運氣都可能磨破鞋跟:祝你早安!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好人的運氣也可能磨破鞋跟:祝你早安!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: The Duke’s to blame in this: ’twill be ill taken.
passages.vernacular: 公爵喺呢件事上有錯:呢會被人記恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵在這件事上有錯:這會被人記恨。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Good King, that must approve the common saw, Thou out of heaven’s benediction com’st To the warm sun.
passages.vernacular: 好國王,你必須證實嗰句俗語:你從天堂嘅祝福中嚟,走到暖同嘅太陽下(意為每況愈下)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好國王,你必須證實那句俗語:你從天堂的祝福中來,走到暖和的太陽下(意為每況愈下)。

passages.original: Approach, thou beacon to this under globe, That by thy comfortable beams I may Peruse this letter.
passages.vernacular: 走近,你呢下界嘅燈塔,借你安慰嘅光束,我可以讀呢封信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走近,你這下界的燈塔,借你安慰的光束,我可以讀這封信。

passages.original: Nothing almost sees miracles But misery.
passages.vernacular: 除咗悲慘,幾乎冇乜嘢能睇到奇蹟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了悲慘,幾乎沒有什麼能看到奇蹟。

passages.original: I know ’tis from Cordelia, Who hath most fortunately been inform’d Of my obscured course.
passages.vernacular: 我知道呢個係考黛莉亞寫嘅,佢好幸運地得知咗我隱蔽嘅行蹤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道這是考黛莉亞寫的,她非常幸運地得知了我隱蔽的行蹤。

passages.original: And shall find time From this enormous state, seeking to give Losses their remedies.
passages.vernacular: 佢會從呢可怕嘅狀態中找到時間,設法補救損失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會從這可怕的狀態中找到時間,設法補救損失。

passages.original: All weary and o’erwatch’d, Take vantage, heavy eyes, not to behold This shameful lodging.
passages.vernacular: 全然疲憊、熬夜過度嘅,沉重嘅眼睛,趁機不去睇呢恥辱嘅住處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全然疲憊、熬夜過度的,沉重的眼睛,趁機不去看這恥辱的住處。

passages.original: Fortune, good night: smile once more, turn thy wheel!
passages.vernacular: 命運,晚安:再微笑一次,轉動你嘅輪子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 命運,晚安:再微笑一次,轉動你的輪子!

passages.original: [He sleeps.]
passages.vernacular: [佢瞓。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [他睡。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene III — The Open Country 第二幕第三場:曠野

passages.original: Enter Edgar.
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽上。]

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: I heard myself proclaim’d, And by the happy hollow of a tree Escap’d the hunt.
passages.vernacular: 我聽到自己被通緝,靠一棵樹幸運嘅樹洞逃過追捕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到自己被通緝,靠一棵樹幸運的樹洞逃過追捕。

passages.original: No port is free, no place That guard and most unusual vigilance Does not attend my taking.
passages.vernacular: 冇港口係自由嘅,冇地方冇守衛同異常嘅警戒喺等住抓我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有港口是自由的,沒有地方沒有守衛和異常的警戒在等著抓我。

passages.original: While I may scape I will preserve myself: and am bethought To take the basest and most poorest shape That ever penury in contempt of man, Brought near to beast:
passages.vernacular: 只要我能逃脫,我就保全自己:我已想到,要扮成最卑賤、最貧窮嘅形象,嗰種貧困鄙視人,將人帶近野獸:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我能逃脫,我就保全自己:我已想到,要扮成最卑賤、最貧窮的形象,那種貧困鄙視人,將人帶近野獸:

passages.original: my face I’ll grime with filth, Blanket my loins;
passages.vernacular: 我要把臉塗上污泥,用毯子裹腰;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把臉塗上污泥,用毯子裹腰;

passages.original: elf all my hair in knots, And with presented nakedness outface The winds and persecutions of the sky.
passages.vernacular: 把頭髮纏成妖精結,以赤裸嘅身體對抗風同天空嘅迫害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把頭髮纏成妖精結,以赤裸的身體對抗風和天空的迫害。

passages.original: The country gives me proof and precedent Of Bedlam beggars, who, with roaring voices, Strike in their numb’d and mortified bare arms Pins, wooden pricks, nails, sprigs of rosemary;
passages.vernacular: 呢個國家畀咗我乞丐瘋子嘅證據同先例,佢哋用吼叫嘅聲音,把針、木刺、釘子、迷迭香枝插進自己麻木僵死嘅赤裸手臂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個國家給了我乞丐瘋子的證據和先例,他們用吼叫的聲音,把針、木刺、釘子、迷迭香枝插進自己麻木僵死的赤裸手臂;

passages.original: And with this horrible object, from low farms, Poor pelting villages, sheep-cotes, and mills, Sometime with lunatic bans, sometime with prayers, Enforce their charity.
passages.vernacular: 用呢可怕嘅模樣,從低矮農場、貧窮鄉村、羊圈同磨坊,有時用瘋子嘅咒語,有時用祈禱,強迫人施捨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用這可怕的模樣,從低矮農場、貧窮鄉村、羊圈和磨坊,有時用瘋子的咒語,有時用祈禱,強迫人施捨。

passages.original: Poor Turlygod!
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅特利高德!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的特利高德!

passages.original: poor Tom, That’s something yet: Edgar I nothing am.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅湯姆,嗰仲算點乜嘢:愛德伽,我乜嘢都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的湯姆,那還算點什麼:愛德伽,我什麼都不是。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene IV — Before Gloucester’s Castle; Kent in the Stocks 第二幕第四場:葛羅斯特城堡前,肯特被鎖在木枷中

passages.original: Enter Lear, Fool and Gentleman.
passages.vernacular: [李爾、弄臣同紳士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾、弄臣和紳士上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: ’Tis strange that they should so depart from home, And not send back my messenger.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪,佢哋竟咁樣離家,又不把我嘅信使送回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪,他們竟這樣離家,又不把我的信使送回來。

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: As I learn’d, The night before there was no purpose in them Of this remove.
passages.vernacular: 據我所知,前一晚佢哋仲冇呢次搬走嘅打算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據我所知,前一晚他們還沒有這次搬走的打算。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Hail to thee, noble master!
passages.vernacular: 向你致敬,高貴嘅主人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向你致敬,高貴的主人!

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Ha!
passages.vernacular: 哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈!

passages.original: Mak’st thou this shame thy pastime?
passages.vernacular: 你把呢恥辱當消遣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把這恥辱當消遣嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: No, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 不,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,大人。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Ha, ha!
passages.vernacular: 哈,哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈,哈!

passages.original: he wears cruel garters.
passages.vernacular: 佢戴住殘酷嘅襪帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他戴著殘酷的襪帶。

passages.original: Horses are tied by the heads; dogs and bears by the neck, monkeys by the loins, and men by the legs:
passages.vernacular: 馬係繫頭嘅;狗同熊繫脖子,猴子繫腰,人繫腿:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬是繫頭的;狗和熊繫脖子,猴子繫腰,人繫腿:

passages.original: when a man is overlusty at legs, then he wears wooden nether-stocks.
passages.vernacular: 當一個人腿太有勁,就得穿木頭嘅長襪(木枷)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當一個人腿太有勁,就得穿木頭的長襪(木枷)。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What’s he that hath so much thy place mistook To set thee here?
passages.vernacular: 係邊個咁樣誤解你嘅身份,把你放喺呢度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是誰這樣誤解你的身份,把你放在這裡?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: It is both he and she, Your son and daughter.
passages.vernacular: 係佢都係佢,你嘅兒子同女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是他也是她,你的兒子和女兒。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No.
passages.vernacular: 不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Yes.
passages.vernacular: 係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No, I say.
passages.vernacular: 不,我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我說。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I say, yea.
passages.vernacular: 我講,係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說,是。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No, no; they would not.
passages.vernacular: 不,不;佢哋唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不;她們不會。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Yes, they have.
passages.vernacular: 係,佢哋做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,她們做了。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: By Jupiter, I swear no.
passages.vernacular: 憑朱庇特,我發誓不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑朱庇特,我發誓不。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: By Juno, I swear ay.
passages.vernacular: 憑朱諾,我發誓係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑朱諾,我發誓是。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: They durst not do’t.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔敢咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們不敢這樣做。

passages.original: They could not, would not do’t; ’tis worse than murder, To do upon respect such violent outrage:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔能夠、唔會咁樣做;有意地做咁樣暴力嘅凌辱,比謀殺更糟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們不能、不會這樣做;有意地做這樣暴力的凌辱,比謀殺更糟:

passages.original: Resolve me, with all modest haste, which way Thou mightst deserve or they impose this usage, Coming from us.
passages.vernacular: 儘快而不失禮地告訴我,你點會該受,或佢哋點會施加咁樣嘅待遇,而你係從我哋呢度嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘快而不失禮地告訴我,你怎麼會該受,或她們怎麼會施加這樣的待遇,而你是從我們這裡來的。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: My lord, when at their home I did commend your highness’ letters to them, Ere I was risen from the place that show’d My duty kneeling, came there a reeking post, Stew’d in his haste, half breathless, panting forth From Goneril his mistress salutations;
passages.vernacular: 大人,當我喺佢哋家把陛下嘅信交畀佢哋,我仲冇從表達我責任嘅跪姿中站起,嚟咗一個汗流浹背嘅驛使,匆忙得熱氣騰騰,半喘不過氣,喘住傳嚟佢嘅女主人高納麗嘅問候;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,當我在她們家把陛下的信交給她們,我還沒從表達我責任的跪姿中站起,來了一個汗流浹背的驛使,匆忙得熱氣騰騰,半喘不過氣,喘著傳來他的女主人高納麗的問候;

passages.original: Deliver’d letters, spite of intermission, Which presently they read;
passages.vernacular: 儘管打斷咗我,佢遞上信件,佢哋即刻讀喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管打斷了我,他遞上信件,她們立刻讀了;

passages.original: on those contents, They summon’d up their meiny, straight took horse;
passages.vernacular: 睇咗內容,佢哋召集隨從,即刻上馬;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看了內容,她們召集隨從,立刻上馬;

passages.original: Commanded me to follow and attend The leisure of their answer;
passages.vernacular: 命令我跟隨並等候佢哋答覆嘅空閒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 命令我跟隨並等候她們答覆的空閒;

passages.original: gave me cold looks: And meeting here the other messenger, Whose welcome I perceiv’d had poison’d mine, Being the very fellow which of late Display’d so saucily against your highness, Having more man than wit about me, drew;
passages.vernacular: 對我冷眼:而喺呢度遇見另一個信使,我察覺佢嘅受歡迎毒害咗我嘅,佢正是最近對陛下咁放肆嘅嗰個人,我膽氣多過智慧,拔咗劍;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我冷眼:而在這裡遇見另一個信使,我察覺他的受歡迎毒害了我的,他正是最近對陛下那麼放肆的那個人,我膽氣多過智慧,拔了劍;

passages.original: He rais’d the house with loud and coward cries.
passages.vernacular: 佢發出大聲而懦弱嘅叫喊驚動全屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發出大聲而懦弱的叫喊驚動全屋。

passages.original: Your son and daughter found this trespass worth The shame which here it suffers.
passages.vernacular: 您嘅兒子同女兒認為呢個過失值得受呢度所受嘅恥辱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您的兒子和女兒認為這個過失值得受這裡所受的恥辱。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Winter’s not gone yet, if the wild geese fly that way.
passages.vernacular: 冬天仲冇過去,如果野鵝往嗰邊飛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冬天還沒過去,如果野鵝往那邊飛。

passages.original: Fathers that wear rags Do make their children blind, But fathers that bear bags Shall see their children kind.
passages.vernacular: 穿破衣嘅父親使細路眼盲,但帶住錢袋嘅父親將見細路哋孝順。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穿破衣的父親使孩子眼盲,但帶著錢袋的父親將見孩子們孝順。

passages.original: Fortune, that arrant whore, Ne’er turns the key to th’ poor.
passages.vernacular: 命運,嗰個十足嘅娼婦,從不為窮人轉動鑰匙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 命運,那個十足的娼婦,從不為窮人轉動鑰匙。

passages.original: But for all this, thou shalt have as many dolours for thy daughters as thou canst tell in a year.
passages.vernacular: 不過儘管如此,你為你嘅女兒哋將有你一年數不完嘅悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過儘管如此,你為你的女兒們將有你一年數不完的悲傷。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O, how this mother swells up toward my heart!
passages.vernacular: 啊,呢股母親病(歇斯底里)幾咁向我心口湧上嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,這股母親病(歇斯底里)多麼向我心口湧上來!

passages.original: Hysterica passio, down, thou climbing sorrow, Thy element’s below!
passages.vernacular: 歇斯底里嘅痛苦,下去,你向上爬嘅悲傷,你嘅所在喺下面!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歇斯底里的痛苦,下去,你向上爬的悲傷,你的所在在下面!

passages.original: Where is this daughter?
passages.vernacular: 呢個女兒喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個女兒在哪裡?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: With the earl, sir, here within.
passages.vernacular: 同伯爵喺裡面,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和伯爵在裡面,大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Follow me not; stay here.
passages.vernacular: 別跟住我;留喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別跟著我;留在這裡。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: Made you no more offence but what you speak of?
passages.vernacular: 你就只有你講嘅呢啲冒犯嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就只有你說的這些冒犯嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: None.
passages.vernacular: 冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有。

passages.original: How chance the King comes with so small a number?
passages.vernacular: 國王點解只帶咁少嘅人嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王為什麼只帶這麼少的人來?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: An thou hadst been set i’ the stocks for that question, thou hadst well deserved it.
passages.vernacular: 如果你因為呢個問題被鎖進木枷,你係活該。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你因為這個問題被鎖進木枷,你是活該。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Why, fool?
passages.vernacular: 點解,弄臣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,弄臣?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: We’ll set thee to school to an ant, to teach thee there’s no labouring i’the winter.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會送你向螞蟻學習,教你冬天冇勞作呢回事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會送你向螞蟻學習,教你冬天沒有勞作這回事。

passages.original: All that follow their noses are led by their eyes but blind men;
passages.vernacular: 所有跟住鼻子走嘅人都由眼睛領路,只有瞎子除外;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有跟著鼻子走的人都由眼睛領路,只有瞎子除外;

passages.original: and there’s not a nose among twenty but can smell him that’s stinking.
passages.vernacular: 二十個鼻子裡冇一個聞不出臭嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 二十個鼻子裡沒有一個聞不出臭的。

passages.original: Let go thy hold when a great wheel runs down a hill, lest it break thy neck with following it;
passages.vernacular: 當一個大輪子滾下山時,放手,免得你跟住佢跌斷脖子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當一個大輪子滾下山時,放手,免得你跟著它跌斷脖子;

passages.original: but the great one that goes upward, let him draw thee after.
passages.vernacular: 但向上走嘅大輪子,就讓佢拉住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但向上走的大輪子,就讓它拉著你。

passages.original: When a wise man gives thee better counsel, give me mine again:
passages.vernacular: 當聰明人畀你更好嘅忠告時,把我嘅還畀我:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當聰明人給你更好的忠告時,把我的還給我:

passages.original: I would have none but knaves follow it, since a fool gives it.
passages.vernacular: 我要讓只有惡棍才遵從佢,因為係弄臣畀嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要讓只有惡棍才遵從它,因為是弄臣給的。

passages.original: That sir which serves and seeks for gain, And follows but for form, Will pack when it begins to rain, And leave thee in the storm.
passages.vernacular: 為利益而侍奉、只係為了形式而跟隨嘅先生,下雨時就會打包走人,把你留喺風暴中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為利益而侍奉、只是為了形式而跟隨的先生,下雨時就會打包走人,把你留在風暴中。

passages.original: But I will tarry; the fool will stay, And let the wise man fly:
passages.vernacular: 但我要留下;弄臣要留下,讓聰明人逃走:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我要留下;弄臣要留下,讓聰明人逃走:

passages.original: The knave turns fool that runs away; The fool no knave perdy.
passages.vernacular: 逃走嘅惡棍變成弄臣;弄臣可唔係惡棍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 逃走的惡棍變成弄臣;弄臣可不是惡棍。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Where learn’d you this, fool?
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊度學嘅呢個,弄臣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪裡學的這個,弄臣?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Not i’ the stocks, fool.
passages.vernacular: 唔係喺木枷裡,弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是在木枷裡,弄臣。

passages.original: Enter Lear and Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: [李爾同葛羅斯特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾和葛羅斯特上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Deny to speak with me?
passages.vernacular: 拒絕同我講話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拒絕和我說話?

passages.original: They are sick?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋病喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們病了?

passages.original: they are weary?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋累喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們累了?

passages.original: They have travell’d all the night?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋整夜趕路?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們整夜趕路?

passages.original: Mere fetches; The images of revolt and flying off.
passages.vernacular: 純粹係託詞;反叛同疏遠嘅影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 純粹是託詞;反叛和疏遠的影子。

passages.original: Fetch me a better answer.
passages.vernacular: 畀我一個更好嘅答覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我一個更好的答覆。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: My dear lord, You know the fiery quality of the Duke;
passages.vernacular: 我親愛嘅大人,您知道公爵嘅火暴性情;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我親愛的大人,您知道公爵的火暴性情;

passages.original: How unremovable and fix’d he is In his own course.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾咁不可動搖,固守自己嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他多麼不可動搖,固守自己的路。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Vengeance! plague! death! confusion! Fiery?
passages.vernacular: 復仇!瘟疫!死亡!混亂!火暴?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 復仇!瘟疫!死亡!混亂!火暴?

passages.original: What quality?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢性情?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼性情?

passages.original: Why, Gloucester, Gloucester, I’d speak with the Duke of Cornwall and his wife.
passages.vernacular: 咦,葛羅斯特,葛羅斯特,我要同康華爾公爵同佢妻子講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,葛羅斯特,葛羅斯特,我要和康華爾公爵和他妻子說話。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Well, my good lord, I have inform’d them so.
passages.vernacular: 好,我嘅好大人,我已咁樣通知佢哋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我的好大人,我已這樣通知他們了。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Inform’d them!
passages.vernacular: 通知佢哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通知他們!

passages.original: Dost thou understand me, man?
passages.vernacular: 你明白我嘅意思嗎,老兄?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你明白我的意思嗎,老兄?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Ay, my good lord.
passages.vernacular: 係,我嘅好大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,我的好大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: The King would speak with Cornwall; the dear father Would with his daughter speak, commands, tends, service, Are they inform’d of this?
passages.vernacular: 國王要同康華爾講話;親愛嘅父親要同佢嘅女兒講話,命令、期待、服務,佢哋被告知呢啲咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王要和康華爾說話;親愛的父親要和他的女兒說話,命令、期待、服務,他們被告知這些了嗎?

passages.original: My breath and blood! Fiery?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅氣息同血!火暴?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的氣息和血!火暴?

passages.original: The fiery Duke, tell the hot Duke that— No, but not yet:
passages.vernacular: 火暴嘅公爵,告訴嗰熱血嘅公爵:——不,仲不:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火暴的公爵,告訴那熱血的公爵:——不,還不:

passages.original: maybe he is not well: Infirmity doth still neglect all office Whereto our health is bound:
passages.vernacular: 或者佢不舒服:疾病總是忽略我哋健康時所負嘅一切職責:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許他不舒服:疾病總是忽略我們健康時所負的一切職責:

passages.original: we are not ourselves When nature, being oppress’d, commands the mind To suffer with the body:
passages.vernacular: 當自然受壓迫,命令心靈同身體一同受苦時,我哋就唔係自己:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當自然受壓迫,命令心靈與身體一同受苦時,我們就不是自己:

passages.original: I’ll forbear; And am fallen out with my more headier will, To take the indispos’d and sickly fit For the sound man.
passages.vernacular: 我要忍耐;我同自己更急躁嘅意志鬧翻喇,竟把不舒服嘅病態當成健康嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要忍耐;我與自己更急躁的意志鬧翻了,竟把不舒服的病態當成健康的人。

passages.original: [Looking on Kent.]
passages.vernacular: [睇住肯特。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [看著肯特。]

passages.original: Death on my state!
passages.vernacular: 死亡降喺我嘅身份上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 死亡降在我的身份上!

passages.original: Wherefore Should he sit here?
passages.vernacular: 點解佢要坐喺呢度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼他要坐在這裡?

passages.original: This act persuades me That this remotion of the Duke and her Is practice only.
passages.vernacular: 呢個舉動使我確信公爵同佢嘅呢次離開不過係詭計。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個舉動使我確信公爵和她的這次離開不過是詭計。

passages.original: Give me my servant forth.
passages.vernacular: 把我嘅僕人放出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把我的僕人放出來。

passages.original: Go tell the Duke and’s wife I’d speak with them, Now, presently:
passages.vernacular: 去告訴公爵同佢妻子,我要同佢哋講話,而家,即刻:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去告訴公爵和他妻子,我要和他們說話,現在,立刻:

passages.original: bid them come forth and hear me, Or at their chamber door I’ll beat the drum Till it cry sleep to death.
passages.vernacular: 叫佢哋出嚟聽我講,否則我就喺佢哋房門口擂鼓,直到把瞓眠吵死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫他們出來聽我說,否則我就在他們房門口擂鼓,直到把睡眠吵死。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I would have all well betwixt you.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你哋之間一切都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你們之間一切都好。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O me, my heart, my rising heart! But down!
passages.vernacular: 啊我,我嘅心,我上升嘅心!下去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我,我的心,我上升的心!下去!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Cry to it, nuncle, as the cockney did to the eels when she put ’em i’ the paste alive;
passages.vernacular: 對佢喊,叔叔,就像嗰個倫敦女人把活鰻魚放進麵團時對牠哋喊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對它喊,叔叔,就像那個倫敦女人把活鰻魚放進麵團時對牠們喊:

passages.original: she knapped ’em o’ the coxcombs with a stick and cried ‘Down, wantons, down!’
passages.vernacular: 佢用棍子敲牠哋嘅頭,喊「下去,放蕩嘅嘢,下去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用棍子敲牠們的頭,喊「下去,放蕩的東西,下去!」

passages.original: ’Twas her brother that, in pure kindness to his horse buttered his hay.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係佢嘅哥哥,出於對馬嘅純粹好意,畀乾草塗上奶油。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是她的哥哥,出於對馬的純粹好意,給乾草塗上奶油。

passages.original: Enter Cornwall, Regan, Gloucester and Servants.
passages.vernacular: [康華爾、里根、葛羅斯特同僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [康華爾、里根、葛羅斯特和僕人們上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Good morrow to you both.
passages.vernacular: 早安,兩位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,兩位。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Hail to your grace!
passages.vernacular: 向殿下致敬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向殿下致敬!

passages.original: [Kent here set at liberty.]
passages.vernacular: [肯特喺此被釋放。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特在此被釋放。]

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: I am glad to see your highness.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興見到殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興見到殿下。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Regan, I think you are; I know what reason I have to think so:
passages.vernacular: 里根,我想你係嘅;我知道我有乜嘢理由咁樣想:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 里根,我想你是的;我知道我有什麼理由這樣想:

passages.original: if thou shouldst not be glad, I would divorce me from thy mother’s tomb, Sepulchring an adultress.
passages.vernacular: 如果你不高興,我就要同你母親嘅墳墓離婚,因為埋咗一個通姦者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你不高興,我就要和你母親的墳墓離婚,因為埋了一個通姦者。

passages.original: [To Kent] O, are you free?
passages.vernacular: [對肯特]啊,你自由喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對肯特]啊,你自由了?

passages.original: Some other time for that.—Beloved Regan, Thy sister’s naught:
passages.vernacular: 以後再講嗰個。——親愛嘅里根,你姊姊不行:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以後再說那個。——親愛的里根,你姊姊不行:

passages.original: O Regan, she hath tied Sharp-tooth’d unkindness, like a vulture, here.
passages.vernacular: 啊里根,佢喺呢度綁咗一隻尖牙嘅無情,像禿鷹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊里根,她在這裡綁了一隻尖牙的無情,像禿鷹。

passages.original: [Points to his heart.]
passages.vernacular: [指住心。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [指著心。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I can scarce speak to thee; thou’lt not believe With how deprav’d a quality—O Regan!
passages.vernacular: 我幾乎對你講不出嚟;你唔會相信佢品性幾咁敗壞——啊里根!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾乎對你說不出來;你不會相信她品性多麼敗壞——啊里根!

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: I pray you, sir, take patience.
passages.vernacular: 請你,先生,耐心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,先生,耐心。

passages.original: I have hope You less know how to value her desert Than she to scant her duty.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你係唔知道點樣珍惜佢嘅功德,而唔係佢吝嗇咗佢嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你是不知道怎樣珍惜她的功德,而不是她吝嗇了她的責任。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Say, how is that?
passages.vernacular: 講,點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說,怎麼說?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: I cannot think my sister in the least Would fail her obligation.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠想像我姊姊喺最小嘅事上會缺少佢嘅義務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能想像我姊姊在最小的事上會缺少她的義務。

passages.original: If, sir, perchance She have restrain’d the riots of your followers, ’Tis on such ground, and to such wholesome end, As clears her from all blame.
passages.vernacular: 如果,先生,佢碰巧約束咗您隨從嘅放蕩,嗰都係基於咁樣嘅理由、為咁樣有益嘅目的,足以使佢免受一切責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果,先生,她碰巧約束了您隨從的放蕩,那也是基於這樣的理由、為這樣有益的目的,足以使她免受一切責備。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: My curses on her.
passages.vernacular: 我詛咒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我詛咒她。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: O, sir, you are old; Nature in you stands on the very verge Of her confine:
passages.vernacular: 啊,先生,您老喇;自然喺您身上正站喺佢界限嘅邊緣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,先生,您老了;自然在您身上正站在她界限的邊緣:

passages.original: you should be rul’d and led By some discretion, that discerns your state Better than you yourself.
passages.vernacular: 您應該受某種審慎嘅人嘅規範同引導,佢比您自己更了解您嘅處境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您應該受某種審慎的人的規範與引導,他比您自己更了解您的處境。

passages.original: Therefore I pray you, That to our sister you do make return;
passages.vernacular: 所以我請求您,回到我姊姊嗰度去;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我請求您,回到我姊姊那裡去;

passages.original: Say you have wrong’d her, sir.
passages.vernacular: 講您冤枉咗佢,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說您冤枉了她,先生。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Ask her forgiveness?
passages.vernacular: 向佢請求寬恕?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向她請求寬恕?

passages.original: Do you but mark how this becomes the house?
passages.vernacular: 你只管睇睇呢喺呢家裡幾咁得體?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只管看看這在這家裡多麼得體?

passages.original: ‘Dear daughter, I confess that I am old; [Kneeling.]
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅女兒,我承認我老喇;[跪下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的女兒,我承認我老了;[跪下。]

passages.original: Age is unnecessary: on my knees I beg That you’ll vouchsafe me raiment, bed, and food.’
passages.vernacular: 老年係多餘嘅:我跪住求你,賜我衣服、床同食物。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老年是多餘的:我跪著求你,賜我衣服、床和食物。」

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Good sir, no more!
passages.vernacular: 好先生,唔好再講喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好先生,別再說了!

passages.original: These are unsightly tricks: Return you to my sister.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲係難睇嘅把戲:回到我姊姊嗰度去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些是難看的把戲:回到我姊姊那裡去。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: [Rising.]
passages.vernacular: [起身。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [起身。]

passages.original: Never, Regan: She hath abated me of half my train;
passages.vernacular: 永不,里根:佢削減咗我一半嘅隨從;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永不,里根:她削減了我一半的隨從;

passages.original: Look’d black upon me; struck me with her tongue, Most serpent-like, upon the very heart.
passages.vernacular: 對我黑住臉;用佢嘅舌頭打擊我,像蛇一樣,正打喺心上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我黑著臉;用她的舌頭打擊我,像蛇一樣,正打在心上。

passages.original: All the stor’d vengeances of heaven fall On her ingrateful top!
passages.vernacular: 願天上所有儲存嘅報復都降喺佢忘恩負義嘅頭上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願天上所有儲存的報復都降在她忘恩負義的頭上!

passages.original: Strike her young bones, You taking airs, with lameness!
passages.vernacular: 你哋呢啲吹毒氣嘅,用跛足擊打佢年輕嘅骨頭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們這些吹毒氣的,用跛足擊打她年輕的骨頭!

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Fie, sir, fie!
passages.vernacular: 呸,先生,呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,先生,呸!

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: You nimble lightnings, dart your blinding flames Into her scornful eyes!
passages.vernacular: 你哋呢啲敏捷嘅閃電,把你哋使人盲目的火焰射進佢輕蔑嘅眼睛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們這些敏捷的閃電,把你們使人盲目的火焰射進她輕蔑的眼睛!

passages.original: Infect her beauty, You fen-suck’d fogs, drawn by the powerful sun, To fall and blast her pride!
passages.vernacular: 你哋呢啲被強大太陽吸起嘅沼澤霧氣,降下嚟玷污佢嘅美貌,摧毀佢嘅驕傲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們這些被強大太陽吸起的沼澤霧氣,降下來玷污她的美貌,摧毀她的驕傲!

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: O the blest gods!
passages.vernacular: 啊,有福嘅諸神!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,有福的諸神!

passages.original: So will you wish on me when the rash mood is on.
passages.vernacular: 等你喺衝動嘅情緒中,你都會咁樣咒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等你在衝動的情緒中,你也會這樣咒我。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No, Regan, thou shalt never have my curse.
passages.vernacular: 不,里根,你永遠唔會得到我嘅詛咒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,里根,你永遠不會得到我的詛咒。

passages.original: Thy tender-hefted nature shall not give Thee o’er to harshness.
passages.vernacular: 你溫柔嘅天性唔會使你轉為苛刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你溫柔的天性不會使你轉為苛刻。

passages.original: Her eyes are fierce; but thine Do comfort, and not burn.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛兇猛;但你嘅眼睛使人安慰,不灼人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛兇猛;但你的眼睛使人安慰,不灼人。

passages.original: ’Tis not in thee To grudge my pleasures, to cut off my train, To bandy hasty words, to scant my sizes, And, in conclusion, to oppose the bolt Against my coming in.
passages.vernacular: 你唔會吝嗇我嘅樂趣,削減我嘅隨從,頂嘴講急躁嘅話,減少我嘅份額,最終用門閂擋住我進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會吝嗇我的樂趣,削減我的隨從,頂嘴說急躁的話,減少我的份額,最終用門閂擋住我進來。

passages.original: Thou better know’st The offices of nature, bond of childhood, Effects of courtesy, dues of gratitude;
passages.vernacular: 你更懂得天性嘅義務、孩童嘅紐帶、禮貌嘅作用、感恩嘅責任:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你更懂得天性的義務、孩童的紐帶、禮貌的作用、感恩的責任:

passages.original: Thy half o’ the kingdom hast thou not forgot, Wherein I thee endow’d.
passages.vernacular: 我分畀你嘅嗰一半王國,你冇忘記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我分給你的那一半王國,你沒有忘記。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Good sir, to the purpose.
passages.vernacular: 好先生,講正題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好先生,說正題。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Who put my man i’ the stocks?
passages.vernacular: 邊個把我嘅人放進木枷?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰把我的人放進木枷?

passages.original: [Tucket within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: What trumpet’s that?
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係乜嘢號角?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是什麼號角?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: I know’t, my sister’s: this approves her letter, That she would soon be here.
passages.vernacular: 我知道,係我姊姊嘅:呢證實佢嘅信,講佢好快就到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道,是我姊姊的:這證實她的信,說她很快就到。

passages.original: Enter Oswald.
passages.vernacular: [奧斯華上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧斯華上。]

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Is your lady come?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅夫人嚟咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的夫人來了嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: This is a slave, whose easy borrowed pride Dwells in the fickle grace of her he follows.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個奴才,佢輕易借嚟嘅驕傲,依存於佢所追隨者善變嘅恩寵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個奴才,他輕易借來的驕傲,依存於他所追隨者善變的恩寵。

passages.original: Out, varlet, from my sight!
passages.vernacular: 滾,無賴,離開我嘅視線!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾,無賴,離開我的視線!

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: What means your grace?
passages.vernacular: 殿下係乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下是什麼意思?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Who stock’d my servant?
passages.vernacular: 邊個把我嘅僕人鎖進木枷?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰把我的僕人鎖進木枷?

passages.original: Regan, I have good hope Thou didst not know on’t.
passages.vernacular: 里根,我好希望你唔知道呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 里根,我很希望你不知道這件事。

passages.original: Who comes here? O heavens!
passages.vernacular: 邊個嚟喇?啊天啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰來了?啊天啊!

passages.original: Enter Goneril.
passages.vernacular: [高納麗上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [高納麗上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: If you do love old men, if your sweet sway Allow obedience, if yourselves are old, Make it your cause;
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋愛老人,如果你哋甜美嘅統治容許服從,如果你哋自己都老,就把呢作為你哋嘅事業;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們愛老人,如果你們甜美的統治容許服從,如果你們自己也老,就把這作為你們的事業;

passages.original: send down, and take my part!
passages.vernacular: 派下(諸神)嚟,站喺我呢邊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 派下(諸神)來,站在我這邊!

passages.original: [To Goneril.]
passages.vernacular: [對高納麗。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對高納麗。]

passages.original: Art not asham’d to look upon this beard?
passages.vernacular: 你睇呢把鬍子,不覺得羞恥嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看這把鬍子,不覺得羞恥嗎?

passages.original: O Regan, wilt thou take her by the hand?
passages.vernacular: 啊里根,你要牽佢嘅手嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊里根,你要牽她的手嗎?

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Why not by the hand, sir?
passages.vernacular: 點解不牽手,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼不牽手,先生?

passages.original: How have I offended?
passages.vernacular: 我邊度冒犯喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我哪裡冒犯了?

passages.original: All’s not offence that indiscretion finds And dotage terms so.
passages.vernacular: 唔係所有輕率發現、老年昏聵稱為過錯嘅都係冒犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是所有輕率發現、老年昏聵稱為過錯的都是冒犯。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O sides, you are too tough!
passages.vernacular: 啊,肋骨,你哋太堅韌喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,肋骨,你們太堅韌了!

passages.original: Will you yet hold?
passages.vernacular: 你哋仲撐得住嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們還撐得住嗎?

passages.original: How came my man i’ the stocks?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅人點會喺木枷裡?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的人怎麼會在木枷裡?

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: I set him there, sir: but his own disorders Deserv’d much less advancement.
passages.vernacular: 係我放佢喺嗰度嘅,先生:但佢自己嘅放肆配不上更高嘅待遇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我放他在那裡的,先生:但他自己的放肆配不上更高的待遇。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: You? Did you?
passages.vernacular: 你?係你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你?是你?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: I pray you, father, being weak, seem so.
passages.vernacular: 請你,父親,既然軟弱,就顯得軟弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,父親,既然軟弱,就顯得軟弱。

passages.original: If, till the expiration of your month, You will return and sojourn with my sister, Dismissing half your train, come then to me:
passages.vernacular: 如果,喺你嘅月份期滿之前,你回嚟住喺我姊姊嗰兒,辭退一半隨從,然後來我呢度:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果,在你的月份期滿之前,你回來住在我姊姊那兒,辭退一半隨從,然後來我這裡:

passages.original: I am now from home, and out of that provision Which shall be needful for your entertainment.
passages.vernacular: 我而家不喺家,都冇為款待你所需嘅準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在不在家,也沒有為款待你所需的準備。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Return to her, and fifty men dismiss’d?
passages.vernacular: 回到佢嗰度,辭退五十個人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回到她那裡,辭退五十個人?

passages.original: No, rather I abjure all roofs, and choose To wage against the enmity o’ the air;
passages.vernacular: 不,我寧願放棄所有屋頂,選擇同空氣嘅敵意抗爭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我寧願放棄所有屋頂,選擇與空氣的敵意抗爭;

passages.original: To be a comrade with the wolf and owl, Necessity’s sharp pinch!
passages.vernacular: 同狼同貓頭鷹為伴,必要嘅尖銳煎熬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 與狼和貓頭鷹為伴,必要的尖銳煎熬!

passages.original: Return with her?
passages.vernacular: 跟佢回去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟她回去?

passages.original: Why, the hot-blooded France, that dowerless took Our youngest born, I could as well be brought To knee his throne, and, squire-like, pension beg To keep base life afoot.
passages.vernacular: 咦,嗰熱血嘅法蘭西,唔好嫁妝娶咗我哋嘅幼女,我寧可去跪喺佢嘅寶座前,像侍從一樣乞討津貼嚟維持卑賤嘅生命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,那熱血的法蘭西,不要嫁妝娶了我們的幼女,我寧可去跪在他的寶座前,像侍從一樣乞討津貼來維持卑賤的生命。

passages.original: Return with her?
passages.vernacular: 跟佢回去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟她回去?

passages.original: Persuade me rather to be slave and sumpter To this detested groom.
passages.vernacular: 勸我寧可做呢個可憎馬夫嘅奴隸同馱獸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勸我寧可做這個可憎馬夫的奴隸和馱獸。

passages.original: [Pointing to Oswald.]
passages.vernacular: [指住奧斯華。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [指著奧斯華。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: At your choice, sir.
passages.vernacular: 隨您選擇,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨您選擇,先生。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I prythee, daughter, do not make me mad: I will not trouble thee, my child;
passages.vernacular: 我請求你,女兒,唔好畀我發瘋:我不麻煩你,我嘅細路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請求你,女兒,別讓我發瘋:我不麻煩你,我的孩子;

passages.original: farewell: We’ll no more meet, no more see one another.
passages.vernacular: 再見:我哋唔會再見面,唔會再互相見到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見:我們不會再見面,不會再互相見到。

passages.original: But yet thou art my flesh, my blood, my daughter;
passages.vernacular: 但你仍係我嘅肉、我嘅血、我嘅女兒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你仍是我的肉、我的血、我的女兒;

passages.original: Or rather a disease that’s in my flesh, Which I must needs call mine.
passages.vernacular: 或者講係我肉裡嘅一種病,我唔得不稱之為我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者說是我肉裡的一種病,我不得不稱之為我的。

passages.original: Thou art a boil, A plague sore, or embossed carbuncle In my corrupted blood.
passages.vernacular: 你係個癤子,瘟疫瘡,或隆起嘅癰,喺我腐敗嘅血液中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個癤子,瘟疫瘡,或隆起的癰,在我腐敗的血液中。

passages.original: But I’ll not chide thee; Let shame come when it will, I do not call it:
passages.vernacular: 但我不責備你;讓羞恥喺佢想嚟嘅時候嚟,我不召喚佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不責備你;讓羞恥在它想來的時候來,我不召喚它:

passages.original: I do not bid the thunder-bearer shoot, Nor tell tales of thee to high-judging Jove:
passages.vernacular: 我不叫執雷霆者射擊,都不向審判高處嘅朱庇特告你嘅狀:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不叫執雷霆者射擊,也不向審判高處的朱庇特告你的狀:

passages.original: Mend when thou canst; be better at thy leisure:
passages.vernacular: 你能改時就改;你有空時變好:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能改時就改;你有空時變好:

passages.original: I can be patient; I can stay with Regan, I and my hundred knights.
passages.vernacular: 我可以忍耐;我可以同里根住,我同我嘅一百名騎士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以忍耐;我可以和里根住,我和我的一百名騎士。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Not altogether so, I look’d not for you yet, nor am provided For your fit welcome.
passages.vernacular: 不完全係咁樣,我仲冇預期您,都冇為您恰當嘅歡迎作準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不完全是這樣,我還沒預期您,也沒有為您恰當的歡迎作準備。

passages.original: Give ear, sir, to my sister; For those that mingle reason with your passion Must be content to think you old, and so— But she knows what she does.
passages.vernacular: 請聽我姊姊嘅話,先生;因為嗰啲把理智摻入您嘅激情嘅人,必須甘心認為您老喇,所以——但佢知道佢喺做乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請聽我姊姊的話,先生;因為那些把理智摻入您的激情的人,必須甘心認為您老了,所以——但她知道她在做什麼。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Is this well spoken?
passages.vernacular: 呢話講得好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這話說得好嗎?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: I dare avouch it, sir: what, fifty followers?
passages.vernacular: 我敢保證,先生:乜嘢,五十個隨從?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢保證,先生:什麼,五十個隨從?

passages.original: Is it not well?
passages.vernacular: 不好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不好嗎?

passages.original: What should you need of more?
passages.vernacular: 您仲需要更多做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您還需要更多做什麼?

passages.original: Yea, or so many, sith that both charge and danger Speak ’gainst so great a number?
passages.vernacular: 係啊,甚至咁多,既然費用同危險都反對咁大嘅數目?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,甚至這麼多,既然費用和危險都反對這麼大的數目?

passages.original: How in one house Should many people, under two commands, Hold amity?
passages.vernacular: 一座房子裡,兩個指揮下嘅許多人,怎能保持和睦?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一座房子裡,兩個指揮下的許多人,怎能保持和睦?

passages.original: ’Tis hard; almost impossible.
passages.vernacular: 好難;幾乎唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很難;幾乎不可能。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Why might not you, my lord, receive attendance From those that she calls servants, or from mine?
passages.vernacular: 大人,您點解唔能夠接受佢稱為僕人嘅人或我嘅人嘅侍候?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,您為什麼不能接受她稱為僕人的人或我的人的侍候?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Why not, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 點解不行,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼不行,大人?

passages.original: If then they chanc’d to slack ye, We could control them.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋偶然怠慢咗您,我哋可以管束佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們偶然怠慢了您,我們可以管束他們。

passages.original: If you will come to me,— For now I spy a danger,—I entreat you To bring but five-and-twenty:
passages.vernacular: 如果您到我呢度嚟——因為而家我睇到一種危險——我請求您只帶二十五個人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您到我這裡來——因為現在我看到一種危險——我請求您只帶二十五個人:

passages.original: to no more Will I give place or notice.
passages.vernacular: 超過呢個數目,我不畀住處或留意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 超過這個數目,我不給住處或留意。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I gave you all,—
passages.vernacular: 我把一切都畀咗你哋——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把一切都給了你們——

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: And in good time you gave it.
passages.vernacular: 而且畀得正是時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且給得正是時候。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Made you my guardians, my depositaries; But kept a reservation to be followed With such a number.
passages.vernacular: 讓你哋做我嘅監護人、保管人;但保留咗要由咁多隨從跟隨嘅條件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓你們做我的監護人、保管人;但保留了要由這麼多隨從跟隨的條件。

passages.original: What, must I come to you With five-and-twenty, Regan, said you so?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我必須帶住二十五個人嚟你呢度,里根,你咁講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我必須帶著二十五個人來你這裡,里根,你這麼說?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: And speak’t again my lord; no more with me.
passages.vernacular: 我再講一次,大人;唔能夠多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再說一次,大人;不能多了。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Those wicked creatures yet do look well-favour’d When others are more wicked;
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲邪惡嘅生物,當別人更邪惡時,仍顯得好睇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些邪惡的生物,當別人更邪惡時,仍顯得好看;

passages.original: not being the worst Stands in some rank of praise.
passages.vernacular: 唔係最壞嘅,就能得到啲讚賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是最壞的,就能得到一些讚賞。

passages.original: [To Goneril.]
passages.vernacular: [對高納麗。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對高納麗。]

passages.original: I’ll go with thee: Thy fifty yet doth double five-and-twenty, And thou art twice her love.
passages.vernacular: 我跟你去:你嘅五十仍係二十五嘅兩倍,你嘅愛係佢嘅兩倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟你去:你的五十仍是二十五的兩倍,你的愛是她的兩倍。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Hear me, my lord: What need you five-and-twenty? Ten? Or five?
passages.vernacular: 聽我講,大人:您需要二十五個做乜嘢?十個?或五個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽我說,大人:您需要二十五個做什麼?十個?或五個?

passages.original: To follow in a house where twice so many Have a command to tend you?
passages.vernacular: 喺一座有雙倍人手受命侍候您嘅房子裡跟隨您?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一座有雙倍人手受命侍候您的房子裡跟隨您?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: What need one?
passages.vernacular: 一個人需要乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人需要什麼?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O, reason not the need: our basest beggars Are in the poorest thing superfluous:
passages.vernacular: 啊,別論需要:我哋最卑賤嘅乞丐喺最窮嘅嘢上都有多餘:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,別論需要:我們最卑賤的乞丐在最窮的東西上也有多餘:

passages.original: Allow not nature more than nature needs, Man’s life is cheap as beast’s.
passages.vernacular: 不許自然多於自然所需,人嘅生命就同野獸嘅一樣便宜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不許自然多於自然所需,人的生命就和野獸的一樣便宜。

passages.original: Thou art a lady; If only to go warm were gorgeous, Why, nature needs not what thou gorgeous wear’st Which scarcely keeps thee warm.
passages.vernacular: 你係位夫人;如果只為保暖就算華麗,咦,自然並不需要你所穿戴嘅華麗,佢幾乎唔能夠使你保暖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是位夫人;如果只為保暖就算華麗,咦,自然並不需要你所穿戴的華麗,它幾乎不能使你保暖。

passages.original: But, for true need,— You heavens, give me that patience, patience I need!
passages.vernacular: 但講到真正嘅需要——你哋諸天,賜我耐心,我需要耐心!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但說到真正的需要——你們諸天,賜我耐心,我需要耐心!

passages.original: You see me here, you gods, a poor old man, As full of grief as age; wretched in both!
passages.vernacular: 你哋睇,諸神,我係個可憐嘅老人,充滿悲傷,正如充滿年歲;兩者都悲慘!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們看,諸神,我是個可憐的老人,充滿悲傷,正如充滿年歲;兩者都悲慘!

passages.original: If it be you that stirs these daughters’ hearts Against their father, fool me not so much To bear it tamely;
passages.vernacular: 如果係你哋煽動呢啲女兒嘅心嚟反對佢哋嘅父親,別咁樣愚弄我,讓我溫順地忍受;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是你們煽動這些女兒的心來反對她們的父親,別這樣愚弄我,讓我溫順地忍受;

passages.original: touch me with noble anger, And let not women’s weapons, water-drops, Stain my man’s cheeks!
passages.vernacular: 用高貴嘅憤怒觸動我,唔好畀女人嘅武器,水滴,玷污我男子漢嘅臉頰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用高貴的憤怒觸動我,別讓女人的武器,水滴,玷污我男子漢的臉頰!

passages.original: No, you unnatural hags, I will have such revenges on you both That all the world shall,—I will do such things,— What they are yet, I know not;
passages.vernacular: 不,你哋呢啲不自然嘅老妖婦,我要對你哋兩個進行咁樣嘅報復,使全世界都將——我要做咁樣嘅事——佢哋係乜嘢我仲唔知道;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,你們這些不自然的老妖婦,我要對你們兩個進行這樣的報復,使全世界都將——我要做這樣的事——它們是什麼我還不知道;

passages.original: but they shall be The terrors of the earth.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋將成為大地嘅恐怖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們將成為大地的恐怖。

passages.original: You think I’ll weep; No, I’ll not weep:— [Storm and tempest.]
passages.vernacular: 你哋以為我會哭;不,我不哭:——[暴風雨。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們以為我會哭;不,我不哭:——[暴風雨。]

passages.original: I have full cause of weeping; but this heart Shall break into a hundred thousand flaws Or ere I’ll weep.—O fool, I shall go mad!
passages.vernacular: 我有充分嘅理由哭;但呢顆心要碎成十萬片,我才哭。——啊弄臣,我要發瘋喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有充分的理由哭;但這顆心要碎成十萬片,我才哭。——啊弄臣,我要發瘋了!

passages.original: [Exeunt Lear, Gloucester, Kent and Fool.]
passages.vernacular: [李爾、葛羅斯特、肯特同弄臣下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾、葛羅斯特、肯特和弄臣下。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Let us withdraw; ’twill be a storm.
passages.vernacular: 我哋退下吧;要有暴風雨喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們退下吧;要有暴風雨了。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: This house is little: the old man and his people Cannot be well bestow’d.
passages.vernacular: 呢房子小:老人同佢嘅人無法好好安置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這房子小:老人和他的人無法好好安置。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: ’Tis his own blame; hath put himself from rest And must needs taste his folly.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係佢自己嘅錯;自己離開咗安寧,必須嚐到自己愚蠢嘅後果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是他自己的錯;自己離開了安寧,必須嚐到自己愚蠢的後果。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: For his particular, I’ll receive him gladly, But not one follower.
passages.vernacular: 就佢個人而言,我會歡迎佢,但一個隨從都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就他個人而言,我會歡迎他,但一個隨從都不行。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: So am I purpos’d.
passages.vernacular: 我都咁樣打算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這樣打算。

passages.original: Where is my lord of Gloucester?
passages.vernacular: 葛羅斯特大人喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛羅斯特大人在哪裡?

passages.original: Enter Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特上。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Followed the old man forth, he is return’d.
passages.vernacular: 跟住老人出去喇,佢回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟著老人出去了,他回來了。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: The King is in high rage.
passages.vernacular: 國王大怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王大怒。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Whither is he going?
passages.vernacular: 佢去邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他去哪?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: He calls to horse; but will I know not whither.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫備馬;但去邊我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他叫備馬;但去哪我不知道。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: ’Tis best to give him way; he leads himself.
passages.vernacular: 最好讓佢走;佢自己領路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最好讓他走;他自己領路。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: My lord, entreat him by no means to stay.
passages.vernacular: 大人,千萬別勸佢留下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,千萬別勸他留下。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Alack, the night comes on, and the high winds Do sorely ruffle;
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,夜晚來臨,大風猛烈地翻騰;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,夜晚來臨,大風猛烈地翻騰;

passages.original: for many miles about There’s scarce a bush.
passages.vernacular: 方圓數里幾乎冇一叢灌木。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 方圓數里幾乎沒有一叢灌木。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: O, sir, to wilful men The injuries that they themselves procure Must be their schoolmasters.
passages.vernacular: 啊,先生,對任性嘅人,佢哋自己招嚟嘅傷害必須成為佢哋嘅老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,先生,對任性的人,他們自己招來的傷害必須成為他們的老師。

passages.original: Shut up your doors.
passages.vernacular: 關上你嘅門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關上你的門。

passages.original: He is attended with a desperate train, And what they may incense him to, being apt To have his ear abus’d, wisdom bids fear.
passages.vernacular: 佢帶住一夥亡命之徒,佢哋可能煽動佢做乜嘢,佢又易於被耳語所誤,智慧叫人害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他帶著一夥亡命之徒,他們可能煽動他做什麼,他又易於被耳語所誤,智慧叫人害怕。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Shut up your doors, my lord; ’tis a wild night.
passages.vernacular: 關上你嘅門,大人;呢個係個狂野嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關上你的門,大人;這是個狂野的夜晚。

passages.original: My Regan counsels well: come out o’ the storm.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅里根勸得好:到風暴外面嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的里根勸得好:到風暴外面來。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene I — A Heath 第三幕第一場:荒野

passages.original: A storm with thunder and lightning. Enter Kent and a Gentleman, severally.
passages.vernacular: [暴風雨,雷電交加。肯特同一位紳士分別上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [暴風雨,雷電交加。肯特和一位紳士分別上。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Who’s there, besides foul weather?
passages.vernacular: 除咗惡劣天氣,嗰邊係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了惡劣天氣,那邊是誰?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: One minded like the weather, most unquietly.
passages.vernacular: 一個像天氣一樣心緒、極不安寧嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個像天氣一樣心緒、極不安寧的人。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I know you.
passages.vernacular: 我認得你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認得你。

passages.original: Where’s the King?
passages.vernacular: 國王喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王在哪裡?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: Contending with the fretful elements; Bids the wind blow the earth into the sea, Or swell the curled waters ’bove the main, That things might change or cease;
passages.vernacular: 正同暴躁嘅元素搏鬥;叫風把大地吹進海裡,或讓捲曲嘅水浪漲過陸地,使萬物改變或終止;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正與暴躁的元素搏鬥;叫風把大地吹進海裡,或讓捲曲的水浪漲過陸地,使萬物改變或終止;

passages.original: tears his white hair, Which the impetuous blasts with eyeless rage, Catch in their fury and make nothing of;
passages.vernacular: 扯住佢嘅白髮,嗰猛烈嘅狂風以盲目的怒氣抓住佢,喺狂怒中不當一回事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 扯著他的白髮,那猛烈的狂風以盲目的怒氣抓住它,在狂怒中不當一回事;

passages.original: Strives in his little world of man to outscorn The to-and-fro-conflicting wind and rain.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢渺小嘅人類世界裡努力蔑視嗰嚟回衝突嘅風同雨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他渺小的人類世界裡努力蔑視那來回衝突的風和雨。

passages.original: This night, wherein the cub-drawn bear would couch, The lion and the belly-pinched wolf Keep their fur dry, unbonneted he runs, And bids what will take all.
passages.vernacular: 今夜,連被幼崽拖累嘅母熊都會蜷縮,獅子同飢餓嘅狼都保持毛皮乾燥,佢卻不戴帽子奔跑,叫一切都嚟吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今夜,連被幼崽拖累的母熊都會蜷縮,獅子和飢餓的狼都保持毛皮乾燥,他卻不戴帽子奔跑,叫一切都來吧。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: But who is with him?
passages.vernacular: 但邊個同佢喺一起?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但誰和他在一起?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: None but the fool, who labours to out-jest His heart-struck injuries.
passages.vernacular: 只有弄臣,佢努力用玩笑抵消被刺中心嘅傷害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有弄臣,他努力用玩笑抵消被刺中心的傷害。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Sir, I do know you; And dare, upon the warrant of my note Commend a dear thing to you.
passages.vernacular: 先生,我確實認識您;我敢憑我嘅觀察,把一件珍貴嘅事託付畀您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我確實認識您;我敢憑我的觀察,把一件珍貴的事託付給您。

passages.original: There is division, Although as yet the face of it be cover’d With mutual cunning, ’twixt Albany and Cornwall;
passages.vernacular: 奧本尼同康華爾之間有分歧,雖然目前表面仲被彼此嘅狡詐掩蓋住;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧本尼與康華爾之間有分歧,雖然目前表面還被彼此的狡詐掩蓋著;

passages.original: Who have, as who have not, that their great stars Throne’d and set high;
passages.vernacular: 佢哋,像所有有高位嘅人一樣,被佢哋嘅大星座登上寶座高高放置;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們,像所有有高位的人一樣,被他們的大星座登上寶座高高放置;

passages.original: servants, who seem no less, Which are to France the spies and speculations Intelligent of our state.
passages.vernacular: 有僕人,睇似如此,卻係法蘭西嘅密探同眼線,通曉我哋嘅國情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有僕人,看似如此,卻是法蘭西的密探與眼線,通曉我們的國情。

passages.original: What hath been seen, Either in snuffs and packings of the Dukes;
passages.vernacular: 所見到嘅,無論係公爵哋嘅生氣同串謀;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所見到的,無論是公爵們的生氣與串謀;

passages.original: Or the hard rein which both of them have borne Against the old kind King;
passages.vernacular: 或兩人對年老善良國王所施加嘅嚴厲約束;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或兩人對年老善良國王所施加的嚴厲約束;

passages.original: or something deeper, Whereof, perchance, these are but furnishings;— But, true it is, from France there comes a power Into this scatter’d kingdom;
passages.vernacular: 或更深嘅事,呢啲或者只係其陳設;——但確實,有一支軍隊從法蘭西嚟到呢個分裂嘅王國;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或更深的事,這些也許只是其陳設;——但確實,有一支軍隊從法蘭西來到這個分裂的王國;

passages.original: who already, Wise in our negligence, have secret feet In some of our best ports, and are at point To show their open banner.—Now to you:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋已經睇準我哋嘅疏忽,喺我哋啲最好嘅港口有祕密嘅立足點,並即將舉起公開嘅旗幟。——而家講到您:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們已經看準我們的疏忽,在我們一些最好的港口有祕密的立足點,並即將舉起公開的旗幟。——現在說到您:

passages.original: If on my credit you dare build so far To make your speed to Dover, you shall find Some that will thank you making just report Of how unnatural and bemadding sorrow The King hath cause to plain.
passages.vernacular: 如果您敢憑我嘅信用,築得咁遠,趕去多佛,您會發現有人會感謝您如實報告國王有理由控訴嘅係點樣不自然、令人發瘋嘅悲痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您敢憑我的信用,築得這麼遠,趕去多佛,您會發現有人會感謝您如實報告國王有理由控訴的是怎樣不自然、令人發瘋的悲痛。

passages.original: I am a gentleman of blood and breeding; And from some knowledge and assurance Offer this office to you.
passages.vernacular: 我係個有血統、有教養嘅紳士;憑啲了解同把握,把呢個任務託付畀您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是個有血統、有教養的紳士;憑一些了解與把握,把這個任務託付給您。

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: I will talk further with you.
passages.vernacular: 我要同您再多談談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要和您再多談談。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: No, do not.
passages.vernacular: 不,別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,別。

passages.original: For confirmation that I am much more Than my out-wall, open this purse, and take What it contains.
passages.vernacular: 為證實我遠比我嘅外表更多,打開呢錢袋,攞走裡面嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為證實我遠比我的外表更多,打開這錢袋,拿走裡面的東西。

passages.original: If you shall see Cordelia, As fear not but you shall, show her this ring;
passages.vernacular: 如果您見到考黛莉亞(您一定會見到,唔使擔心),把呢枚戒指畀佢睇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您見到考黛莉亞(您一定會見到,不必擔心),把這枚戒指給她看;

passages.original: And she will tell you who your fellow is That yet you do not know.
passages.vernacular: 佢會告訴您您仲不認識嘅呢位同伴係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會告訴您您還不認識的這位同伴是誰。

passages.original: Fie on this storm!
passages.vernacular: 呸呢暴風雨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸這暴風雨!

passages.original: I will go seek the King.
passages.vernacular: 我去找國王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去找國王。

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: Give me your hand: have you no more to say?
passages.vernacular: 把手畀我:您冇別嘅要講咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把手給我:您沒有別的要說了嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Few words, but, to effect, more than all yet:
passages.vernacular: 話不多,但就效果而言,比至今所有嘅都多:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 話不多,但就效果而言,比至今所有的都多:

passages.original: That, when we have found the King, in which your pain That way, I’ll this;
passages.vernacular: 就係當我哋找到國王時,您往嗰邊找,我往呢邊找;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是當我們找到國王時,您往那邊找,我往這邊找;

passages.original: he that first lights on him Holla the other.
passages.vernacular: 先找到佢嘅人向另一個呼喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先找到他的人向另一個呼喊。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene II — Another Part of the Heath 第三幕第二場:荒野另一處

passages.original: Storm continues. Enter Lear and Fool.
passages.vernacular: [暴風雨繼續。李爾同弄臣上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [暴風雨繼續。李爾和弄臣上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! Rage! blow!
passages.vernacular: 吹吧,風,把你哋嘅臉頰吹裂!狂怒!吹!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吹吧,風,把你們的臉頰吹裂!狂怒!吹!

passages.original: You cataracts and hurricanoes, spout Till you have drench’d our steeples, drown’d the cocks!
passages.vernacular: 你哋瀑布同颶風,噴湧吧,直到淹沒我哋嘅尖塔,淹死風向雞!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們瀑布和颶風,噴湧吧,直到淹沒我們的尖塔,淹死風向雞!

passages.original: You sulphurous and thought-executing fires, Vaunt-couriers to oak-cleaving thunderbolts, Singe my white head!
passages.vernacular: 你哋含硫磺、迅如思想嘅火焰,劈開橡樹嘅霹靂嘅先鋒,燒焦我嘅白頭吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們含硫磺、迅如思想的火焰,劈開橡樹的霹靂的先鋒,燒焦我的白頭吧!

passages.original: And thou, all-shaking thunder, Strike flat the thick rotundity o’ the world!
passages.vernacular: 仲有你,震撼一切嘅雷,把世界厚厚嘅圓體劈平!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你,震撼一切的雷,把世界厚厚的圓體劈平!

passages.original: Crack nature’s moulds, all germens spill at once, That make ingrateful man!
passages.vernacular: 打碎自然嘅模子,一下子灑盡所有造出忘恩負義嘅人嘅種子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打碎自然的模子,一下子灑盡所有造出忘恩負義的人的種子!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: O nuncle, court holy-water in a dry house is better than this rain-water out o’ door.
passages.vernacular: 啊叔叔,喺乾燥房子裡嘅宮廷聖水,勝過呢門外嘅雨水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊叔叔,在乾燥房子裡的宮廷聖水,勝過這門外的雨水。

passages.original: Good nuncle, in; and ask thy daughters blessing:
passages.vernacular: 好叔叔,進去;向你嘅女兒哋求祝福:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好叔叔,進去;向你的女兒們求祝福:

passages.original: here’s a night pities neither wise men nor fools.
passages.vernacular: 呢夜晚既不憐憫聰明人都不憐憫弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這夜晚既不憐憫聰明人也不憐憫弄臣。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Rumble thy bellyful! Spit, fire!
passages.vernacular: 轟鳴吧,盡你嘅肚子!吐吧,火!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轟鳴吧,盡你的肚子!吐吧,火!

passages.original: spout, rain!
passages.vernacular: 噴吧,雨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 噴吧,雨!

passages.original: Nor rain, wind, thunder, fire are my daughters;
passages.vernacular: 雨、風、雷、火都唔係我嘅女兒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雨、風、雷、火都不是我的女兒;

passages.original: I tax not you, you elements, with unkindness.
passages.vernacular: 元素哋,我不指責你哋無情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 元素們,我不指責你們無情。

passages.original: I never gave you kingdom, call’d you children;
passages.vernacular: 我從未畀你哋王國,叫你哋細路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未給你們王國,叫你們孩子;

passages.original: You owe me no subscription: then let fall Your horrible pleasure.
passages.vernacular: 你哋不欠我臣服:嗰就降下你哋可怕嘅意志吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不欠我臣服:那就降下你們可怕的意志吧。

passages.original: Here I stand your slave, A poor, infirm, weak, and despis’d old man:
passages.vernacular: 我站喺呢度做你哋嘅奴隸,一個可憐、虛弱、被輕視嘅老人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站在這裡做你們的奴隸,一個可憐、虛弱、被輕視的老人:

passages.original: But yet I call you servile ministers, That will with two pernicious daughters join Your high-engender’d battles ’gainst a head So old and white as this! O! O! ’tis foul!
passages.vernacular: 然而我稱你哋為卑賤嘅幫兇,竟同兩個有害嘅女兒聯合,用你哋高處生成嘅戰鬥嚟打一個如此年老白髮嘅頭!啊!啊!太卑鄙喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而我稱你們為卑賤的幫兇,竟與兩個有害的女兒聯合,用你們高處生成的戰鬥來打一個如此年老白髮的頭!啊!啊!太卑鄙了!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: He that has a house to put’s head in has a good head-piece.
passages.vernacular: 有房子放頭嘅人,有個好頭腦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有房子放頭的人,有個好頭腦。

passages.original: The codpiece that will house Before the head has any, The head and he shall louse: So beggars marry many.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會先畀頭顱準備褲襠(護襠)房子嘅人,頭同佢都會生虱子:乞丐就係咁樣結許多次婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會先給頭顱準備褲襠(護襠)房子的人,頭和他都會生虱子:乞丐就是這樣結許多次婚。

passages.original: The man that makes his toe What he his heart should make Shall of a corn cry woe, And turn his sleep to wake.
passages.vernacular: 把腳趾當成該當心嘅人,會為雞眼哭,並把瞓眠變成失眠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把腳趾當成該當心的人,會為雞眼哭,並把睡眠變成失眠。

passages.original: For there was never yet fair woman but she made mouths in a glass.
passages.vernacular: 因為從來冇邊個美麗女人不對鏡子做鬼臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為從來沒有哪個美麗女人不對鏡子做鬼臉。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: No, I will be the pattern of all patience; I will say nothing.
passages.vernacular: 不,我要做一切耐心嘅榜樣;我乜嘢都不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我要做一切耐心的榜樣;我什麼都不說。

passages.original: Enter Kent.
passages.vernacular: [肯特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特上。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Who’s there?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在那裡?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Marry, here’s grace and a codpiece; that’s a wise man and a fool.
passages.vernacular: 嘿,呢度有一位恩典同一個褲襠;嗰個係個聰明人同一個弄臣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘿,這裡有一位恩典和一個褲襠;那是個聰明人和一個弄臣。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Alas, sir, are you here?
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,先生,您喺呢度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,先生,您在這裡嗎?

passages.original: Things that love night Love not such nights as these;
passages.vernacular: 愛夜晚嘅嘢,不愛咁樣嘅夜晚:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛夜晚的東西,不愛這樣的夜晚:

passages.original: the wrathful skies Gallow the very wanderers of the dark, And make them keep their caves.
passages.vernacular: 憤怒嘅天空嚇壞咗黑暗中嘅漫遊者,使佢哋躲喺洞裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憤怒的天空嚇壞了黑暗中的漫遊者,使它們躲在洞裡。

passages.original: Since I was man, Such sheets of fire, such bursts of horrid thunder, Such groans of roaring wind and rain I never Remember to have heard.
passages.vernacular: 自從我成年,咁樣嘅火片,咁樣可怕嘅雷爆,咁樣吼叫嘅風雨呻吟,我都記唔得聽過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我成年,這樣的火片,這樣可怕的雷爆,這樣吼叫的風雨呻吟,我都記不得聽過。

passages.original: Man’s nature cannot carry Th’affliction, nor the fear.
passages.vernacular: 人嘅天性承受不了呢種折磨,都承受不了呢種恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人的天性承受不了這種折磨,也承受不了這種恐懼。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Let the great gods, That keep this dreadful pudder o’er our heads, Find out their enemies now.
passages.vernacular: 讓嗰啲喺我哋頭上製造呢可怕喧鬧嘅偉大諸神,而家找出佢哋嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓那些在我們頭上製造這可怕喧鬧的偉大諸神,現在找出他們的敵人。

passages.original: Tremble, thou wretch, That hast within thee undivulged crimes Unwhipp’d of justice.
passages.vernacular: 顫抖吧,你呢可憐蟲,你心裡有未被正義鞭打嘅、未揭發嘅罪行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顫抖吧,你這可憐蟲,你心裡有未被正義鞭打的、未揭發的罪行。

passages.original: Hide thee, thou bloody hand; Thou perjur’d, and thou simular of virtue That art incestuous.
passages.vernacular: 藏起嚟,你呢沾血嘅手;你呢背誓者,你呢假扮美德嘅亂倫者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 藏起來,你這沾血的手;你這背誓者,你這假扮美德的亂倫者。

passages.original: Caitiff, to pieces shake That under covert and convenient seeming Hast practis’d on man’s life:
passages.vernacular: 顫抖成碎片吧,你呢躲喺隱蔽、方便外表之下對人命下手嘅惡棍:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顫抖成碎片吧,你這躲在隱蔽、方便外表之下對人命下手的惡棍:

passages.original: close pent-up guilts, Rive your concealing continents, and cry These dreadful summoners grace.
passages.vernacular: 緊緊關押嘅罪咎,撕裂你哋掩蓋嘅外殼,向呢啲可怕嘅傳喚者求恩吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 緊緊關押的罪咎,撕裂你們掩蓋的外殼,向這些可怕的傳喚者求恩吧。

passages.original: I am a man More sinn’d against than sinning.
passages.vernacular: 我係一個受罪多於犯罪嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是一個受罪多於犯罪的人。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Alack, bareheaded!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,冇戴帽子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,沒戴帽子!

passages.original: Gracious my lord, hard by here is a hovel; Some friendship will it lend you ’gainst the tempest:
passages.vernacular: 仁慈嘅大人,呢附近有一間茅屋;佢會借畀您啲友誼,抵抗風暴:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仁慈的大人,這附近有一間茅屋;它會借給您一些友誼,抵抗風暴:

passages.original: Repose you there, whilst I to this hard house,— More harder than the stones whereof ’tis rais’d;
passages.vernacular: 您喺嗰兒休息,我去呢座堅硬嘅房子——比建造佢嘅石頭仲堅硬——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您在那兒休息,我去這座堅硬的房子——比建造它的石頭還堅硬——

passages.original: Which even but now, demanding after you, Denied me to come in,—return, and force Their scanted courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 佢頭先我向佢打聽您時,不讓我進去,——我去,回嚟,強迫佢哋吝嗇嘅禮節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它剛才我向它打聽您時,不讓我進去,——我去,回來,強迫它們吝嗇的禮節。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: My wits begin to turn.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅神志開始轉動(混亂)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的神志開始轉動(混亂)。

passages.original: Come on, my boy.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,我嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,我的孩子。

passages.original: How dost, my boy? Art cold?
passages.vernacular: 你點樣,我嘅細路?冷嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎樣,我的孩子?冷嗎?

passages.original: I am cold myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己都冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己也冷。

passages.original: Where is this straw, my fellow?
passages.vernacular: 呢稻草喺邊度,我嘅朋友?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這稻草在哪裡,我的朋友?

passages.original: The art of our necessities is strange, That can make vile things precious.
passages.vernacular: 我哋需要嘅技藝奇妙,能使卑賤嘅嘢變珍貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們需要的技藝奇妙,能使卑賤的東西變珍貴。

passages.original: Come, your hovel.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,你嘅茅屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,你的茅屋。

passages.original: Poor fool and knave, I have one part in my heart That’s sorry yet for thee.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅弄臣同惡棍,我心裡仲有一部分為你難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的弄臣和惡棍,我心裡還有一部分為你難過。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: [Singing.]
He that has and a little tiny wit, With heigh-ho, the wind and the rain, Must make content with his fortunes fit, Though the rain it raineth every day.
passages.vernacular: 有啲點小聰明嘅人,嘿嚯,風同雨,必須滿足於適合佢嘅命運,雖然雨天天下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一點點小聰明的人,嘿嚯,風和雨,必須滿足於適合他的命運,雖然雨天天下。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: True, boy.
passages.vernacular: 對,細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,孩子。

passages.original: Come, bring us to this hovel.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,帶我哋去呢茅屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,帶我們去這茅屋。

passages.original: [Exeunt Lear and Kent.]
passages.vernacular: [李爾同肯特下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [李爾和肯特下。]

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: This is a brave night to cool a courtezan.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個冷卻娼婦嘅好夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個冷卻娼婦的好夜晚。

passages.original: I’ll speak a prophecy ere I go: When priests are more in word than matter;
passages.vernacular: 我走之前要講一個預言:當神父言辭多過實質;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我走之前要說一個預言:當神父言辭多過實質;

passages.original: When brewers mar their malt with water; When nobles are their tailors’ tutors;
passages.vernacular: 當釀酒師用水糟蹋麥芽;當貴族教佢哋嘅裁縫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當釀酒師用水糟蹋麥芽;當貴族教他們的裁縫;

passages.original: No heretics burn’d, but wenches’ suitors; When every case in law is right;
passages.vernacular: 被燒嘅唔係異端,而係追求姑娘嘅人;當每樁官司都公正;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被燒的不是異端,而是追求姑娘的人;當每樁官司都公正;

passages.original: No squire in debt, nor no poor knight; When slanders do not live in tongues;
passages.vernacular: 冇侍從欠債,都冇窮騎士;當誹謗唔再活喺舌頭上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有侍從欠債,也沒有窮騎士;當誹謗不再活在舌頭上;

passages.original: Nor cut-purses come not to throngs; When usurers tell their gold i’ the field;
passages.vernacular: 扒手唔再混進人群;當放高利貸嘅人喺野外數金子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 扒手不再混進人群;當放高利貸的人在野外數金子;

passages.original: And bawds and whores do churches build, Then shall the realm of Albion Come to great confusion:
passages.vernacular: 皮條客同娼妓建造教堂,嗰時阿爾比恩王國將陷入大混亂:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮條客和娼妓建造教堂,那時阿爾比恩王國將陷入大混亂:

passages.original: Then comes the time, who lives to see’t, That going shall be us’d with feet.
passages.vernacular: 然後嗰時刻到來,活住睇到嘅人,將係用腳走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後那時刻到來,活著看到的人,將是用腳走路。

passages.original: This prophecy Merlin shall make; for I live before his time.
passages.vernacular: 呢預言將由梅林做出;因為我生活喺佢嘅時代之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這預言將由梅林做出;因為我生活在他的時代之前。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene III — A Room in Gloucester’s Castle 第三幕第三場:葛羅斯特城堡一室

passages.original: Enter Gloucester and Edmund.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特同愛德蒙上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特和愛德蒙上。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Alack, alack, Edmund, I like not this unnatural dealing.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,哎呀,愛德蒙,我不鍾意呢種不自然嘅行徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,哎呀,愛德蒙,我不喜歡這種不自然的行徑。

passages.original: When I desired their leave that I might pity him, they took from me the use of mine own house;
passages.vernacular: 我請求佢哋准許我可憐佢,佢哋卻剝奪咗我使用自己房子嘅權利;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請求她們准許我可憐他,她們卻剝奪了我使用自己房子的權利;

passages.original: charged me on pain of perpetual displeasure, neither to speak of him, entreat for him, or any way sustain him.
passages.vernacular: 以永遠不悅為懲罰命令我,不許提佢,不許為佢求情,不許以任何方式資助佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以永遠不悅為懲罰命令我,不許提他,不許為他求情,不許以任何方式資助他。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Most savage and unnatural!
passages.vernacular: 最野蠻最不自然!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最野蠻最不自然!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Go to; say you nothing.
passages.vernacular: 好喇;你乜嘢都唔好講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了;你什麼都別說。

passages.original: There is division between the Dukes, and a worse matter than that:
passages.vernacular: 公爵哋之間有分歧,仲有比嗰更糟嘅事:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵們之間有分歧,還有比那更糟的事:

passages.original: I have received a letter this night;—’tis dangerous to be spoken;—I have locked the letter in my closet:
passages.vernacular: 今晚我收到一封信;——講出嚟危險;——我把信鎖喺我嘅書房裡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚我收到一封信;——說出來危險;——我把信鎖在我的書房裡:

passages.original: these injuries the King now bears will be revenged home;
passages.vernacular: 國王而家所受嘅呢啲傷害,會被徹底報復;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王現在所受的這些傷害,會被徹底報復;

passages.original: there’s part of a power already footed: we must incline to the King.
passages.vernacular: 已有一支軍隊嘅一部分登陸:我哋必須傾向國王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已有一支軍隊的一部分登陸:我們必須傾向國王。

passages.original: I will look him, and privily relieve him: go you and maintain talk with the Duke, that my charity be not of him perceived:
passages.vernacular: 我要去找佢,私下救濟佢:你去同公爵周旋,唔好畀佢察覺我嘅仁慈:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要去找他,私下救濟他:你去和公爵周旋,別讓他察覺我的仁慈:

passages.original: if he ask for me, I am ill, and gone to bed.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢問起我,講我病喇,上床喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他問起我,說我病了,上床了。

passages.original: If I die for it, as no less is threatened me, the King my old master must be relieved.
passages.vernacular: 即使為此而死(威脅我嘅不亞於死),我嘅老主人國王都必須得到救濟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使為此而死(威脅我的不亞於死),我的老主人國王也必須得到救濟。

passages.original: There is some strange thing toward, Edmund; pray you be careful.
passages.vernacular: 有些奇怪嘅事將要發生,愛德蒙;請你小心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些奇怪的事將要發生,愛德蒙;請你小心。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: This courtesy, forbid thee, shall the Duke Instantly know; and of that letter too.
passages.vernacular: 呢份被禁止嘅恩惠,公爵即刻會知道;連嗰封信都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這份被禁止的恩惠,公爵馬上會知道;連那封信也是。

passages.original: This seems a fair deserving, and must draw me That which my father loses, no less than all:
passages.vernacular: 呢個睇嚟係一種美好嘅功勞,必定畀我帶嚟我父親失去嘅一切,不亞於全部:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這看來是一種美好的功勞,必定給我帶來我父親失去的一切,不亞於全部:

passages.original: The younger rises when the old doth fall.
passages.vernacular: 老嘅倒下,年輕嘅就升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老的倒下,年輕的就升起。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene IV — The Heath, with a Hovel 第三幕第四場:荒野上的茅屋

passages.original: Storm continues. Enter Lear, Kent and Fool.
passages.vernacular: [暴風雨繼續。李爾、肯特同弄臣上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [暴風雨繼續。李爾、肯特和弄臣上。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Here is the place, my lord; good my lord, enter:
passages.vernacular: 就係呢度,大人;好大人,進去:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這裡,大人;好大人,進去:

passages.original: The tyranny of the open night’s too rough For nature to endure.
passages.vernacular: 露天夜晚嘅暴虐太粗暴,天性無法忍受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露天夜晚的暴虐太粗暴,天性無法忍受。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Let me alone.
passages.vernacular: 別管我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別管我。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Good my lord, enter here.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,進嚟呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,進來這裡。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Wilt break my heart?
passages.vernacular: 你要打碎我嘅心嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要打碎我的心嗎?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: I had rather break mine own.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願打碎我自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願打碎我自己的。

passages.original: Good my lord, enter.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,進去。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Thou think’st ’tis much that this contentious storm Invades us to the skin:
passages.vernacular: 你以為呢場爭鬥不休嘅風暴侵襲到我哋皮膚好嚴重:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為這場爭鬥不休的風暴侵襲到我們皮膚很嚴重:

passages.original: so ’tis to thee, But where the greater malady is fix’d, The lesser is scarce felt.
passages.vernacular: 對你確係如此,但喺更大病痛紮根之處,較小嘅幾乎感覺唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對你確是如此,但在更大病痛紮根之處,較小的幾乎感覺不到。

passages.original: Thou’dst shun a bear; But if thy flight lay toward the raging sea, Thou’dst meet the bear i’ the mouth.
passages.vernacular: 你會躲避一頭熊;但如果你嘅逃路通向怒吼嘅大海,你會迎面撞上嗰熊嘅嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會躲避一頭熊;但如果你的逃路通向怒吼的大海,你會迎面撞上那熊的嘴。

passages.original: When the mind’s free, The body’s delicate: the tempest in my mind Doth from my senses take all feeling else Save what beats there.
passages.vernacular: 當心靈自由時,身體就嬌嫩:我心裡嘅風暴把我感官裡其他一切感覺都奪走,只剩下嗰度捶打嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當心靈自由時,身體就嬌嫩:我心裡的風暴把我感官裡其他一切感覺都奪走,只剩下那裡捶打的。

passages.original: Filial ingratitude!
passages.vernacular: 細路嘅忘恩負義!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子的忘恩負義!

passages.original: Is it not as this mouth should tear this hand For lifting food to’t?
passages.vernacular: 呢不就像呢張嘴撕咬呢隻手,因為佢把食物舉到嘴邊嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不就像這張嘴撕咬這隻手,因為它把食物舉到嘴邊嗎?

passages.original: But I will punish home; No, I will weep no more.
passages.vernacular: 但我要徹底懲罰;不,我唔再哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我要徹底懲罰;不,我不再哭了。

passages.original: In such a night To shut me out!
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚把我關喺門外!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚把我關在門外!

passages.original: Pour on; I will endure: In such a night as this!
passages.vernacular: 傾瀉吧;我會忍受:喺咁樣嘅夜晚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傾瀉吧;我會忍受:在這樣的夜晚!

passages.original: O Regan, Goneril!
passages.vernacular: 啊里根,高納麗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊里根,高納麗!

passages.original: Your old kind father, whose frank heart gave all, O, that way madness lies;
passages.vernacular: 你哋年老善良嘅父親,佢坦率嘅心畀咗一切——啊,嗰條路通往瘋狂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們年老善良的父親,他坦率的心給了一切——啊,那條路通往瘋狂;

passages.original: let me shun that; No more of that.
passages.vernacular: 讓我躲開佢;唔好再講呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我躲開它;別再說這個。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Good my lord, enter here.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,進嚟呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,進來這裡。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Prythee go in thyself; seek thine own ease: This tempest will not give me leave to ponder On things would hurt me more.
passages.vernacular: 請你自己進去,去求你嘅安適:呢場暴風雨不許我思索嗰啲會更傷害我嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你自己進去,去求你的安適:這場暴風雨不許我思索那些會更傷害我的事。

passages.original: But I’ll go in.
passages.vernacular: 但我進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我進去。

passages.original: [To the Fool.]
passages.vernacular: [對弄臣。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對弄臣。]

passages.original: In, boy; go first.
passages.vernacular: 進去,細路;你先走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進去,孩子;你先走。

passages.original: You houseless poverty, Nay, get thee in.
passages.vernacular: 你呢無家可歸嘅貧窮,不,進去吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這無家可歸的貧窮,不,進去吧。

passages.original: I’ll pray, and then I’ll sleep.
passages.vernacular: 我要祈禱,然後瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要祈禱,然後睡覺。

passages.original: [Fool goes in.]
passages.vernacular: [弄臣進去。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [弄臣進去。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Poor naked wretches, wheresoe’er you are, That bide the pelting of this pitiless storm, How shall your houseless heads and unfed sides, Your loop’d and window’d raggedness, defend you From seasons such as these?
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅赤身流浪者,無論你哋喺邊度,忍受住呢無情風暴嘅襲擊,你哋無屋頂嘅頭同冇食飽嘅肋旁、你哋漏洞窗戶般嘅破衣,怎能抵禦咁樣嘅季節?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的赤身流浪者,無論你們在哪裡,忍受著這無情風暴的襲擊,你們無屋頂的頭和沒吃飽的肋旁、你們漏洞窗戶般的破衣,怎能抵禦這樣的季節?

passages.original: O, I have ta’en Too little care of this!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我對此太不關心喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我對此太不關心了!

passages.original: Take physic, pomp; Expose thyself to feel what wretches feel, That thou mayst shake the superflux to them And show the heavens more just.
passages.vernacular: 服藥吧,排場;讓自己暴露於可憐人所感受嘅,好把多餘嘅抖畀佢哋,顯得上天更公正。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 服藥吧,排場;讓自己暴露於可憐人所感受的,好把多餘的抖給他們,顯得上天更公正。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: [Within.]
Fathom and half, fathom and half! Poor Tom!
passages.vernacular: 一噚半,一噚半!可憐嘅湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一噚半,一噚半!可憐的湯姆!

passages.original: [The Fool runs out from the hovel.]
passages.vernacular: [弄臣從茅屋跑出嚟。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [弄臣從茅屋跑出來。]

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Come not in here, nuncle, here’s a spirit.
passages.vernacular: 別進嚟呢度,叔叔,呢度有鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別進來這裡,叔叔,這裡有鬼。

passages.original: Help me, help me!
passages.vernacular: 救我,救我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 救我,救我!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Give me thy hand.
passages.vernacular: 把手畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把手給我。

passages.original: Who’s there?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在那裡?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: A spirit, a spirit: he says his name’s poor Tom.
passages.vernacular: 一個鬼,一個鬼:佢講佢嘅名字係可憐嘅湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個鬼,一個鬼:他說他的名字是可憐的湯姆。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: What art thou that dost grumble there i’ the straw? Come forth.
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢嘢,喺稻草裡嘟囔?出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼東西,在稻草裡嘟囔?出來。

passages.original: Enter Edgar, disguised as a madman.
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽喬裝成瘋子上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽喬裝成瘋子上。]

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Away!
passages.vernacular: 走開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開!

passages.original: the foul fiend follows me!
passages.vernacular: 嗰邪惡嘅魔鬼喺追我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那邪惡的魔鬼在追我!

passages.original: Through the sharp hawthorn blows the cold wind. Humh!
passages.vernacular: 寒風吹過尖利嘅山楂樹。哼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寒風吹過尖利的山楂樹。哼!

passages.original: go to thy cold bed, and warm thee.
passages.vernacular: 去你冷床上暖暖身子吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去你冷床上暖暖身子吧。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Didst thou give all to thy two daughters?
passages.vernacular: 你把一切都畀咗你兩個女兒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把一切都給了你兩個女兒嗎?

passages.original: And art thou come to this?
passages.vernacular: 你竟落到呢地步?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你竟落到這地步?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Who gives anything to poor Tom?
passages.vernacular: 邊個肯畀可憐嘅湯姆啲嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰肯給可憐的湯姆一點東西?

passages.original: Whom the foul fiend hath led through fire and through flame, through ford and whirlpool, o’er bog and quagmire;
passages.vernacular: 邪惡嘅魔鬼領住佢穿過火穿過焰,穿過淺灘同漩渦,越過沼澤同泥潭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邪惡的魔鬼領著他穿過火穿過焰,穿過淺灘和漩渦,越過沼澤和泥潭;

passages.original: that hath laid knives under his pillow and halters in his pew, set ratsbane by his porridge;
passages.vernacular: 喺佢枕下放刀,喺佢座位上放絞索,喺佢粥邊放老鼠藥;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他枕下放刀,在他座位上放絞索,在他粥邊放老鼠藥;

passages.original: made him proud of heart, to ride on a bay trotting horse over four-inched bridges, to course his own shadow for a traitor.
passages.vernacular: 使佢心驕氣傲,騎喺栗色小跑即刻過四吋寬嘅橋,追逐自己嘅影子當作叛徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使他心驕氣傲,騎在栗色小跑馬上過四吋寬的橋,追逐自己的影子當作叛徒。

passages.original: Bless thy five wits!
passages.vernacular: 保佑你嘅五官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你的五官!

passages.original: Tom’s a-cold.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆冷。

passages.original: O, do, de, do, de, do, de.
passages.vernacular: 哦,多,嘅,多,嘅,多,嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,多,的,多,的,多,的。

passages.original: Bless thee from whirlwinds, star-blasting, and taking!
passages.vernacular: 保佑你免於旋風、星辰嘅災禍同邪術!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你免於旋風、星辰的災禍和邪術!

passages.original: Do poor Tom some charity, whom the foul fiend vexes.
passages.vernacular: 畀被邪惡魔鬼折磨嘅可憐湯姆啲慈善吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給被邪惡魔鬼折磨的可憐湯姆一點慈善吧。

passages.original: There could I have him now, and there,—and there again, and there.
passages.vernacular: 我而家可以喺嗰度抓住佢,喺嗰度,——仲有嗰度,仲有嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在可以在那裡抓住他,在那裡,——還有那裡,還有那裡。

passages.original: [Storm continues.]
passages.vernacular: [暴風雨繼續。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [暴風雨繼續。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What, have his daughters brought him to this pass?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,佢嘅女兒哋把佢逼到呢地步?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,他的女兒們把他逼到這地步?

passages.original: Couldst thou save nothing?
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢都冇保住嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼都沒保住嗎?

passages.original: Didst thou give ’em all?
passages.vernacular: 你全畀佢哋咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你全給她們了嗎?

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Nay, he reserv’d a blanket, else we had been all shamed.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢留咗一條毯子,否則我哋全都要丟臉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他留了一條毯子,否則我們全都要丟臉了。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Now all the plagues that in the pendulous air Hang fated o’er men’s faults light on thy daughters!
passages.vernacular: 而家,所有懸喺空中、注定為人哋嘅過錯而設嘅瘟疫,降喺你嘅女兒哋身上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,所有懸在空中、注定為人們的過錯而設的瘟疫,降在你的女兒們身上!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: He hath no daughters, sir.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇女兒,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有女兒,先生。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Death, traitor!
passages.vernacular: 該死,叛徒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 該死,叛徒!

passages.original: nothing could have subdu’d nature To such a lowness but his unkind daughters.
passages.vernacular: 除咗佢不仁慈嘅女兒哋,冇乜嘢能把天性壓制到咁樣卑微嘅地步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了他不仁慈的女兒們,沒有什麼能把天性壓制到這樣卑微的地步。

passages.original: Is it the fashion that discarded fathers Should have thus little mercy on their flesh?
passages.vernacular: 難道被遺棄嘅父親哋慣例應對自己嘅肉體咁不留情?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難道被遺棄的父親們慣例應對自己的肉體這麼不留情?

passages.original: Judicious punishment!
passages.vernacular: 明智嘅懲罰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明智的懲罰!

passages.original: ’twas this flesh begot Those pelican daughters.
passages.vernacular: 正是呢塊肉生出咗嗰啲像鵜鶘一樣嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是這塊肉生出了那些像鵜鶘一樣的女兒。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Pillicock sat on Pillicock hill, Alow, alow, loo loo!
passages.vernacular: 皮利科坐喺皮利科山上,嚯嚯,嚯嚯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮利科坐在皮利科山上,嚯嚯,嚯嚯!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: This cold night will turn us all to fools and madmen.
passages.vernacular: 呢冷夜會把我哋全都變成傻瓜同瘋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這冷夜會把我們全都變成傻瓜和瘋子。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Take heed o’ th’ foul fiend: obey thy parents;
passages.vernacular: 提防邪惡嘅魔鬼:服從你父母;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提防邪惡的魔鬼:服從你父母;

passages.original: keep thy word justly; swear not; commit not with man’s sworn spouse;
passages.vernacular: 守信用;不發誓;不同有夫之婦通姦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 守信用;不發誓;不和有夫之婦通姦;

passages.original: set not thy sweet-heart on proud array.
passages.vernacular: 唔好把心愛嘅人放喺驕傲嘅華服上。
