passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要把心愛的人放在驕傲的華服上。

passages.original: Tom’s a-cold.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆冷。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What hast thou been?
passages.vernacular: 你以前係乜嘢人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以前是什麼人?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: A serving-man, proud in heart and mind; that curled my hair;
passages.vernacular: 一個僕人,心高氣傲;曾捲頭髮;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個僕人,心高氣傲;曾捲頭髮;

passages.original: wore gloves in my cap; served the lust of my mistress’ heart, and did the act of darkness with her;
passages.vernacular: 帽子裡戴手套;滿足我女主人心中嘅情慾,同佢幹黑暗嘅勾當;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帽子裡戴手套;滿足我女主人心中的情慾,與她幹黑暗的勾當;

passages.original: swore as many oaths as I spake words, and broke them in the sweet face of heaven.
passages.vernacular: 我發嘅誓同我講嘅話一樣多,並喺天上甜美嘅面前破誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發的誓和我說的話一樣多,並在天上甜美的面前破誓。

passages.original: One that slept in the contriving of lust, and waked to do it.
passages.vernacular: 一個喺策劃情慾中瞓去、醒嚟就去實行嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個在策劃情慾中睡去、醒來就去實行的人。

passages.original: Wine loved I deeply, dice dearly; and in woman out-paramour’d the Turk.
passages.vernacular: 我深愛酒,深愛骰子;喺女人方面勝過土耳其人嘅情人氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我深愛酒,深愛骰子;在女人方面勝過土耳其人的情人氣。

passages.original: False of heart, light of ear, bloody of hand;
passages.vernacular: 心虛偽,耳根輕,手沾血;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 心虛偽,耳根輕,手沾血;

passages.original: hog in sloth, fox in stealth, wolf in greediness, dog in madness, lion in prey.
passages.vernacular: 懶惰如豬,偷偷摸摸如狐,貪婪如狼,瘋狂如狗,捕食如獅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懶惰如豬,偷偷摸摸如狐,貪婪如狼,瘋狂如狗,捕食如獅。

passages.original: Let not the creaking of shoes nor the rustling of silks betray thy poor heart to woman.
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀鞋子嘅吱吱聲或絲綢嘅沙沙聲,把你可憐嘅心出賣畀女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別讓鞋子的吱吱聲或絲綢的沙沙聲,把你可憐的心出賣給女人。

passages.original: Keep thy foot out of brothels, thy hand out of plackets, thy pen from lender’s book, and defy the foul fiend.
passages.vernacular: 腳遠離妓院,手遠離裙襟,筆遠離債主嘅帳本,並蔑視邪惡嘅魔鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 腳遠離妓院,手遠離裙襟,筆遠離債主的帳本,並蔑視邪惡的魔鬼。

passages.original: Still through the hawthorn blows the cold wind: says suum, mun, nonny.
passages.vernacular: 寒風仍穿過山楂吹嚟:講「蘇姆,蒙,諾尼」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寒風仍穿過山楂吹來:說「蘇姆,蒙,諾尼」。

passages.original: Dolphin my boy, boy, sessa!
passages.vernacular: 海豚,我嘅細路,細路,嘶薩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海豚,我的孩子,孩子,嘶薩!

passages.original: let him trot by.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢小跑過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他小跑過去。

passages.original: [Storm still continues.]
passages.vernacular: [暴風雨仍繼續。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [暴風雨仍繼續。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Why, thou wert better in thy grave than to answer with thy uncovered body this extremity of the skies.
passages.vernacular: 咦,你最好躺喺墳墓裡,都勝過用赤裸嘅身體回應天上呢極端嘅天氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,你最好躺在墳墓裡,也勝過用赤裸的身體回應天上這極端的天氣。

passages.original: Is man no more than this?
passages.vernacular: 人不過係咁樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人不過是這樣嗎?

passages.original: Consider him well.
passages.vernacular: 好好睇睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好好看看他。

passages.original: Thou owest the worm no silk, the beast no hide, the sheep no wool, the cat no perfume. Ha!
passages.vernacular: 你不欠蠶絲,不欠獸皮,不欠羊毛,不欠貓香。哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不欠蠶絲,不欠獸皮,不欠羊毛,不欠貓香。哈!

passages.original: here’s three on’s are sophisticated!
passages.vernacular: 我哋三個都係加工過嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們三個都是加工過的!

passages.original: Thou art the thing itself: unaccommodated man is no more but such a poor, bare, forked animal as thou art.
passages.vernacular: 你就係嗰嘢本身:冇被裝備嘅人,不過係像你咁樣一頭可憐、赤裸、分叉嘅動物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就是那東西本身:沒有被裝備的人,不過是像你這樣一頭可憐、赤裸、分叉的動物。

passages.original: Off, off, you lendings!
passages.vernacular: 脫掉,脫掉,你哋呢啲借嚟嘅嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 脫掉,脫掉,你們這些借來的東西!

passages.original: Come, unbutton here.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,喺呢度解開鈕扣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,在這裡解開鈕扣。

passages.original: [Tears off his clothes.]
passages.vernacular: [撕掉衣服。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [撕掉衣服。]

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Prythee, nuncle, be contented; ’tis a naughty night to swim in.
passages.vernacular: 請你,叔叔,安心;呢個係個不適合游泳嘅壞夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,叔叔,安心;這是個不適合游泳的壞夜晚。

passages.original: Now a little fire in a wild field were like an old lecher’s heart, a small spark, all the rest on’s body cold.
passages.vernacular: 而家,荒野上啲小火,就像老色鬼嘅心,啲小火花,身體其餘全係冷嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,荒野上一點小火,就像老色鬼的心,一點小火花,身體其餘全是冷的。

passages.original: Look, here comes a walking fire.
passages.vernacular: 睇,走嚟一團行走嘅火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,走來一團行走的火。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: This is the foul fiend Flibbertigibbet: he begins at curfew, and walks till the first cock;
passages.vernacular: 呢個係邪惡嘅魔鬼弗利貝提吉比特:佢從宵禁開始,走到第一聲雞啼;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是邪惡的魔鬼弗利貝提吉比特:他從宵禁開始,走到第一聲雞啼;

passages.original: he gives the web and the pin, squints the eye, and makes the harelip;
passages.vernacular: 佢畀人添白內障同針眼,使人斜視,造成兔唇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給人添白內障和針眼,使人斜視,造成兔唇;

passages.original: mildews the white wheat, and hurts the poor creature of earth.
passages.vernacular: 使白麥發霉,傷害地上可憐嘅生物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使白麥發霉,傷害地上可憐的生物。

passages.original: Swithold footed thrice the old; He met the nightmare, and her nine-fold;
passages.vernacular: 聖斯威索德三次走過荒原;佢遇見夢魘同佢嘅九個細路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖斯威索德三次走過荒原;他遇見夢魘和她的九個孩子;

passages.original: Bid her alight and her troth plight, And aroint thee, witch, aroint thee!
passages.vernacular: 命令佢下嚟並立誓,然後你走開,女巫,走開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 命令她下來並立誓,然後你走開,女巫,走開!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: How fares your grace?
passages.vernacular: 殿下點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下怎麼樣?

passages.original: Enter Gloucester with a torch.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特持火把上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特持火把上。]

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: What’s he?
passages.vernacular: 佢係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是誰?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Who’s there?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在那裡?

passages.original: What is’t you seek?
passages.vernacular: 你喺找乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在找什麼?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: What are you there? Your names?
passages.vernacular: 你哋係邊個?你哋叫乜嘢名字?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們是誰?你們叫什麼名字?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Poor Tom; that eats the swimming frog, the toad, the todpole, the wall-newt and the water;
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅湯姆;食游水嘅青蛙、蟾蜍、蝌蚪、壁虎同水蜥蜴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的湯姆;吃游水的青蛙、蟾蜍、蝌蚪、壁虎和水蜥蜴;

passages.original: that in the fury of his heart, when the foul fiend rages, eats cow-dung for sallets;
passages.vernacular: 心中狂怒時,當邪惡嘅魔鬼發作,食牛糞當沙拉;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 心中狂怒時,當邪惡的魔鬼發作,吃牛糞當沙拉;

passages.original: swallows the old rat and the ditch-dog; drinks the green mantle of the standing pool;
passages.vernacular: 吞老鼠同水溝裡嘅死狗;飲死水池嘅綠浮沫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吞老鼠和水溝裡的死狗;喝死水池的綠浮沫;

passages.original: who is whipped from tithing to tithing, and stocked, punished, and imprisoned;
passages.vernacular: 被人從一個十戶區鞭打到另一個十戶區,被鎖喺木枷裡,受懲罰,被監禁;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被人從一個十戶區鞭打到另一個十戶區,被鎖在木枷裡,受懲罰,被監禁;

passages.original: who hath had three suits to his back, six shirts to his body, Horse to ride, and weapon to wear.
passages.vernacular: 有過三套衣服喺背上,六件襯衫喺身上,有馬騎,有武器佩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有過三套衣服在背上,六件襯衫在身上,有馬騎,有武器佩。

passages.original: But mice and rats and such small deer, Have been Tom’s food for seven long year.
passages.vernacular: 但老鼠同小鹿一樣嘅小嘢,係湯姆七年嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但老鼠和小鹿一樣的小東西,是湯姆七年的食物。

passages.original: Beware my follower.
passages.vernacular: 小心我嘅跟班。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小心我的跟班。

passages.original: Peace, Smulkin; peace, thou fiend!
passages.vernacular: 安靜,斯穆金;安靜,你呢魔鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,斯穆金;安靜,你這魔鬼!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: What, hath your grace no better company?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,殿下冇更好嘅同伴嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,殿下沒有更好的同伴嗎?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: The prince of darkness is a gentleman: Modo he’s call’d, and Mahu.
passages.vernacular: 黑暗嘅王子係位紳士:佢叫莫多,都叫馬胡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑暗的王子是位紳士:他叫莫多,也叫馬胡。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Our flesh and blood, my lord, is grown so vile That it doth hate what gets it.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我哋嘅血肉已變得如此卑劣,以致憎恨生佢嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我們的血肉已變得如此卑劣,以致憎恨生它的人。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Poor Tom’s a-cold.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅湯姆冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的湯姆冷。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Go in with me: my duty cannot suffer T’obey in all your daughters’ hard commands;
passages.vernacular: 跟我進去:我嘅責任唔能夠容許我完全服從你哋女兒嗰啲嚴酷嘅命令;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟我進去:我的責任不能容許我完全服從你們女兒那些嚴酷的命令;

passages.original: Though their injunction be to bar my doors, And let this tyrannous night take hold upon you, Yet have I ventur’d to come seek you out, And bring you where both fire and food is ready.
passages.vernacular: 雖然佢哋嘅指令係關上我嘅門,讓呢暴虐嘅夜晚抓住你哋,我仍冒險嚟找你哋,帶你哋去既有火又有食物嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然她們的指令是關上我的門,讓這暴虐的夜晚抓住你們,我仍冒險來找你們,帶你們去既有火又有食物的地方。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: First let me talk with this philosopher.
passages.vernacular: 先讓我同呢位哲學家談談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先讓我和這位哲學家談談。

passages.original: What is the cause of thunder?
passages.vernacular: 雷嘅原因係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷的原因是什麼?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Good my lord, take his offer; go into the house.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,接受佢嘅提議;進屋去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,接受他的提議;進屋去。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I’ll talk a word with this same learned Theban.
passages.vernacular: 我要同呢位博學嘅底比斯人講句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要和這位博學的底比斯人說句話。

passages.original: What is your study?
passages.vernacular: 你研究乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你研究什麼?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: How to prevent the fiend and to kill vermin.
passages.vernacular: 點樣防範魔鬼同殺滅害蟲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎樣防範魔鬼和殺滅害蟲。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Let me ask you one word in private.
passages.vernacular: 讓我私下問你一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我私下問你一句話。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Importune him once more to go, my lord; His wits begin t’unsettle.
passages.vernacular: 大人,再勸佢一次進去;佢嘅神志開始不穩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,再勸他一次進去;他的神志開始不穩了。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Canst thou blame him?
passages.vernacular: 你能責怪佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能責怪他嗎?

passages.original: His daughters seek his death.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅女兒哋想要佢嘅命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的女兒們想要他的命。

passages.original: Ah, that good Kent!
passages.vernacular: 啊,嗰好肯特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那好肯特!

passages.original: He said it would be thus, poor banish’d man!
passages.vernacular: 佢講過會咁樣,可憐嘅被放逐嘅人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說過會這樣,可憐的被放逐的人!

passages.original: Thou sayest the King grows mad; I’ll tell thee, friend, I am almost mad myself.
passages.vernacular: 你講國王瘋喇;我告訴你,朋友,我自己都快瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說國王瘋了;我告訴你,朋友,我自己也快瘋了。

passages.original: I had a son, Now outlaw’d from my blood; he sought my life But lately, very late:
passages.vernacular: 我曾有個兒子,而家被逐出我嘅血脈;佢最近想要我嘅命,就喺最近:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾有個兒子,現在被逐出我的血脈;他最近想要我的命,就在最近:

passages.original: I lov’d him, friend, No father his son dearer: true to tell thee,
passages.vernacular: 我愛佢,朋友,冇邊個父親更疼兒子:講實話,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛他,朋友,沒有哪個父親更疼兒子:說實話,

passages.original: [Storm continues.]
passages.vernacular: [暴風雨繼續。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [暴風雨繼續。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: The grief hath craz’d my wits.
passages.vernacular: 悲痛已使我神志錯亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 悲痛已使我神志錯亂。

passages.original: What a night’s this!
passages.vernacular: 呢個係點樣嘅夜晚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是怎樣的夜晚!

passages.original: I do beseech your grace.
passages.vernacular: 我懇求殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求殿下。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: O, cry you mercy, sir.
passages.vernacular: 啊,請原諒,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,請原諒,先生。

passages.original: Noble philosopher, your company.
passages.vernacular: 高貴嘅哲學家,陪我哋吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高貴的哲學家,陪我們吧。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Tom’s a-cold.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆冷。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: In, fellow, there, into the hovel; keep thee warm.
passages.vernacular: 進去,朋友,嗰度,進茅屋;保持溫暖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進去,朋友,那裡,進茅屋;保持溫暖。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Come, let’s in all.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,我哋都進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我們都進去。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: This way, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 呢邊走,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這邊走,大人。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: With him; I will keep still with my philosopher.
passages.vernacular: 跟佢喺一起;我要始終同我嘅哲學家喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟他在一起;我要始終和我的哲學家在一起。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Good my lord, soothe him; let him take the fellow.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,哄哄佢;讓佢帶嗰個傢伙去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,哄哄他;讓他帶那個傢伙去。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Take him you on.
passages.vernacular: 你帶佢走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你帶他走。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Sirrah, come on; go along with us.
passages.vernacular: 小子,嚟;跟我哋走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,來;跟我們走。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Come, good Athenian.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,好雅典人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,好雅典人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: No words, no words, hush.
passages.vernacular: 唔好講話,唔好講話,噓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別說話,別說話,噓。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Child Rowland to the dark tower came, His word was still—Fie, foh, and fum, I smell the blood of a British man.
passages.vernacular: 羅蘭騎士嚟到黑塔,佢嘅口令始終係——呸,呼,呋,我聞到不列顛人嘅血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅蘭騎士來到黑塔,他的口令始終是——呸,呼,呋,我聞到不列顛人的血。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene V — A Room in Gloucester’s Castle 第三幕第五場:葛羅斯特城堡一室

passages.original: Enter Cornwall and Edmund.
passages.vernacular: [康華爾同愛德蒙上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [康華爾和愛德蒙上。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: I will have my revenge ere I depart his house.
passages.vernacular: 我離開佢家之前,我要報仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我離開他家之前,我要報仇。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: How, my lord, I may be censured, that nature thus gives way to loyalty, something fears me to think of.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我可能會受到責難,因為天性咁樣向忠誠讓步,想到呢點我有些害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我可能會受到責難,因為天性這樣向忠誠讓步,想到這點我有些害怕。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: I now perceive it was not altogether your brother’s evil disposition made him seek his death;
passages.vernacular: 我而家睇出,不完全係你哥哥嘅邪惡性情促使佢尋求佢嘅死;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在看出,不完全是你哥哥的邪惡性情促使他尋求他的死;

passages.original: but a provoking merit, set a-work by a reproveable badness in himself.
passages.vernacular: 而係一種挑起嘅功績,被佢自己應受責備嘅惡行所驅動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而是一種挑起的功績,被他自己應受責備的惡行所驅動。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: How malicious is my fortune, that I must repent to be just!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅命運幾咁惡意,我竟必須為公正而後悔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的命運多麼惡意,我竟必須為公正而後悔!

passages.original: This is the letter he spoke of, which approves him an intelligent party to the advantages of France. O heavens!
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係佢講嘅嗰封信,佢證明佢係法蘭西有利行動嘅知情同謀者。啊天!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是他說的那封信,它證明他是法蘭西有利行動的知情同謀者。啊天!

passages.original: that this treason were not; or not I the detector!
passages.vernacular: 但願呢叛逆不存在;或發現者唔係我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願這叛逆不存在;或發現者不是我!

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Go with me to the Duchess.
passages.vernacular: 跟我去見公爵夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟我去見公爵夫人。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: If the matter of this paper be certain, you have mighty business in hand.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢紙上嘅內容確實,你有重大嘅事務喺手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這紙上的內容確實,你有重大的事務在手。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: True or false, it hath made thee Earl of Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: 無論真假,佢已使你成為葛羅斯特伯爵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論真假,它已使你成為葛羅斯特伯爵。

passages.original: Seek out where thy father is, that he may be ready for our apprehension.
passages.vernacular: 找出你父親喺邊度,好讓佢準備好被我哋逮捕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找出你父親在哪裡,好讓他準備好被我們逮捕。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: If I find him comforting the King, it will stuff his suspicion more fully.
passages.vernacular: 如果我發現佢喺安慰國王,呢會更加充實佢嘅嫌疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我發現他在安慰國王,這會更加充實他的嫌疑。

passages.original: I will persever in my course of loyalty, though the conflict be sore between that and my blood.
passages.vernacular: 我要堅持我忠誠嘅路,雖然喺佢同我嘅血脈之間衝突劇烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要堅持我忠誠的路,雖然在它與我的血脈之間衝突劇烈。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: I will lay trust upon thee; and thou shalt find a dearer father in my love.
passages.vernacular: 我要信任你;你將喺我嘅愛中發現一位更親嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要信任你;你將在我的愛中發現一位更親的父親。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene VI — A Chamber in a Farmhouse 第三幕第六場:農舍一室

passages.original: Enter Gloucester, Lear, Kent, Fool and Edgar.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特、李爾、肯特、弄臣同愛德伽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特、李爾、肯特、弄臣和愛德伽上。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Here is better than the open air; take it thankfully.
passages.vernacular: 呢度比露天好;感激地接受吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡比露天好;感激地接受吧。

passages.original: I will piece out the comfort with what addition I can:
passages.vernacular: 我會盡我所能添補呢份安慰:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會盡我所能添補這份安慰:

passages.original: I will not be long from you.
passages.vernacular: 我好快回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很快回來。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: All the power of his wits have given way to his impatience:— the gods reward your kindness!
passages.vernacular: 佢全部嘅智力都屈從於佢嘅急躁:——願諸神報償你嘅善意!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他全部的智力都屈從於他的急躁:——願諸神報償你的善意!

passages.original: [Exit Gloucester.]
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特下。]

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Frateretto calls me; and tells me Nero is an angler in the lake of darkness.
passages.vernacular: 弗拉特雷托叫我;告訴我尼祿喺黑暗湖裡釣魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗拉特雷托叫我;告訴我尼祿在黑暗湖裡釣魚。

passages.original: Pray, innocent, and beware the foul fiend.
passages.vernacular: 祈禱吧,天真嘅人,提防邪惡嘅魔鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 祈禱吧,天真的人,提防邪惡的魔鬼。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Prythee, nuncle, tell me whether a madman be a gentleman or a yeoman.
passages.vernacular: 請你,叔叔,告訴我瘋子係紳士定係自耕農。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,叔叔,告訴我瘋子是紳士還是自耕農。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: A king, a king!
passages.vernacular: 一個國王,一個國王!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個國王,一個國王!

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: No, he’s a yeoman that has a gentleman to his son;
passages.vernacular: 不,係一個有個紳士兒子嘅自耕農;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,是一個有個紳士兒子的自耕農;

passages.original: for he’s a mad yeoman that sees his son a gentleman before him.
passages.vernacular: 因為一個睇到兒子比自己先成為紳士嘅自耕農,係個瘋自耕農。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為一個看到兒子比自己先成為紳士的自耕農,是個瘋自耕農。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: To have a thousand with red burning spits Come hissing in upon ’em.
passages.vernacular: 讓一千個攞住紅熱烤叉嘅人嘶嘶地衝向佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓一千個拿著紅熱烤叉的人嘶嘶地衝向他們。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: The foul fiend bites my back.
passages.vernacular: 邪惡嘅魔鬼咬我嘅背。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邪惡的魔鬼咬我的背。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: He’s mad that trusts in the tameness of a wolf, a horse’s health, a boy’s love, or a whore’s oath.
passages.vernacular: 相信狼嘅溫馴、馬嘅健康、男孩嘅愛、娼妓嘅誓言嘅人,係瘋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信狼的溫馴、馬的健康、男孩的愛、娼妓的誓言的人,是瘋子。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: It shall be done; I will arraign them straight. [To Edgar.]
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣辦;我即刻審判佢哋。[對愛德伽。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣辦;我立刻審判她們。[對愛德伽。]

passages.original: Come, sit thou here, most learned justicer; [To the Fool.]
passages.vernacular: 嚟,坐呢度,最博學嘅法官;[對弄臣。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,坐這裡,最博學的法官;[對弄臣。]

passages.original: Thou, sapient sir, sit here.
passages.vernacular: 你,明智嘅先生,坐呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,明智的先生,坐這裡。

passages.original: Now, you she-foxes!—
passages.vernacular: 而家,你哋呢啲母狐狸!——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,你們這些母狐狸!——

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Look, where he stands and glares!
passages.vernacular: 睇,佢站喺嗰兒瞪眼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,他站在那兒瞪眼!

passages.original: Want’st thou eyes at trial, madam?
passages.vernacular: 夫人,你審判時仲要眼睛嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,你審判時還要眼睛嗎?

passages.original: Come o’er the bourn, Bessy, to me.
passages.vernacular: 越過小溪嚟我呢度,貝西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 越過小溪來我這裡,貝西。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Her boat hath a leak, And she must not speak Why she dares not come over to thee.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅船漏水,佢唔能夠講點解唔敢過嚟找你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的船漏水,她不能說為什麼不敢過來找你。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: The foul fiend haunts poor Tom in the voice of a nightingale.
passages.vernacular: 邪惡嘅魔鬼用夜鶯嘅聲音纏住可憐嘅湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邪惡的魔鬼用夜鶯的聲音纏著可憐的湯姆。

passages.original: Hoppedance cries in Tom’s belly for two white herring.
passages.vernacular: 蹦跳喺湯姆肚子裡喊住要兩條白鯡魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蹦跳在湯姆肚子裡喊著要兩條白鯡魚。

passages.original: Croak not, black angel; I have no food for thee.
passages.vernacular: 別呱呱叫,黑天使;我冇食物畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別呱呱叫,黑天使;我沒有食物給你。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: How do you, sir?
passages.vernacular: 您點樣,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您怎麼樣,先生?

passages.original: Stand you not so amaz’d; Will you lie down and rest upon the cushions?
passages.vernacular: 別咁樣驚愕地站住;您要躺下,喺墊子上休息嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別這樣驚愕地站著;您要躺下,在墊子上休息嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: I’ll see their trial first.
passages.vernacular: 我先睇佢哋受審。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我先看她們受審。

passages.original: Bring in their evidence. [To Edgar.]
passages.vernacular: 把佢哋嘅證據帶上嚟。[對愛德伽。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把她們的證據帶上來。[對愛德伽。]

passages.original: Thou, robed man of justice, take thy place.
passages.vernacular: 你,穿長袍嘅正義之人,就座。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,穿長袍的正義之人,就座。

passages.original: [To the Fool.]
passages.vernacular: [對弄臣。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對弄臣。]

passages.original: And thou, his yokefellow of equity, Bench by his side. [To Kent.]
passages.vernacular: 仲有你,佢公平嘅共軛伙伴,坐喺佢旁邊。[對肯特。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你,他公平的共軛伙伴,坐在他旁邊。[對肯特。]

passages.original: You are o’ the commission, Sit you too.
passages.vernacular: 你係委員會嘅一員,你都坐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是委員會的一員,你也坐。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Let us deal justly.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋公正行事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們公正行事。

passages.original: Sleepest or wakest thou, jolly shepherd?
passages.vernacular: 你係瞓住定係醒住,快樂嘅牧羊人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是睡著還是醒著,快樂的牧羊人?

passages.original: Thy sheep be in the corn; And for one blast of thy minikin mouth Thy sheep shall take no harm. Purr!
passages.vernacular: 你嘅羊喺麥田裡;只要你小嘴吹一口氣,你嘅羊就唔會受害。咕嚕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的羊在麥田裡;只要你小嘴吹一口氣,你的羊就不會受害。咕嚕!

passages.original: the cat is grey.
passages.vernacular: 嗰隻貓係灰嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那隻貓是灰的。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Arraign her first; ’tis Goneril.
passages.vernacular: 先審佢:呢個係高納麗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先審她:這是高納麗。

passages.original: I here take my oath before this honourable assembly, she kicked the poor King her father.
passages.vernacular: 我喺此高貴嘅集會面前宣誓,佢踢咗可憐嘅國王,佢嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在此高貴的集會面前宣誓,她踢了可憐的國王,她的父親。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Come hither, mistress.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,夫人。

passages.original: Is your name Goneril?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅名字係高納麗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的名字是高納麗嗎?

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: She cannot deny it.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔能夠否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不能否認。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: Cry you mercy, I took you for a joint-stool.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,我把你當成折凳喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,我把你當成折凳了。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: And here’s another, whose warp’d looks proclaim What store her heart is made on.
passages.vernacular: 呢度仲有一個,佢扭曲嘅神情宣告佢嘅心係用乜嘢材料做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡還有一個,她扭曲的神情宣告她的心是用什麼材料做的。

passages.original: Stop her there! Arms, arms! sword! fire!
passages.vernacular: 攔住佢!武器,武器!劍!火!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 攔住她!武器,武器!劍!火!

passages.original: Corruption in the place!
passages.vernacular: 呢地方腐敗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這地方腐敗!

passages.original: False justicer, why hast thou let her ’scape?
passages.vernacular: 虛假嘅法官,你點解讓佢逃喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虛假的法官,你為什麼讓她逃了?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Bless thy five wits!
passages.vernacular: 保佑你嘅五官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你的五官!

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: O pity!
passages.vernacular: 啊,可憐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,可憐!

passages.original: Sir, where is the patience now That you so oft have boasted to retain?
passages.vernacular: 先生,您常常誇口保持嘅耐心而家喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,您常常誇口保持的耐心現在在哪裡?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: My tears begin to take his part so much They mar my counterfeiting.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅眼淚開始咁偏向佢,毀咗我嘅偽裝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的眼淚開始這麼偏向他,毀了我的偽裝。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: The little dogs and all, Trey, Blanch, and Sweetheart, see, they bark at me.
passages.vernacular: 小狗哋,連同特雷、布蘭奇同甜心,睇,佢哋對我吠叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小狗們,連同特雷、布蘭奇和甜心,看,它們對我吠叫。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Tom will throw his head at them.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆要把頭朝佢哋扔去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆要把頭朝它們扔去。

passages.original: Avaunt, you curs!
passages.vernacular: 走開,你哋呢啲惡狗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,你們這些惡狗!

passages.original: Be thy mouth or black or white, Tooth that poisons if it bite;
passages.vernacular: 不管你嘅嘴係黑係白,咬人就有毒嘅牙齒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管你的嘴是黑是白,咬人就有毒的牙齒;

passages.original: Mastiff, greyhound, mongrel grim, Hound or spaniel, brach or him, Or bobtail tike or trundle-tail, Tom will make them weep and wail;
passages.vernacular: 獒犬、靈缇、雜種惡犬、獵犬或西班牙獵犬、母犬或公犬、短尾狗或拖尾狗,湯姆會讓佢哋哭號;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獒犬、靈缇、雜種惡犬、獵犬或西班牙獵犬、母犬或公犬、短尾狗或拖尾狗,湯姆會讓它們哭號;

passages.original: For, with throwing thus my head, Dogs leap the hatch, and all are fled.
passages.vernacular: 因為像咁樣甩頭,狗跳過柵欄,全都逃走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為像這樣甩頭,狗跳過柵欄,全都逃走了。

passages.original: Do, de, de, de. Sessa!
passages.vernacular: 多,嘅,嘅,嘅。嘶薩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多,的,的,的。嘶薩!

passages.original: Come, march to wakes and fairs and market towns.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,去趕集、市集同市鎮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,去趕集、市集和市鎮。

passages.original: Poor Tom, thy horn is dry.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅湯姆,你嘅角杯乾喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的湯姆,你的角杯乾了。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Then let them anatomize Regan; see what breeds about her heart.
passages.vernacular: 咁讓佢哋解剖里根;睇睇佢心周圍長住乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼讓他們解剖里根;看看她心周圍長著什麼。

passages.original: Is there any cause in nature that makes these hard hearts? [To Edgar.]
passages.vernacular: 自然中有乜嘢原因造出呢啲硬心腸?[對愛德伽。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自然中有什麼原因造出這些硬心腸?[對愛德伽。]

passages.original: You, sir, I entertain you for one of my hundred;
passages.vernacular: 你,先生,我雇你做我一百名隨從之一;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,先生,我雇你做我一百名隨從之一;

passages.original: only I do not like the fashion of your garments.
passages.vernacular: 只係我不鍾意你衣服嘅款式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是我不喜歡你衣服的款式。

passages.original: You’ll say they are Persian; but let them be changed.
passages.vernacular: 你會講佢哋係波斯式嘅;但讓佢哋換掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會說它們是波斯式的;但讓它們換掉。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Now, good my lord, lie here and rest awhile.
passages.vernacular: 而家,好大人,躺喺呢度休息一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,好大人,躺在這裡休息一會兒。

passages.title: Lear 李爾
passages.original: Make no noise, make no noise; draw the curtains. So, so.
passages.vernacular: 別出聲,別出聲;拉上帳子。咁樣,咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別出聲,別出聲;拉上帳子。這樣,這樣。

passages.original: We’ll go to supper i’ the morning.
passages.vernacular: 我哋朝早去食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們早上去吃晚飯。

passages.title: Fool 弄臣
passages.original: And I’ll go to bed at noon.
passages.vernacular: 我中午去瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我中午去睡覺。

passages.original: Enter Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特上。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Come hither, friend; Where is the King my master?
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,朋友;我主人國王喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,朋友;我主人國王在哪裡?

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Here, sir; but trouble him not, his wits are gone.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,先生;但別打擾佢,佢嘅神志已經走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,先生;但別打擾他,他的神志已經走了。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Good friend, I prythee, take him in thy arms;
passages.vernacular: 好朋友,我請求你,把佢抱喺懷裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好朋友,我請求你,把他抱在懷裡;

passages.original: I have o’erheard a plot of death upon him; There is a litter ready;
passages.vernacular: 我偷聽到一個要佢命嘅陰謀;有一副擔架準備好喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我偷聽到一個要他命的陰謀;有一副擔架準備好了;

passages.original: lay him in’t And drive towards Dover, friend, where thou shalt meet Both welcome and protection.
passages.vernacular: 把佢放喺上面,向多佛駛去,朋友,喺嗰度你會得到歡迎同保護。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他放在上面,向多佛駛去,朋友,在那裡你會得到歡迎與保護。

passages.original: Take up thy master; If thou shouldst dally half an hour, his life, With thine, and all that offer to defend him, Stand in assured loss.
passages.vernacular: 抬起你嘅主人;如果你耽擱半小時,佢嘅性命,連同你嘅同所有想保護佢嘅人,都肯定要失去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 抬起你的主人;如果你耽擱半小時,他的性命,連同你的和所有想保護他的人,都肯定要失去。

passages.original: Take up, take up; And follow me, that will to some provision Give thee quick conduct.
passages.vernacular: 抬起,抬起;跟我嚟,我會讓你好快得到啲補畀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 抬起,抬起;跟我來,我會讓你很快得到一些補給。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Oppressed nature sleeps.
passages.vernacular: 被壓迫嘅天性瞓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被壓迫的天性睡了。

passages.original: This rest might yet have balm’d thy broken sinews, Which, if convenience will not allow, Stand in hard cure.
passages.vernacular: 呢次休息本可以滋養你破碎嘅筋骨,若條件不允許,就難治癒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次休息本可以滋養你破碎的筋骨,若條件不允許,就難治癒了。

passages.original: Come, help to bear thy master; [To the Fool.]
passages.vernacular: 嚟,幫忙抬你嘅主人;[對弄臣。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,幫忙抬你的主人;[對弄臣。]

passages.original: Thou must not stay behind.
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠留喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能留在後面。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Come, come, away!
passages.vernacular: 嚟,嚟,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,來,走!

passages.original: [Exeunt Kent, Gloucester and the Fool bearing off Lear.]
passages.vernacular: [肯特、葛羅斯特同弄臣抬住李爾下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特、葛羅斯特和弄臣抬著李爾下。]

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: When we our betters see bearing our woes, We scarcely think our miseries our foes.
passages.vernacular: 當我哋睇到比我哋高貴嘅人都承受我哋嘅苦難,我哋幾乎不認為自己嘅悲慘係敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我們看到比我們高貴的人也承受我們的苦難,我們幾乎不認為自己的悲慘是敵人。

passages.original: Who alone suffers, suffers most i’ the mind, Leaving free things and happy shows behind:
passages.vernacular: 獨自受苦嘅人喺心靈上受苦最多,把自由嘅事物同快樂嘅景象拋喺身後:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獨自受苦的人在心靈上受苦最多,把自由的事物和快樂的景象拋在身後:

passages.original: But then the mind much sufferance doth o’erskip When grief hath mates, and bearing fellowship.
passages.vernacular: 但當悲傷有伴、有人同擔時,心靈就跳過許多苦難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當悲傷有伴、有人同擔時,心靈就跳過許多苦難。

passages.original: How light and portable my pain seems now, When that which makes me bend makes the King bow;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅痛苦而家顯得幾咁輕、幾咁容易承受,當嗰使我彎腰嘅都使國王低頭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的痛苦現在顯得多麼輕、多麼容易承受,當那使我彎腰的也使國王低頭;

passages.original: He childed as I fathered! Tom, away!
passages.vernacular: 佢受細路之累,我受父親之累!湯姆,走吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他受孩子之累,我受父親之累!湯姆,走吧!

passages.original: Mark the high noises; and thyself bewray, When false opinion, whose wrong thoughts defile thee, In thy just proof repeals and reconciles thee.
passages.vernacular: 留意高處嘅喧鬧;並喺虛假嘅猜疑(佢嘅錯誤想法玷污你)喺你嘅公正證明中撤銷並同你和解時,顯露你自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意高處的喧鬧;並在虛假的猜疑(它的錯誤想法玷污你)在你的公正證明中撤銷並與你和解時,顯露你自己。

passages.original: What will hap more tonight, safe ’scape the King! Lurk, lurk.
passages.vernacular: 今晚仲會發生乜嘢,但願國王安全逃脫!躲起嚟,躲起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚還會發生什麼,但願國王安全逃脫!躲起來,躲起來。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene VII — A Room in Gloucester’s Castle 第三幕第七場:葛羅斯特城堡一室

passages.original: Enter Cornwall, Regan, Goneril, Edmund and Servants.
passages.vernacular: [康華爾、里根、高納麗、愛德蒙同僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [康華爾、里根、高納麗、愛德蒙和僕人們上。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Post speedily to my lord your husband, show him this letter:
passages.vernacular: 火速趕到你丈夫大人嗰度,把呢封信畀佢睇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火速趕到你丈夫大人那裡,把這封信給他看:

passages.original: the army of France is landed.
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西軍隊已經登陸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西軍隊已經登陸。

passages.original: Seek out the traitor Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: 找出叛徒葛羅斯特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找出叛徒葛羅斯特。

passages.original: [Exeunt some of the Servants.]
passages.vernacular: [啲僕人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一些僕人下。]

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Hang him instantly.
passages.vernacular: 即刻吊死佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻吊死他。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Pluck out his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 挖出佢嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 挖出他的眼睛。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Leave him to my displeasure.
passages.vernacular: 把佢交畀我嘅怒氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他交給我的怒氣。

passages.original: Edmund, keep you our sister company: the revenges we are bound to take upon your traitorous father are not fit for your beholding.
passages.vernacular: 愛德蒙,你陪我哋姊姊:我哋必須對你叛逆嘅父親施加嘅報復,不適合你睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛德蒙,你陪我們姊姊:我們必須對你叛逆的父親施加的報復,不適合你看。

passages.original: Advise the Duke where you are going, to a most festinate preparation:
passages.vernacular: 告訴公爵你要去邊度,要佢極其迅速地準備:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴公爵你要去哪裡,要他極其迅速地準備:

passages.original: we are bound to the like.
passages.vernacular: 我哋都要咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們也要這樣。

passages.original: Our posts shall be swift and intelligent betwixt us.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅驛使將喺我哋之間迅速而機靈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的驛使將在我們之間迅速而機靈。

passages.original: Farewell, dear sister, farewell, my lord of Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: 再見,親愛嘅姊姊,再見,葛羅斯特大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,親愛的姊姊,再見,葛羅斯特大人。

passages.original: Enter Oswald.
passages.vernacular: [奧斯華上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧斯華上。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: How now!
passages.vernacular: 點樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣!

passages.original: Where’s the King?
passages.vernacular: 國王喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王在哪裡?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: My lord of Gloucester hath convey’d him hence:
passages.vernacular: 葛羅斯特大人把佢送走喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛羅斯特大人把他送走了:

passages.original: Some five or six and thirty of his knights, Hot questrists after him, met him at gate;
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅三十五六個騎士,熱心地追尋佢,喺門口遇見咗佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的三十五六個騎士,熱心地追尋他,在門口遇見了他;

passages.original: Who, with some other of the lord’s dependants, Are gone with him toward Dover:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋同大人嘅其他啲家臣,一起跟佢去多佛喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們與大人的其他一些家臣,一起跟他去多佛了:

passages.original: where they boast To have well-armed friends.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋誇口喺嗰度有全副武裝嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們誇口在那裡有全副武裝的朋友。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Get horses for your mistress.
passages.vernacular: 畀你家夫人備馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給你家夫人備馬。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Farewell, sweet lord, and sister.
passages.vernacular: 再見,親愛嘅大人同姊姊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,親愛的大人和姊姊。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Edmund, farewell.
passages.vernacular: 愛德蒙,再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛德蒙,再見。

passages.original: [Exeunt Goneril, Edmund and Oswald.]
passages.vernacular: [高納麗、愛德蒙同奧斯華下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [高納麗、愛德蒙和奧斯華下。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Go seek the traitor Gloucester, Pinion him like a thief, bring him before us.
passages.vernacular: 去找叛徒葛羅斯特,像賊一樣綁住佢,帶到我哋面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去找叛徒葛羅斯特,像賊一樣綁住他,帶到我們面前。

passages.original: [Exeunt other Servants.]
passages.vernacular: [其他僕人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [其他僕人下。]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Though well we may not pass upon his life Without the form of justice, yet our power Shall do a courtesy to our wrath, which men May blame, but not control.
passages.vernacular: 雖然我哋冇正義嘅形式唔能夠判決佢嘅生命,但我哋嘅權力要對我哋嘅憤怒做個通融,人哋可以責備,卻無法制止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我們沒有正義的形式不能判決他的生命,但我們的權力要對我們的憤怒做個通融,人們可以責備,卻無法制止。

passages.original: Who’s there?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在那裡?

passages.original: The traitor?
passages.vernacular: 叛徒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叛徒?

passages.original: Enter Gloucester and Servants.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特同僕人哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特和僕人們上。]

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Ingrateful fox! ’tis he.
passages.vernacular: 忘恩負義嘅狐狸!係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 忘恩負義的狐狸!是他。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Bind fast his corky arms.
passages.vernacular: 綁緊佢像軟木一樣乾枯嘅手臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綁緊他像軟木一樣乾枯的手臂。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: What mean your graces?
passages.vernacular: 殿下哋係乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 殿下們是什麼意思?

passages.original: Good my friends, consider you are my guests.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅好朋友哋,想想你哋係我嘅客人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的好朋友們,想想你們是我的客人。

passages.original: Do me no foul play, friends.
passages.vernacular: 朋友哋,別對我使壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朋友們,別對我使壞。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Bind him, I say.
passages.vernacular: 綁佢,我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綁他,我說。

passages.original: [Servants bind him.]
passages.vernacular: [僕人哋綁佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [僕人們綁他。]

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Hard, hard.
passages.vernacular: 緊,緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 緊,緊。

passages.original: O filthy traitor!
passages.vernacular: 啊,骯髒嘅叛徒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,骯髒的叛徒!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Unmerciful lady as you are, I’m none.
passages.vernacular: 無情嘅夫人,你咁樣,我可唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無情的夫人,你這樣,我可不是。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: To this chair bind him.
passages.vernacular: 把佢綁喺呢把椅子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他綁在這把椅子上。

passages.original: Villain, thou shalt find—
passages.vernacular: 惡棍,你會發現——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡棍,你會發現——

passages.original: [Regan plucks his beard.]
passages.vernacular: [里根揪佢嘅鬍子。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [里根揪他的鬍子。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: By the kind gods, ’tis most ignobly done To pluck me by the beard.
passages.vernacular: 憑仁慈嘅諸神,揪我鬍子,呢做得最不光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑仁慈的諸神,揪我鬍子,這做得最不光彩。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: So white, and such a traitor!
passages.vernacular: 咁白,卻係個叛徒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼白,卻是個叛徒!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Naughty lady, These hairs which thou dost ravish from my chin Will quicken, and accuse thee.
passages.vernacular: 壞夫人,你從我下巴上搶走嘅呢啲鬍子,會活起嚟控告你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 壞夫人,你從我下巴上搶走的這些鬍子,會活起來控告你。

passages.original: I am your host: With robber’s hands my hospitable favours You should not ruffle thus.
passages.vernacular: 我係你嘅主人:你不該用強盜嘅手咁樣揉皺我好客嘅面容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是你的主人:你不該用強盜的手這樣揉皺我好客的面容。

passages.original: What will you do?
passages.vernacular: 你要做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要做什麼?

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Come, sir, what letters had you late from France?
passages.vernacular: 嚟,先生,你最近從法蘭西收到乜嘢信?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,先生,你最近從法蘭西收到什麼信?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Be simple answer’d, for we know the truth.
passages.vernacular: 回答要簡單,因為我哋知道真相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回答要簡單,因為我們知道真相。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: And what confederacy have you with the traitors, Late footed in the kingdom?
passages.vernacular: 你同最近喺王國登陸嘅叛徒哋有乜嘢結盟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你與最近在王國登陸的叛徒們有什麼結盟?

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: To whose hands have you sent the lunatic King? Speak.
passages.vernacular: 你把瘋國王送到邊個嘅手裡?講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把瘋國王送到誰的手裡?說。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I have a letter guessingly set down, Which came from one that’s of a neutral heart, And not from one oppos’d.
passages.vernacular: 我有一封猜測性寫成嘅信,來自一位心懷中立嘅人,而唔係對立者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一封猜測性寫成的信,來自一位心懷中立的人,而不是對立者。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Cunning.
passages.vernacular: 狡猾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狡猾。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: And false.
passages.vernacular: 虛假。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虛假。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Where hast thou sent the King?
passages.vernacular: 你把國王送到邊喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把國王送到哪了?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: To Dover.
passages.vernacular: 多佛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多佛。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Wherefore to Dover?
passages.vernacular: 點解去多佛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼去多佛?

passages.original: Wast thou not charg’d at peril,—
passages.vernacular: 你冇被警告,冒住危險——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒有被警告,冒著危險——

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Wherefore to Dover?
passages.vernacular: 點解去多佛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼去多佛?

passages.original: Let him first answer that.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢先回答嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他先回答那個。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I am tied to the stake, and I must stand the course.
passages.vernacular: 我被綁喺柱子上,必須受呢場撲咬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被綁在柱子上,必須受這場撲咬。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Wherefore to Dover, sir?
passages.vernacular: 點解去多佛,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼去多佛,先生?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Because I would not see thy cruel nails Pluck out his poor old eyes;
passages.vernacular: 因為我唔願睇到你殘忍嘅指甲挖出佢可憐嘅老眼睛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我不願看到你殘忍的指甲挖出他可憐的老眼睛;

passages.original: nor thy fierce sister In his anointed flesh stick boarish fangs.
passages.vernacular: 都唔願睇到你兇猛嘅姊姊把野豬獠牙插進佢受膏嘅肉體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不願看到你兇猛的姊姊把野豬獠牙插進他受膏的肉體。

passages.original: The sea, with such a storm as his bare head In hell-black night endur’d, would have buoy’d up, And quench’d the stelled fires;
passages.vernacular: 大海,承受住佢赤裸嘅頭喺地獄般黑夜裡所忍受嘅嗰樣嘅風暴,本會浮起,並熄滅星星之火;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大海,承受著他赤裸的頭在地獄般黑夜裡所忍受的那樣的風暴,本會浮起,並熄滅星星之火;

passages.original: Yet, poor old heart, he holp the heavens to rain.
passages.vernacular: 然而,可憐嘅老心,佢仲幫住天下雨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,可憐的老心,他還幫著天下雨。

passages.original: If wolves had at thy gate howl’d that stern time, Thou shouldst have said, ‘Good porter, turn the key.’
passages.vernacular: 如果喺嗰嚴酷嘅時刻有狼喺你門口嚎叫,你本該講「好睇門人,開鎖」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果在那嚴酷的時刻有狼在你門口嚎叫,你本該說「好看門人,開鎖」。

passages.original: All cruels else subscrib’d: but I shall see The winged vengeance overtake such children.
passages.vernacular: 其他一切殘酷都簽咗名:但我將睇到有翼嘅復仇追上咁樣嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他一切殘酷都簽了名:但我將看到有翼的復仇追上這樣的孩子。

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: See’t shalt thou never.
passages.vernacular: 你永遠睇唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你永遠看不到。

passages.original: Fellows, hold the chair.
passages.vernacular: 夥計哋,扶住椅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夥計們,扶住椅子。

passages.original: Upon these eyes of thine I’ll set my foot.
passages.vernacular: 我要把腳踩喺你呢雙眼睛上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把腳踩在你這雙眼睛上。

passages.original: [Gloucester is held down in his chair, while Cornwall plucks out one of his eyes and sets his foot on it.]
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特被按喺椅子上,康華爾挖出佢一隻眼睛並把腳踩喺上面。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特被按在椅子上,康華爾挖出他一隻眼睛並把腳踩在上面。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: He that will think to live till he be old, Give me some help!—O cruel! O you gods!
passages.vernacular: 想要活到老嘅人,幫幫我!——啊殘忍!啊諸神!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想要活到老的人,幫幫我!——啊殘忍!啊諸神!

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: One side will mock another; the other too!
passages.vernacular: 一邊嘲笑另一邊;另一邊都一樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一邊嘲笑另一邊;另一邊也一樣!

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: If you see vengeance—
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋睇到復仇——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們看到復仇——

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: Hold your hand, my lord: I have serv’d you ever since I was a child;
passages.vernacular: 住手,大人:我從小就侍奉您;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住手,大人:我從小就侍奉您;

passages.original: But better service have I never done you Than now to bid you hold.
passages.vernacular: 但我從未比而家叫您住手做更好嘅服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我從未比現在叫您住手做更好的服務。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: How now, you dog!
passages.vernacular: 點喇,你呢條狗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,你這條狗!

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: If you did wear a beard upon your chin, I’d shake it on this quarrel.
passages.vernacular: 如果你下巴上有鬍子,我會為呢場爭吵揪佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你下巴上有鬍子,我會為這場爭吵揪它。

passages.original: What do you mean?
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼意思?

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: My villain?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅惡棍?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的惡棍?

passages.original: [Draws, and runs at him.]
passages.vernacular: [拔劍,衝向佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拔劍,衝向他。]

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: Nay, then, come on, and take the chance of anger.
passages.vernacular: 不,咁,嚟吧,碰碰憤怒嘅運氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,那麼,來吧,碰碰憤怒的運氣。

passages.original: [Draws. They fight. Cornwall is wounded.]
passages.vernacular: [拔劍。二人搏鬥。康華爾受傷。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [拔劍。二人搏鬥。康華爾受傷。]

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: [To another servant.]
passages.vernacular: [對另一個僕人。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對另一個僕人。]

passages.original: Give me thy sword.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅劍畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的劍給我。

passages.original: A peasant stand up thus?
passages.vernacular: 一個農奴竟咁樣站起嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個農奴竟這樣站起來?

passages.original: [Snatches a sword, comes behind, and stabs him.]
passages.vernacular: [奪過一把劍,從後面刺佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奪過一把劍,從後面刺他。]

passages.title: First Servant 第一僕人
passages.original: O, I am slain!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我被殺喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我被殺了!

passages.original: My lord, you have one eye left To see some mischief on him. O!
passages.vernacular: 大人,您仲有一隻眼睛,可以睇到佢遭些惡報。啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,您還有一隻眼睛,可以看到他遭些惡報。啊!

passages.original: [Dies.]

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: Lest it see more, prevent it.
passages.vernacular: 免得佢睇到更多,阻止佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 免得它看到更多,阻止它。

passages.original: Out, vile jelly!
passages.vernacular: 滾出嚟,卑賤嘅膠凍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾出來,卑賤的膠凍!

passages.original: Where is thy lustre now?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅光澤而家喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的光澤現在在哪裡?

passages.original: [Tears out Gloucester’s other eye and throws it on the ground.]
passages.vernacular: [撕出葛羅斯特嘅另一隻眼睛,扔喺地上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [撕出葛羅斯特的另一隻眼睛,扔在地上。]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: All dark and comfortless.
passages.vernacular: 一片黑暗,冇安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一片黑暗,沒有安慰。

passages.original: Where’s my son Edmund?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅兒子愛德蒙喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的兒子愛德蒙在哪裡?

passages.original: Edmund, enkindle all the sparks of nature To quit this horrid act.
passages.vernacular: 愛德蒙,點燃天性所有嘅火花,為呢可怕嘅行為報仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛德蒙,點燃天性所有的火花,為這可怕的行為報仇。

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Out, treacherous villain!
passages.vernacular: 滾開,奸詐嘅惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾開,奸詐的惡棍!

passages.original: Thou call’st on him that hates thee: it was he That made the overture of thy treasons to us;
passages.vernacular: 你呼喚嘅係恨你嘅人:正是佢向我哋提出你嘅叛逆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你呼喚的是恨你的人:正是他向我們提出你的叛逆;

passages.original: Who is too good to pity thee.
passages.vernacular: 佢太善良,不屑可憐你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他太善良,不屑可憐你。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: O my follies!
passages.vernacular: 啊我嘅愚蠢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我的愚蠢!

passages.original: Then Edgar was abus’d.
passages.vernacular: 咁愛德伽被冤枉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼愛德伽被冤枉了。

passages.original: Kind gods, forgive me that, and prosper him!
passages.vernacular: 仁慈嘅諸神,原諒我呢個,並讓佢興旺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仁慈的諸神,原諒我這個,並讓他興旺!

passages.title: Regan 里根
passages.original: Go thrust him out at gates, and let him smell His way to Dover.
passages.vernacular: 把佢推出大門,讓佢嗅住路去多佛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他推出大門,讓他嗅著路去多佛。

passages.original: How is’t, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人怎樣?

passages.original: How look you?
passages.vernacular: 您睇起嚟點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看起來怎樣?

passages.title: Cornwall 康華爾
passages.original: I have receiv’d a hurt: follow me, lady.
passages.vernacular: 我受咗傷:跟我嚟,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受了傷:跟我來,夫人。

passages.original: Turn out that eyeless villain.
passages.vernacular: 把嗰個無眼嘅惡棍趕出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把那個無眼的惡棍趕出去。

passages.original: Throw this slave Upon the dunghill.
passages.vernacular: 把呢個奴才扔到糞堆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把這個奴才扔到糞堆上。

passages.original: Regan, I bleed apace: Untimely comes this hurt: give me your arm.
passages.vernacular: 里根,我流血好快:呢傷嚟得唔係時候:畀我你嘅手臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 里根,我流血很快:這傷來得不是時候:給我你的手臂。

passages.original: [Exit Cornwall, led by Regan; Servants unbind Gloucester and lead him out.]
passages.vernacular: [康華爾由里根攙扶下;僕人哋解開葛羅斯特,領佢出去。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [康華爾由里根攙扶下;僕人們解開葛羅斯特,領他出去。]

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: I’ll never care what wickedness I do, If this man come to good.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢個人得好報,我再都不在乎我做乜嘢惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這個人得好報,我再也不在乎我做什麼惡。

passages.title: Third Servant 第三僕人
passages.original: If she live long, And in the end meet the old course of death, Women will all turn monsters.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢活得長,最後遇到老年自然嘅死,女人都要變成怪物喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她活得長,最後遇到老年自然的死,女人都要變成怪物了。

passages.title: Second Servant 第二僕人
passages.original: Let’s follow the old Earl, and get the bedlam To lead him where he would:
passages.vernacular: 我哋跟住老伯爵,找嗰個瘋乞丐帶佢去佢想去嘅地方:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們跟著老伯爵,找那個瘋乞丐帶他去他想去的地方:

passages.original: his roguish madness Allows itself to anything.
passages.vernacular: 佢無賴嘅瘋狂允許自己做任何事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他無賴的瘋狂允許自己做任何事。

passages.title: Third Servant 第三僕人
passages.original: Go thou: I’ll fetch some flax and whites of eggs To apply to his bleeding face.
passages.vernacular: 你去:我去攞些亞麻同蛋白,敷喺佢流血嘅臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去:我去拿些亞麻和蛋白,敷在他流血的臉上。

passages.original: Now heaven help him!
passages.vernacular: 而家願上天幫助佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在願上天幫助他!

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene I — The Heath 第四幕第一場:荒野

passages.original: Enter Edgar.
passages.vernacular: [愛德伽上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德伽上。]

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Yet better thus, and known to be contemn’d, Than still contemn’d and flatter’d.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣更好,知道自己被鄙視,勝過一直被鄙視卻被奉承。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣更好,知道自己被鄙視,勝過一直被鄙視卻被奉承。

passages.original: To be worst, The lowest and most dejected thing of fortune, Stands still in esperance, lives not in fear:
passages.vernacular: 處於最壞,命運中最低最沮喪嘅嘢,始終仲有希望,不活喺恐懼中:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 處於最壞,命運中最低最沮喪的東西,始終還有希望,不活在恐懼中:

passages.original: The lamentable change is from the best; The worst returns to laughter.
passages.vernacular: 可悲嘅變化來自最好;最壞嘅反而回到歡笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可悲的變化來自最好;最壞的反而回到歡笑。

passages.original: Welcome then, Thou unsubstantial air that I embrace;
passages.vernacular: 咁歡迎,你呢我所擁抱嘅無實體空氣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼歡迎,你這我所擁抱的無實體空氣;

passages.original: The wretch that thou hast blown unto the worst Owes nothing to thy blasts.
passages.vernacular: 被你吹到最壞嘅可憐人,不欠你嘅風任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被你吹到最壞的可憐人,不欠你的風任何東西。

passages.original: Enter Gloucester, led by an Old Man.
passages.vernacular: [葛羅斯特由一位老人領住上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛羅斯特由一位老人領著上。]

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: But who comes here?
passages.vernacular: 但呢度嚟嘅係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這裡來的是誰?

passages.original: My father, poorly led?
passages.vernacular: 我父親,被人咁樣可憐地領住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親,被人這樣可憐地領著?

passages.original: World, world, O world!
passages.vernacular: 世界,世界,啊世界!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 世界,世界,啊世界!

passages.original: But that thy strange mutations make us hate thee, Life would not yield to age.
passages.vernacular: 若唔係你奇異嘅變化使我哋憎恨你,生命唔會向衰老屈服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 若不是你奇異的變化使我們憎恨你,生命不會向衰老屈服。

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: O my good lord, I have been your tenant, and your father’s tenant these fourscore years.
passages.vernacular: 啊我嘅好大人,我同您嘅父親,我係你哋嘅佃戶,八十年喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我的好大人,我和您的父親,我是你們的佃戶,八十年了。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Away, get thee away; good friend, be gone.
passages.vernacular: 走開,走開;好朋友,走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,走開;好朋友,走吧。

passages.original: Thy comforts can do me no good at all; Thee they may hurt.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅安慰對我毫無益處;對你可能有害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的安慰對我毫無益處;對你可能有害。

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: You cannot see your way.
passages.vernacular: 您睇唔見路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看不見路。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: I have no way, and therefore want no eyes; I stumbled when I saw.
passages.vernacular: 我冇路,所以不需要眼睛;我睇得見時反而跌倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有路,所以不需要眼睛;我看得見時反而跌倒。

passages.original: Full oft ’tis seen Our means secure us, and our mere defects Prove our commodities.
passages.vernacular: 好多時候可見,我哋嘅資源使我哋大意,我哋嘅缺陷反成我哋嘅好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很多時候可見,我們的資源使我們大意,我們的缺陷反成我們的好處。

passages.original: O dear son Edgar, The food of thy abused father’s wrath!
passages.vernacular: 啊親愛嘅兒子愛德伽,你被冤枉嘅父親怒火嘅食物!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊親愛的兒子愛德伽,你被冤枉的父親怒火的食物!

passages.original: Might I but live to see thee in my touch, I’d say I had eyes again!
passages.vernacular: 只要我能活住用觸摸見到你,我就講我又有眼睛喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我能活著用觸摸見到你,我就說我又有眼睛了!

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: How now!
passages.vernacular: 點喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了!

passages.original: Who’s there?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在那裡?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: [Aside.] O gods!
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]啊諸神!
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]啊諸神!

passages.original: Who is’t can say ‘I am at the worst’?
passages.vernacular: 邊個能講「我已到最壞」?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰能說「我已到最壞」?

passages.original: I am worse than e’er I was.
passages.vernacular: 我比以往任何時候都更壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我比以往任何時候都更壞。

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: ’Tis poor mad Tom.
passages.vernacular: 係可憐嘅瘋湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是可憐的瘋湯姆。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: And worse I may be yet.
passages.vernacular: 我可能仲會更壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可能還會更壞。

passages.original: The worst is not So long as we can say ‘This is the worst.’
passages.vernacular: 只要我哋仲能講「呢個係最壞」,就仲唔係最壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我們還能說「這是最壞」,就還不是最壞。

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: Fellow, where goest?
passages.vernacular: 朋友,你去邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朋友,你去哪?

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Is it a beggar-man?
passages.vernacular: 係個乞丐嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是個乞丐嗎?

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: Madman, and beggar too.
passages.vernacular: 瘋子,都係乞丐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瘋子,也是乞丐。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: He has some reason, else he could not beg.
passages.vernacular: 佢有些理智,否則唔能夠乞討。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有些理智,否則不能乞討。

passages.original: I’ the last night’s storm I such a fellow saw;
passages.vernacular: 喺昨夜嘅風暴中我見過咁樣一個人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在昨夜的風暴中我見過這樣一個人;

passages.original: Which made me think a man a worm.
passages.vernacular: 令我覺得人係一條蟲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令我覺得人是一條蟲。

passages.original: My son Came then into my mind, and yet my mind Was then scarce friends with him.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時我兒子進入我嘅腦海,而我嘅心嗰時幾乎不同佢友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時我兒子進入我的腦海,而我的心那時幾乎不和他友好。

passages.original: I have heard more since.
passages.vernacular: 後來我聽到更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來我聽到更多。

passages.original: As flies to wanton boys are we to the gods, They kill us for their sport.
passages.vernacular: 我哋對諸神,像蒼蠅對頑童:佢哋為了消遣殺死我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們對諸神,像蒼蠅對頑童:他們為了消遣殺死我們。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: How should this be?
passages.vernacular: 呢點可能?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這怎麼可能?

passages.original: Bad is the trade that must play fool to sorrow, Angering itself and others.
passages.vernacular: 要為悲傷扮演弄臣嘅行當不好,既激怒自己又激怒別人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要為悲傷扮演弄臣的行當不好,既激怒自己又激怒別人。

passages.original: Bless thee, master!
passages.vernacular: 保佑你,主人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你,主人!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Is that the naked fellow?
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係嗰個赤身嘅人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是那個赤身的人嗎?

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: Ay, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 係,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,大人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Then prythee get thee away.
passages.vernacular: 咁請你走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼請你走開。

passages.original: If for my sake Thou wilt o’ertake us hence a mile or twain, I’ the way toward Dover, do it for ancient love, And bring some covering for this naked soul, Which I’ll entreat to lead me.
passages.vernacular: 如果為了我,你肯喺前面一兩里路趕上我哋,喺去多佛嘅路上,出於舊日嘅情誼,帶些衣物畀呢赤身嘅靈魂,我要請求佢畀我領路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果為了我,你肯在前面一兩里路趕上我們,在去多佛的路上,出於舊日的情誼,帶些衣物給這赤身的靈魂,我要請求他給我領路。

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: Alack, sir, he is mad.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,先生,佢係瘋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,先生,他是瘋子。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: ’Tis the time’s plague when madmen lead the blind.
passages.vernacular: 瘋子領盲人,係時代嘅瘟疫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瘋子領盲人,是時代的瘟疫。

passages.original: Do as I bid thee, or rather do thy pleasure; Above the rest, be gone.
passages.vernacular: 照我吩咐嘅做,或者講隨你嘅意;總之,走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照我吩咐的做,或者說隨你的意;總之,走吧。

passages.title: Old Man 老人
passages.original: I’ll bring him the best ’parel that I have, Come on’t what will.
passages.vernacular: 我把我最好嘅衣服帶畀佢,無論點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把我最好的衣服帶給他,無論怎樣。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Sirrah naked fellow.
passages.vernacular: 小子,赤身嘅傢伙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,赤身的傢伙。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Poor Tom’s a-cold. [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅湯姆冷。[旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的湯姆冷。[旁白。]

passages.original: I cannot daub it further.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠再裝下去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能再裝下去了。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Come hither, fellow.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,朋友。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: And yet I must.
passages.vernacular: 然而我必須。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而我必須。

passages.original: Bless thy sweet eyes, they bleed.
passages.vernacular: 保佑你美麗嘅眼睛,佢哋喺流血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你美麗的眼睛,它們在流血。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Know’st thou the way to Dover?
passages.vernacular: 你知道去多佛嘅路嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道去多佛的路嗎?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Both stile and gate, horseway and footpath.
passages.vernacular: 梯子同大門,馬路同人行小徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 梯子和大門,馬路和人行小徑。

passages.original: Poor Tom hath been scared out of his good wits.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅湯姆被嚇得失去咗佢嘅好神智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的湯姆被嚇得失去了他的好神智。

passages.original: Bless thee, good man’s son, from the foul fiend!
passages.vernacular: 保佑你,好人嘅兒子,免於邪惡嘅魔鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你,好人的兒子,免於邪惡的魔鬼!

passages.original: Five fiends have been in poor Tom at once; of lust, as Obidicut;
passages.vernacular: 五個魔鬼同時附喺可憐嘅湯姆身上;淫慾魔奧比迪卡特;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 五個魔鬼同時附在可憐的湯姆身上;淫慾魔奧比迪卡特;

passages.original: Hobbididence, prince of darkness; Mahu, of stealing;
passages.vernacular: 霍比迪登斯,黑暗王子;馬胡,偷竊魔;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 霍比迪登斯,黑暗王子;馬胡,偷竊魔;

passages.original: Modo, of murder; Flibbertigibbet, of mopping and mowing, who since possesses chambermaids and waiting women.
passages.vernacular: 莫多,殺人魔;弗利貝提吉比特,扮鬼臉魔,此後附身於侍女同女傭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莫多,殺人魔;弗利貝提吉比特,扮鬼臉魔,此後附身於侍女和女傭。

passages.original: So, bless thee, master!
passages.vernacular: 所以,保佑你,主人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,保佑你,主人!

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: Here, take this purse, thou whom the heaven’s plagues Have humbled to all strokes:
passages.vernacular: 嚟,攞呢錢袋,你呢個被天上災禍打壓到承受一切打擊嘅人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,拿這錢袋,你這個被天上災禍打壓到承受一切打擊的人:

passages.original: that I am wretched Makes thee the happier.
passages.vernacular: 我悲慘,使你更幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我悲慘,使你更幸福。

passages.original: Heavens deal so still!
passages.vernacular: 願諸天始終咁樣處置!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願諸天始終這樣處置!

passages.original: Let the superfluous and lust-dieted man, That slaves your ordinance, that will not see Because he does not feel, feel your power quickly;
passages.vernacular: 讓嗰奢侈無度、縱慾嘅人,佢奴役你哋嘅法令,因為不感受所以不睇,快快感受你哋嘅力量;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓那奢侈無度、縱慾的人,他奴役你們的法令,因為不感受所以不看,快快感受你們的力量;

passages.original: So distribution should undo excess, And each man have enough.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣分配就消除過剩,每人都有足夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣分配就消除過剩,每人都有足夠。

passages.original: Dost thou know Dover?
passages.vernacular: 你認識多佛嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認識多佛嗎?

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Ay, master.
passages.vernacular: 認識,主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 認識,主人。

passages.title: Gloucester 葛羅斯特
passages.original: There is a cliff, whose high and bending head Looks fearfully in the confined deep:
passages.vernacular: 嗰度有一處懸崖,佢高聳彎曲嘅頭可怕地俯視深唔見底嘅海:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡有一處懸崖,它高聳彎曲的頭可怕地俯視深不見底的海:

passages.original: Bring me but to the very brim of it, And I’ll repair the misery thou dost bear With something rich about me:
passages.vernacular: 只要把我帶到佢嘅邊緣,我就用身上嘅啲貴重物品補償你所承受嘅苦難:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要把我帶到它的邊緣,我就用身上的一些貴重物品補償你所承受的苦難:

passages.original: from that place I shall no leading need.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰地方起我不需人領路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那地方起我不需人領路。

passages.title: Edgar 愛德伽
passages.original: Give me thy arm: Poor Tom shall lead thee.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅手臂畀我:可憐嘅湯姆領你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的手臂給我:可憐的湯姆領你。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene II — Before Albany’s Palace 第四幕第二場:奧本尼宮殿前

passages.original: Enter Goneril, Edmund; Oswald meeting them.
passages.vernacular: [高納麗、愛德蒙上;奧斯華迎面而嚟。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [高納麗、愛德蒙上;奧斯華迎面而來。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Welcome, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,大人。

passages.original: I marvel our mild husband Not met us on the way.
passages.vernacular: 我奇怪我哋溫順嘅丈夫冇喺路上迎接我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我奇怪我們溫順的丈夫沒有在路上迎接我們。

passages.original: Now, where’s your master?
passages.vernacular: 而家,你嘅主人喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,你的主人在哪?

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Madam, within; but never man so chang’d.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,喺裡面;但從冇人變得咁多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,在裡面;但從沒有人變得這麼多。

passages.original: I told him of the army that was landed; He smil’d at it:
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢有軍隊登陸;佢對此微笑:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他有軍隊登陸;他對此微笑:

passages.original: I told him you were coming; His answer was, ‘The worse.’
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢您嚟喇;佢嘅回答係「更糟」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他您來了;他的回答是「更糟」。

passages.original: Of Gloucester’s treachery And of the loyal service of his son When I inform’d him, then he call’d me sot, And told me I had turn’d the wrong side out.
passages.vernacular: 當我向佢報告葛羅斯特嘅背叛同佢兒子嘅忠誠服務,佢就叫我傻瓜,講我把事情講反喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我向他報告葛羅斯特的背叛和他兒子的忠誠服務,他就叫我傻瓜,說我把事情說反了。

passages.original: What most he should dislike seems pleasant to him; What like, offensive.
passages.vernacular: 佢最該厭惡嘅似乎使佢高興;佢該鍾意嘅,反而冒犯佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他最該厭惡的似乎使他高興;他該喜歡的,反而冒犯他。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: [To Edmund.]
passages.vernacular: [對愛德蒙。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對愛德蒙。]

passages.original: Then shall you go no further.
passages.vernacular: 嗰你就唔使再往前走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你就不用再往前走了。

passages.original: It is the cowish terror of his spirit, That dares not undertake.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係佢精神嘅膽怯恐懼,唔敢承擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是他精神的膽怯恐懼,不敢承擔。

passages.original: He’ll not feel wrongs Which tie him to an answer.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會感到嗰啲使佢必須回答嘅冤屈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不會感到那些使他必須回答的冤屈。

passages.original: Our wishes on the way May prove effects.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一路上嘅願望可能成為現實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一路上的願望可能成為現實。

passages.original: Back, Edmund, to my brother; Hasten his musters and conduct his powers.
passages.vernacular: 回去,愛德蒙,去我哥哥嗰度;催佢集結,指揮佢嘅軍隊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回去,愛德蒙,去我哥哥那裡;催他集結,指揮他的軍隊。

passages.original: I must change names at home, and give the distaff Into my husband’s hands.
passages.vernacular: 我必須喺家換名字,把紡錘交到我丈夫手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須在家換名字,把紡錘交到我丈夫手裡。

passages.original: This trusty servant Shall pass between us.
passages.vernacular: 呢個可靠嘅僕人將喺我哋之間傳遞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個可靠的僕人將在我們之間傳遞。

passages.original: Ere long you are like to hear, If you dare venture in your own behalf, A mistress’s command.
passages.vernacular: 不久你可能聽到,如果你敢為自己冒險,一位女主人嘅命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久你可能聽到,如果你敢為自己冒險,一位女主人的命令。

passages.original: [Giving a favour.]
passages.vernacular: [畀一件信物。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [給一件信物。]

passages.original: Wear this; spare speech; Decline your head.
passages.vernacular: 戴上呢個;少講話;低下頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戴上這個;少說話;低下頭。

passages.original: This kiss, if it durst speak, Would stretch thy spirits up into the air.
passages.vernacular: 呢個吻,如果佢敢講話,會把你嘅精神提升到空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個吻,如果它敢說話,會把你的精神提升到空中。

passages.original: Conceive, and fare thee well.
passages.vernacular: 明白吧,再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明白吧,再見。

passages.title: Edmund 愛德蒙
passages.original: Yours in the ranks of death.
passages.vernacular: 我屬於您,喺死亡嘅行列中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我屬於您,在死亡的行列中。

passages.original: [Exit Edmund.]
passages.vernacular: [愛德蒙下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛德蒙下。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: My most dear Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: 我最親愛嘅葛羅斯特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最親愛的葛羅斯特。

passages.original: O, the difference of man and man!
passages.vernacular: 啊,人同人嘅差別!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,人與人的差別!

passages.original: To thee a woman’s services are due; My fool usurps my body.
passages.vernacular: 你應得女人嘅服侍;我嘅傻瓜卻霸佔我嘅身體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你應得女人的服侍;我的傻瓜卻霸佔我的身體。

passages.title: Oswald 奧斯華
passages.original: Madam, here comes my lord.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,我嘅大人嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,我的大人來了。

passages.original: [Exit.]
Enter Albany.
passages.vernacular: [奧本尼上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧本尼上。]

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: I have been worth the whistle.
passages.vernacular: 我曾經值得為你吹口哨(召喚)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾經值得為你吹口哨(召喚)。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: O Goneril!
passages.vernacular: 啊高納麗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊高納麗!

passages.original: You are not worth the dust which the rude wind Blows in your face!
passages.vernacular: 你不配粗風吹到你臉上嘅灰塵!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不配粗風吹到你臉上的灰塵!

passages.original: I fear your disposition; That nature which contemns its origin Cannot be bordered certain in itself.
passages.vernacular: 我怕你嘅性情;嗰鄙視自己根源嘅天性,唔能夠被確定地圍喺自身之內。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕你的性情;那鄙視自己根源的天性,不能被確定地圍在自身之內。

passages.original: She that herself will sliver and disbranch From her material sap, perforce must wither And come to deadly use.
passages.vernacular: 一個自己要劈開、砍斷其物質樹液嘅人,必然枯萎,成為致命嘅用途。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個自己要劈開、砍斷其物質樹液的人,必然枯萎,成為致命的用途。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: No more; the text is foolish.
passages.vernacular: 夠喇;呢篇講教真愚蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夠了;這篇說教真愚蠢。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Wisdom and goodness to the vile seem vile; Filths savour but themselves.
passages.vernacular: 智慧同善良喺卑劣者睇來卑劣;污穢只會品嚐自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 智慧與善良在卑劣者看來卑劣;污穢只會品嚐自己。

passages.original: What have you done?
passages.vernacular: 你哋做咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們做了什麼?

passages.original: Tigers, not daughters, what have you perform’d?
passages.vernacular: 老虎,唔係女兒,你哋幹咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老虎,不是女兒,你們幹了什麼?

passages.original: A father, and a gracious aged man, Whose reverence even the head-lugg’d bear would lick, Most barbarous, most degenerate, have you madded.
passages.vernacular: 一位父親,一位慈祥嘅年老之人,連被拴頭嘅熊都會舔佢嘅敬畏,你哋呢最野蠻最墮落嘅,竟把佢逼瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位父親,一位慈祥的年老之人,連被拴頭的熊都會舔他的敬畏,你們這最野蠻最墮落的,竟把他逼瘋了。

passages.original: Could my good brother suffer you to do it?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅好兄弟點能容忍你哋咁樣做?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的好兄弟怎麼能容忍你們這樣做?

passages.original: A man, a prince, by him so benefitted!
passages.vernacular: 一個男人,一位王子,受佢如此大恩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個男人,一位王子,受他如此大恩!

passages.original: If that the heavens do not their visible spirits Send quickly down to tame these vile offences, It will come, Humanity must perforce prey on itself, Like monsters of the deep.
passages.vernacular: 如果諸天不迅速派下佢哋可見嘅精靈,馴服呢啲卑劣嘅罪行,事情就會到來,人類必然像深海怪物一樣互相吞食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果諸天不迅速派下它們可見的精靈,馴服這些卑劣的罪行,事情就會到來,人類必然像深海怪物一樣互相吞食。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Milk-liver’d man!
passages.vernacular: 軟肝臟嘅男人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 軟肝臟的男人!

passages.original: That bear’st a cheek for blows, a head for wrongs;
passages.vernacular: 你只會伸出臉頰挨打,伸出頭顱受辱;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只會伸出臉頰挨打,伸出頭顱受辱;

passages.original: Who hast not in thy brows an eye discerning Thine honour from thy suffering;
passages.vernacular: 你眉毛下冇能分辨榮譽同受苦嘅眼睛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你眉毛下沒有能分辨榮譽與受苦的眼睛;

passages.original: that not know’st Fools do those villains pity who are punish’d Ere they have done their mischief.
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道只有傻瓜才憐憫嗰啲喺作惡之前就被懲罰嘅惡棍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道只有傻瓜才憐憫那些在作惡之前就被懲罰的惡棍。

passages.original: Where’s thy drum?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅鼓喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的鼓在哪裡?

passages.original: France spreads his banners in our noiseless land;
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西喺我哋寂靜嘅土地上展開旗幟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西在我們寂靜的土地上展開旗幟;

passages.original: With plumed helm thy state begins to threat, Whilst thou, a moral fool, sitt’st still, and criest ‘Alack, why does he so?’
passages.vernacular: 戴住羽盔嘅人開始威脅你嘅國家,而你呢個道德嘅傻瓜卻坐住不動,喊「哎呀,佢點解咁樣做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戴著羽盔的人開始威脅你的國家,而你這個道德的傻瓜卻坐著不動,喊「哎呀,他為什麼這樣做?」

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: See thyself, devil!
passages.vernacular: 睇睇你自己,魔鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看你自己,魔鬼!

passages.original: Proper deformity seems not in the fiend So horrid as in woman.
passages.vernacular: 恰當嘅畸形喺魔鬼身上睇來不如喺女人身上咁可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恰當的畸形在魔鬼身上看來不如在女人身上那麼可怕。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: O vain fool!
passages.vernacular: 啊虛妄嘅傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊虛妄的傻瓜!

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Thou changed and self-cover’d thing, for shame!
passages.vernacular: 你呢改變咗、自我掩蓋嘅嘢,真可恥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這改變了、自我掩蓋的東西,真可恥!

passages.original: Be-monster not thy feature!
passages.vernacular: 唔好把你嘅容貌變成怪物!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要把你的容貌變成怪物!

passages.original: Were’t my fitness To let these hands obey my blood, They are apt enough to dislocate and tear Thy flesh and bones.
passages.vernacular: 若我嘅適當性允許呢雙手服從我嘅血氣,佢哋足以扭斷撕裂你嘅肉同骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 若我的適當性允許這雙手服從我的血氣,它們足以扭斷撕裂你的肉和骨。

passages.original: Howe’er thou art a fiend, A woman’s shape doth shield thee.
passages.vernacular: 儘管你係魔鬼,女人嘅外形保護你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管你是魔鬼,女人的外形保護你。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: Marry, your manhood, mew!
passages.vernacular: 哼,你嘅男子氣概,去關籠吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哼,你的男子氣概,去關籠吧!

passages.original: Enter a Messenger.
passages.vernacular: [一位信使上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一位信使上。]

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: What news?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼消息?

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: O, my good lord, the Duke of Cornwall’s dead;
passages.vernacular: 啊,我嘅好大人,康華爾公爵死喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我的好大人,康華爾公爵死了;

passages.original: Slain by his servant, going to put out The other eye of Gloucester.
passages.vernacular: 被佢嘅僕人殺死,當時佢要挖出葛羅斯特嘅另一隻眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被他的僕人殺死,當時他要挖出葛羅斯特的另一隻眼睛。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Gloucester’s eyes!
passages.vernacular: 葛羅斯特嘅眼睛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛羅斯特的眼睛!

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: A servant that he bred, thrill’d with remorse, Oppos’d against the act, bending his sword To his great master;
passages.vernacular: 一個佢養大嘅僕人,被悔恨刺痛,反對呢行為,把劍指向佢嘅大主人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個他養大的僕人,被悔恨刺痛,反對這行為,把劍指向他的大主人;

passages.original: who, thereat enrag’d, Flew on him, and amongst them fell’d him dead;
passages.vernacular: 公爵因此暴怒,撲向佢,眾人把佢殺倒喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵因此暴怒,撲向他,眾人把他殺倒了;

passages.original: But not without that harmful stroke which since Hath pluck’d him after.
passages.vernacular: 但佢都受咗嗰致命嘅一擊,此後把佢拉走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他也受了那致命的一擊,此後把他拉走了。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: This shows you are above, You justicers, that these our nether crimes So speedily can venge!
passages.vernacular: 呢表明你哋喺上面,你哋呢啲審判者,我哋呢啲下界嘅罪行能咁樣迅速地被你哋報復!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這表明你們在上面,你們這些審判者,我們這些下界的罪行能這樣迅速地被你們報復!

passages.original: But, O poor Gloucester!
passages.vernacular: 但啊,可憐嘅葛羅斯特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但啊,可憐的葛羅斯特!

passages.original: Lost he his other eye?
passages.vernacular: 佢另一隻眼睛都失去咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他另一隻眼睛也失去了嗎?

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: Both, both, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 兩隻,兩隻,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩隻,兩隻,大人。

passages.original: This letter, madam, craves a speedy answer; ’Tis from your sister.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,呢封信要求迅速答覆;係您妹妹寄嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,這封信要求迅速答覆;是您妹妹寄來的。

passages.title: Goneril 高納麗
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: One way I like this well; But being widow, and my Gloucester with her, May all the building in my fancy pluck Upon my hateful life.
passages.vernacular: 一方面我好滿意;但佢成咗寡婦,而我嘅葛羅斯特又同佢喺一起,可能把我幻想中建起嘅一切拉倒喺我可恨嘅生活上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一方面我很滿意;但她成了寡婦,而我的葛羅斯特又和她在一起,可能把我幻想中建起的一切拉倒在我可恨的生活上。

passages.original: Another way The news is not so tart.
passages.vernacular: 另一方面呢消息冇咁酸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一方面這消息沒那麼酸。

passages.original: I’ll read, and answer.
passages.vernacular: 我要讀,並答覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要讀,並答覆。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Where was his son when they did take his eyes?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋挖佢眼睛時,佢兒子喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們挖他眼睛時,他兒子在哪裡?

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: Come with my lady hither.
passages.vernacular: 同我夫人一起到呢度嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和我夫人一起到這裡來了。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: He is not here.
passages.vernacular: 佢不喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不在這裡。

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: No, my good lord; I met him back again.
passages.vernacular: 不,我嘅好大人;我喺回程遇見咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我的好大人;我在回程遇見了他。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Knows he the wickedness?
passages.vernacular: 佢知道呢個惡行嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道這個惡行嗎?

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: Ay, my good lord.
passages.vernacular: 知道,我嘅好大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 知道,我的好大人。

passages.original: ’Twas he inform’d against him; And quit the house on purpose, that their punishment Might have the freer course.
passages.vernacular: 係佢告發咗佢;並故意離開嗰屋子,好讓佢哋嘅懲罰更自由地進行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是他告發了他;並故意離開那屋子,好讓他們的懲罰更自由地進行。

passages.title: Albany 奧本尼
passages.original: Gloucester, I live To thank thee for the love thou show’dst the King, And to revenge thine eyes.
passages.vernacular: 葛羅斯特,我活住就係為了感謝你對國王所表現嘅愛,並為你嘅眼睛報仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛羅斯特,我活著就是為了感謝你對國王所表現的愛,並為你的眼睛報仇。

passages.original: Come hither, friend, Tell me what more thou know’st.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,朋友,告訴我你仲知道乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,朋友,告訴我你還知道什麼。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene III — The French Camp near Dover 第四幕第三場:多佛附近的法軍營地

passages.original: Enter Kent and a Gentleman.
passages.vernacular: [肯特同一位紳士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [肯特和一位紳士上。]

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Why the King of France is so suddenly gone back, know you no reason?
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西國王為何如此突然回國,你知道原因嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西國王為何如此突然回國,你知道原因嗎?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: Something he left imperfect in the state, which since his coming forth is thought of, which imports to the kingdom so much fear and danger that his personal return was most required and necessary.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺國家事務中留下咗啲未了結嘅事,自佢出嚟後才想起,關係到王國如此大嘅恐懼同危險,佢親自返回係最需要、最必要嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在國家事務中留下了一些未了結的事,自他出來後才想起,關係到王國如此大的恐懼和危險,他親自返回是最需要、最必要的。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Who hath he left behind him general?
passages.vernacular: 佢留下邊個做總指揮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他留下誰做總指揮?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: The Mareschal of France, Monsieur La Far.
passages.vernacular: 法蘭西元帥,拉·法爾先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法蘭西元帥,拉·法爾先生。

passages.title: Kent 肯特
passages.original: Did your letters pierce the queen to any demonstration of grief?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅信有冇刺中王后,使佢表現出悲痛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的信有沒有刺中王后,使她表現出悲痛?

passages.title: Gentleman 紳士
passages.original: Ay, sir; she took them, read them in my presence;
passages.vernacular: 有,先生;佢接過,喺我面前讀;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,先生;她接過,在我面前讀;
